Trigger.name: Keep marker
Trigger.script: if inv.annotMode == "iweight" then inv.iwKeep() elseif inv.scan then inv.iKeep() end

Trigger.name: Scan line
Trigger.script: local L = matches[1] if inv.annotMode == "iweight" then inv.iwLine(L) elseif inv.annotMode == "sack" then inv.sackLine(L) elseif inv.scan and inv.scan.kind == "i" then inv.iLine(L) elseif inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.active and inv.roomScan.atItems then inv.roomLine(L) end if inv.showId and inv.showId.active then inv.showIdLine(matches[1]) end if inv.minv and inv.minv.active then inv.minvLine(matches[1]) end

Trigger.name: Carry line
Trigger.script: inv.noteCarry(matches[1]) if not inv.annotMode then inv.iStart() end

Trigger.name: Action get
Trigger.script: local line = matches[1] local body = line:match("^You get (.+)%.$") local toSack = line:match(" to a (.+)%.$") local fromSack = line:match(" from a (.+)%.$") if body then body = body:gsub(" to a .+$",""):gsub(" from a .+$","") inv.onGetEcho(body, toSack, fromSack) end

regexCodeList.string: give you (\d+) silver coins for the (.+?)\.$

Trigger.name: Sold
Trigger.script: local fromSack = matches[1]:match(' from "([^"]+)"') inv.onSold(matches[2], matches[3], fromSack)

Trigger.name: Too heavy
Trigger.script: local body = matches[1]:match("^The (.+) are too heavy%.$") or matches[1]:match("^(.+) is too heavy%.$") if body then inv.onTooHeavy(body) end

Trigger.name: No room
Trigger.script: local body = matches[1]:match("^There is no room for (.+)%.$") or matches[1]:match("^There was no room for (.+)%.$") if body then inv.onNoRoom(body) end

Trigger.name: Non item
Trigger.script: local fixture = matches[1]:match("cannot move the (.+)%.$") if fixture then inv.onNonItem(fixture) end local badh = matches[1]:match("no \'(.+)\' around") if badh then inv.onNoSuchHandle(badh) end

regexCodeList.string: ^You cannot sacrifice items from your keeplist\.$
^You do not seem to have any (.+)\.$
^(.+?) (?:says:.*?you sold items for a total worth of|gives you money worth of) (\d+) silver

Alias.name: iinv
Alias.script: local f=matches[2]; if f=="" then f=nil end; inv.report(f)

Alias.name: iannot
Alias.script:
local a=matches[2] or "" local col=a:match("^col%s+(%d+)$") if col then inv.config.annotCol=tonumber(col); inv.save(); cecho("
<green>[inv]<reset> column "..col.."
") elseif a=="on" then inv.config.annotate=true; inv.save(); cecho("
<green>[inv]<reset> annotations ON
") elseif a=="off" then inv.config.annotate=false; inv.save(); cecho("
<yellow>[inv]<reset> annotations OFF
") else cecho("
<cyan>[inv]<reset> annotations "..(inv.config.annotate and "ON" or "OFF").."
") end

Alias.name: itrack
Alias.script:
local a=matches[2] or ""
if a=="on" then inv.config.tracking=true; inv.save(); cecho("
<green>[inv]<reset> tracking ON
")
elseif a=="off" then inv.config.tracking=false; inv.save(); cecho("
<yellow>[inv]<reset> tracking OFF
")
elseif a=="save" then inv.save(); cecho("
<green>[inv]<reset> saved
")
else cecho(string.format("
<cyan>[inv]<reset> tracking %s | verbose %s
",
  inv.config.tracking and "ON" or "OFF", inv.config.verbose and "ON" or "OFF")) end

Script.name: IcesusInventory
Script.script:
-- ============================================================ -- Icesus Inventory Tracker v2 (instance-aware) -- ============================================================ -- Tracks item TYPES (full name, adjectives significant) and their learned -- stats, plus WHERE instances currently sit (loose / each named sack / keep) -- and the per-container stow order used for positional references. -- -- Key facts about Icesus this models: -- * Listings (i, look in sack, i weight) are ALPHABETICAL -> good for -- membership/counts, useless for stow-order indexes. -- * Positional index (skin 1, skin 2) is by STOW ORDER, newest = 1, and is -- PER-CONTAINER. So indexes come only from watching get/put/drop/sell/sac -- events live; scans validate counts and flag disagreements. -- * sell/sacrifice can target inside a named sack: `sac skin from "looties"`. -- `value` only reaches loose (carried) items. -- * Weight & volume come from `i weight` (loose inventory only); stacked -- lines show the stack TOTAL, divide by qty for per-item. -- ============================================================
inv = inv or {} inv.config = inv.config or {} local C = inv.config if C.tracking == nil then C.tracking = true end if C.verbose == nil then C.verbose = true end if C.annotate == nil then C.annotate = true end if C.annotCol == nil then C.annotCol = 50 end if C.favourPerSilver == nil then C.favourPerSilver = 1.0 end -- Names of the disposal sacks (lowercased handles). Items in these are the -- ones the advisor targets for sell/sacrifice. C.disposalSacks = C.disposalSacks or { ["loot"]=true, ["treasure"]=true } -- Auto-loot tuning: -- cutoffSL : keep threshold in silver-equivalent per litre (value/volume) -- dfToSilver : how many silver one divine favour is worth (value metric) -- trashDiv : an item <= cutoff/trashDiv is trash (never bother again) -- bagOrder : the disposal bags to fill, in order -- estN : value samples needed to call an average "established" -- cutoffSL: raw silver coins run about 500 silver per litre, so this is -- "an item must be worth at least twice the coin it displaces to be worth -- carrying". The old 100 meant a fifth of coin density, which is why the pack -- filled with junk. -- dfToSilver: not a published constant — see inv.dfCalibrate(), which measures -- it from our own sell/sac pairs. The seed says favour is the scarce resource: -- blessings cost 200 / 3,200 / 16,200 DF and drain 4-10 DF per tick forever, -- while silver mostly sits in the bank. if C.cutoffSL == nil then C.cutoffSL = 1000 end if C.dfToSilver == nil then C.dfToSilver = 100 end -- trashDiv tracks cutoffSL, so raising the cutoff raises the permanent-trash -- line with it. `trash` is a one-way door, so it is deliberately kept well -- below the keep line: 10 puts it at 100 s/l, a fifth of coin density. if C.trashDiv == nil then C.trashDiv = 10 end -- Judge coins by the same silver-per-litre line as everything else. Turned off -- automatically and permanently if the game refuses `get all <denom> coins`, -- because without that form the choice is all-or-nothing (see onNoSuchHandle). if C.coinCutoff == nil then C.coinCutoff = true end if C.estN == nil then C.estN = 3 end C.bagOrder = C.bagOrder or { "loot", "treasure" } -- The bag that holds the kept mithril (and group-mode high-DF items). if C.treasureBag == nil then C.treasureBag = "treasure" end if C.bankKeepMithril == nil then C.bankKeepMithril = 500 end -- Group play: high-DF (glowing) items routed to treasure for fair favour -- division; everything else sold and silver shared via bank deposit. if C.groupMode == nil then C.groupMode = false end -- Sell categories that should never be appraised at a shop — route directly -- to isac (or trash if below cutoff). "food" items (hearts, meat, etc.) have -- no shop value and are only useful for sacrifice. C.sacOnlyCats = C.sacOnlyCats or { food = true }
-- Bulk disposal (9.10). Two optimisations over the one-command-per-item paths, -- each safe only in a specific condition, with the per-item path as fallback: -- * bulkSell: once every item in a sale bag is decided, empty the bag with a -- single `sell all from "<bag>"`. Safe because each sold line still names -- and prices the item, so price/vendor learning is unharmed; the sac-routed -- items are moved out to the stage bag first so the vendor cannot buy them. -- * bulkSac: empty the stage bag with one `sacrifice all from "<bag>"`. Only -- fired when EVERY altar-bound item in it is established (favour n >= estN), -- because `sacrifice all` returns one lump favour that cannot be attributed -- to an item — so a single unlearned item would lose its reading. Until the -- whole bag is established the proven per-item learning path runs instead. if C.bulkSell == nil then C.bulkSell = true end if C.bulkSac == nil then C.bulkSac = true end -- Where sac-routed items are staged so a bulk sacrifice can target only them. C.sacStageBag = C.sacStageBag or (C.treasureBag or "treasure")
-- Favour-first disposal (9.14). When on, disposeRoute never sells an item whose -- divine favour is still unmeasured — it sacrifices one to learn the favour -- first, then the better of sell/sac wins. sellBlindMaxSilver is the escape -- hatch: a sale price at or below it sells immediately without the learning -- sacrifice (0 = never, i.e. always learn favour first). Set favourFirst=false -- for the pre-9.14 "any sale value -> sell" behaviour. if C.favourFirst == nil then C.favourFirst = true end if C.sellBlindMaxSilver == nil then C.sellBlindMaxSilver = 0 end
-- Set of disposal sacks verified this session via look-in scan. -- Stored separately from contMeta so it isn't accidentally cleared. inv.scannedSacks = inv.scannedSacks or {} -- per-type "too heavy to carry" memory so we don't retry -- ---- Carrying capacity ------------------------------------------------ -- "You are carrying 157.3kg (56%) of 277.5kg and 100.0l (65%) of 153.5l." -- Every listing opens with this line and it was being thrown away, which is -- why "too heavy" had to be remembered as a permanent property of the item. -- It is not: it is a fact about the item's mass against the room left in your -- pack, and it stops being true the moment you drop something or bank coins. -- -- The table is inv.carry, NOT inv.load: `inv.load` is already the function -- that reads the save file back. Shadowing it left every reader indexing a -- function value, which threw inside roomScanEnd and stopped iloot dead before -- it printed anything — and noteCarry assigning to it would have destroyed the -- loader for the rest of the session. inv.carry = inv.carry or {} function inv.noteCarry(line) if not line then return end local kg, maxKg, l, maxL = line:match("carrying%s+([%d.]+)kg.-of%s+([%d.]+)kg.-and%s+([%d.]+)l.-of%s+([%d.]+)l") if not kg then return end inv.carry = { kg = tonumber(kg), maxKg = tonumber(maxKg), l = tonumber(l), maxL = tonumber(maxL) } end
-- Free carrying mass in GRAMS, to match t.weight, or nil if never seen. function inv.freeGrams() local L = inv.carry if not (L and L.kg and L.maxKg) then return nil end return math.max(0, (L.maxKg - L.kg) * 1000) end
-- Refusals seen in THIS loot run only. A get that failed for weight tells us -- about the pack as it stood at that moment and nothing about the next room, -- so the table is cleared at the start of every run (see ilootRun). inv.tooHeavy = inv.tooHeavy or {}
-- Is this type out of reach right now? Two grounds, both about the present: -- * a get already refused it this run, and nothing has been dropped since -- * we know its mass and it exceeds the room left -- Returns false, or a reason string. function inv.tooHeavyNow(key) local rec = inv.tooHeavy[key] if rec then local now = inv.carry and inv.carry.kg -- If we are lighter than when it failed, the refusal is out of date and -- worth one command to re-test. if not (rec.kg and now and now < rec.kg - 0.05) then return string.format("refused as too heavy this run%s", rec.kg and string.format(" (at %.1fkg carried)", rec.kg) or "") end inv.tooHeavy[key] = nil end local t = inv.types[key] local free = inv.freeGrams() if t and t.weight and free and t.weight > free then return string.format("heavier than the room left (%.1fkg vs %.1fkg free)", t.weight/1000, free/1000) end return false end -- learned non-items (mobs, fixtures): names that refused pickup with -- "you cannot move" / "you see no". Persisted; auto-skipped by iloot. C.nonItems = C.nonItems or {} -- user-maintained exclude list (type keys never auto-looted) C.excludes = C.excludes or {}
inv.emaAlpha = inv.emaAlpha or 0.3
-- ---- Persistent stores ------------------------------------------------ -- types[key] = { name=, weight=, volume=, weightN=, volumeN=, -- sell={avg,min,max,n}, sac={avg,min,max,n}, keep=bool } -- key = lowercased full name (adjectives significant) inv.types = inv.types or {} -- locations: where instances live. Per container, an ORDERED list (index 1 = -- most recently stowed) of type-keys. "loose" and "keep" are pseudo-containers. -- loc[container] = { typeKey, typeKey, ... } (container = "loose"/"keep"/sackname) inv.loc = inv.loc or { loose = {}, keep = {} } -- containers[sackKey] = { name=, trusted=bool } trusted=false until re-stowed inv.contMeta = inv.contMeta or {}
inv.lastFavor = inv.lastFavor or nil inv.pendingSac = nil
-- ---- Name / handle utilities ----------------------------------------- -- Extract the glow affix from a raw item name, e.g. "<intense green glow>" or -- "<deep white glow>". Returns intensity, color (either may be nil) and the -- raw tag, or nil if the item doesn't glow. Glow is a candidate high-DF signal -- (collected now; not yet weighted in disposal). function inv.parseGlow(raw) if not raw then return nil end local tag = raw:match("<([^>]-glow)>") if not tag then return nil end -- forms: "intense green glow", "deep white glow", "green glow", "glow" local words = {} for w in tag:gmatch("%a+") do words[#words+1] = w end -- drop trailing "glow" if words[#words] == "glow" then words[#words] = nil end local intensity, color if #words >= 2 then intensity, color = words[1], words[2] elseif #words == 1 then color = words[1] end return { intensity = intensity, color = color, tag = tag } end
function inv.cleanName(raw) if not raw then return nil end local s = raw s = s:gsub("\27%[[0-9;]*m", "") s = s:gsub("%s*<[^>]->%s*", " ") -- strip <glow> tags s = s:gsub('%s+named%s+"[^"]*"', "") s = s:gsub("%s+named%s+'[^']*'", "") s = s:gsub("^%s*%d+%s*x%s+", "") -- "2 x " s = s:gsub("%s+%b()%s*$", "") -- trailing "(lit)" "(dark)" s = s:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") return s end
-- type key: full cleaned name lowercased, leading article removed function inv.key(raw) local c = inv.cleanName(raw) if not c then return nil end c = c:lower():gsub("^a%s+", ""):gsub("^an%s+", ""):gsub("^the%s+", "") return c end
-- ---- Handle candidate generation -------------------------------------- -- Icesus item names are display strings; the parser matches a SUBSET of the -- item's real id words. Empirically (see "big long smelly thing", whose real -- handles are "long smelly thing", "long thing", "smelly thing", "thing"): -- * the head noun always participates, -- * any order-preserving subset of the preceding modifiers may be prefixed, -- * not every display word is an id word ("big" above is not), -- * "<noun> of <qualifier>" is a valid, highly-specific handle, -- * words after a descriptive clause ("made out of caribou bone") can still -- be id words, usually as adjectives on the noun ("bone knife"). -- Because display words and id words do not coincide, we do NOT try to guess -- which subset is real. We ENUMERATE the plausible space and let inv.probe* -- test each one against the game. Guessing was the old design's mistake. -- -- The bare head noun is always the LAST entry: several call sites take -- cands[#cands] as "the head noun of this type".
inv._ladderCache = {}
-- ---- Hearts: one handle, always --------------------------------------- -- Almost every monster drops one. They are always "Bloodstained heart of -- <mob>", and the parser answers to exactly `heart` for all of them — no -- more (the mob words are not id words) and no less. That is a constant, so -- the ladder, the probe and the whole retry machinery have nothing to -- contribute here except commands spent rediscovering it every session. -- -- Consequence to keep in mind: `heart` names EVERY heart you are carrying. -- With four kinds in the bag, `sacrifice heart from "loot"` reaches one of -- them and the altar's short echo ("sacrifice heart on the altar") cannot say -- which. See inv.heartRivals / onSacFavour. inv.HEART_HANDLE = "heart"
function inv.isHeart(key) return key ~= nil and key:find("^bloodstained heart") ~= nil end
-- How many OTHER heart types share this container. >0 means a favour reading -- taken there cannot be pinned to the type we queued. function inv.heartRivals(container, key) if not inv.isHeart(key) then return 0 end local seen, n = {}, 0 for _, k in ipairs(inv.loc[container or "loose"] or {}) do if k ~= key and inv.isHeart(k) and not seen[k] then seen[k] = true; n = n + 1 end end return n end
-- Give a heart type its one true handle and clear anything the guessing -- machinery wrote about it earlier. function inv.heartSeed(key) if not inv.isHeart(key) or not inv.types[key] then return false end local h = inv.handlesOf(key, true) if not h then return false end local changed = (h.ok[inv.HEART_HANDLE] == nil) for k in pairs(h.ok) do if k ~= inv.HEART_HANDLE then h.ok[k] = nil; changed = true end end for k in pairs(h.bad) do h.bad[k] = nil; changed = true end for k in pairs(h.amb) do h.amb[k] = nil; changed = true end h.ok[inv.HEART_HANDLE] = h.ok[inv.HEART_HANDLE] or 1 h.probedAt = h.probedAt or os.time() if inv.stuck and inv.stuck[key] then inv.stuck[key] = nil; changed = true end
-- Every heart sells for 0 or 1 silver, which rounds to "not worth a shop -- visit" either way. Recording an established 0 up front means ishop never -- pulls one out, shows it to a keeper and stows it again — a three-command -- cycle per heart type, repeated forever, to learn a constant. local t = inv.types[key] t.sellCat = "food" -- sac-only: classify ignores silver t.noSell = nil -- 0 is a real figure, not "n/a" local want = math.max(inv.config.estN or 3, 1) if not (t.sell and t.sell.avg == 0 and (t.sell.n or 0) >= want) then t.sell = { avg = 0, min = 0, max = 0, n = want } changed = true end return changed end
-- ---- Gear vocabulary (from 'help materials' / 'help armour types' / -- 'help weapon types') ------------------------------------------------ -- The game publishes its own id words. Two rules fall straight out of them: -- -- ARMOUR: a piece answers to <main material> + <slot noun>. -- "Chitin studded leather leggings" -> `chitin leggings`. -- The main material is the one named BEFORE the armour type -- ("studded"); anything after it is the foundation the type is -- built on ("...studded into a backing" — help armour types), and -- it is not what the piece is called. -- WEAPONS: the description's "It most closely resembles a X." names the -- weapon type, which is a handle on its own and usually also with -- the material in front: `executioner's sword`, `steel sword`. -- -- This is not guessing: every string below is copied from a help file, so a -- candidate built from two of them is a far better first guess than the -- word-subset ladder, which has no idea which of "chitin", "studded" and -- "leather" the parser actually indexes. -- Longest entries first in each list — matching is longest-wins. inv.GEAR = { materials = { "augmented chain mail", -- (guarded below; never a material, see types) "chitinium silk", "heavy cloth", "soft leather", "fine steel", "cuir-boulli", "dragonscale", "adamantium", "aluminium", "demonhide", "platinum", "titanium", "crystal", "diamond", "mithril", "iceron", "leather", "bronze", "copper", "nickel", "silver", "chitin", "brass", "cloth", "steel", "stone", "wood", "bone", "gold", "iron", "lead", "silk", "clay", "coal", "fur", "tin", "zinc", }, armourTypes = { "augmented chain mail", "double chain mail", "chain mail", "scale mail", "plate mail", "full plate", "brigandine", "bezainted", "laminated", "lamellar", "ring mail", "studded", "standard", }, slots = { "augmented chain mail", -- placeholder trimmed at build time "horse leggings", "neck guard", "breastplate", "half-plate", "bracelets", "gauntlets", "medallion", "earrings", "leggings", "gambeson", "greaves", "sandals", "bracers", "cuirass", "hauberk", "earring", "helmet", "amulet", "pendant", "byrnie", "collar", "gloves", "tights", "shoes", "boots", "barding", "cloak", "scarf", "skirt", "pants", "shirt", "jerkin", "vest", "jack", "coat", "robe", "coif", "belt", "ring", "mask", "cap", "full helm", "helm", "armour", "armor", }, weapons = { "executioner's sword", "two-handed sword", "augmented chain mail", "hand crossbow", "throwing hammer", "throwing dagger", "throwing axe", "quarterstaff", "knight shield", "morningstar", "ball'n'chain", "manure fork", "kite shield", "tower shield", "small shield", "bastard sword", "bearded axe", "balestarius", "broadsword", "shortsword", "greatsword", "longsword", "staff sling", "pitch fork", "battle axe", "broad axe", "great axe", "hand axe", "head axe", "short bow", "long bow", "warhammer", "crossbow", "scimitar", "falchion", "claymore", "cutlass", "gladius", "buckler", "blowgun", "hatchet", "crowbar", "scourge", "javelin", "tziraan", "rapier", "dagger", "shovel", "scythe", "sickle", "pernat", "maul", "mace", "club", "dabus", "flail", "staff", "sling", "whip", "spear", "knife", "dart", "sabre", "hammer", "pick", "rake", "sword", "axe", "bow", }, } -- The placeholder above keeps each list non-empty in the source; drop it. for _, listName in ipairs({ "materials", "slots", "weapons" }) do local l = inv.GEAR[listName] for i = #l, 1, -1 do if l[i] == "augmented chain mail" then table.remove(l, i) end end end
-- Every occurrence of any list entry, as { phrase, from, to } word indexes. local function gearMatches(words, list) local lower = {} for i, w in ipairs(words) do lower[i] = w:lower() end local out = {} for _, phrase in ipairs(list) do local pw = {} for w in phrase:gmatch("%S+") do pw[#pw+1] = w end for i = 1, #lower - #pw + 1 do local hit = true for j = 1, #pw do if lower[i + j - 1] ~= pw[j] then hit = false; break end end if hit then out[#out+1] = { phrase = phrase, from = i, to = i + #pw - 1 } end end end return out end
-- The entry that ENDS latest (longest wins a tie), optionally ignoring -- matches that sit entirely inside another phrase's span. -- -- Rightmost, not longest-anywhere: Icesus names put the thing itself at the -- end. "Heavy cloth ring mail cap" is a cap, and picking the longest match -- anywhere made it a `ring` — `ring` being both a slot (finger) and the first -- word of the armour type `ring mail`. local function gearFindTail(words, list, exFrom, exTo) local best for _, m in ipairs(gearMatches(words, list)) do local inside = exFrom and exTo and m.from >= exFrom and m.to <= exTo if not inside then if (not best) or m.to > best.to or (m.to == best.to and #m.phrase > #best.phrase) then best = m end end end if not best then return nil end return best.phrase, best.from, best.to end
local ARMOUR_TYPE_WORD = {} -- filled after the tables above; used to stop nameParts treating an armour -- type like "studded" as a decorative clause marker. for _, t in ipairs(inv.GEAR.armourTypes) do for w in t:gmatch("%S+") do ARMOUR_TYPE_WORD[w] = true end end inv.ARMOUR_TYPE_WORD = ARMOUR_TYPE_WORD
-- What the help files can tell us about one type key. function inv.gearParts(key) local words = {} for w in (key or ""):gmatch("%S+") do words[#words+1] = w:gsub("[,%.]", "") end if #words == 0 then return nil end local atype, atypeAt, atypeEnd = gearFindTail(words, inv.GEAR.armourTypes) local slot = gearFindTail(words, inv.GEAR.slots, atypeAt, atypeEnd) local weapon = gearFindTail(words, inv.GEAR.weapons, atypeAt, atypeEnd)
-- Materials: every one present, leftmost first. The main one is the one -- named BEFORE the armour type; anything after it is the foundation the -- type is built on, which is not what the piece is called. local mats = gearMatches(words, inv.GEAR.materials) table.sort(mats, function(a, b) if a.from ~= b.from then return a.from < b.from end return #a.phrase > #b.phrase -- "heavy cloth" over "cloth" end) local material if atypeAt then for _, x in ipairs(mats) do if x.to < atypeAt then material = x.phrase; break end end end material = material or (mats[1] and mats[1].phrase)
return { material = material, atype = atype, slot = slot, weapon = weapon, lastWord = words[#words], nMats = #mats } end
-- Ordered, high-confidence candidates for a piece of gear. Empty for -- anything the help files do not describe. function inv.vocabLadder(key) local g = inv.gearParts(key) if not g then return {} end local out, seen = {}, {} local function add(s) if not s or s == "" or seen[s] then return end seen[s] = true; out[#out+1] = s end -- Prefer the slot noun for armour; fall back to the weapon type. When both -- match (a "shield" is both), the one nearer the end of the name wins by -- being the longer match, and slot is checked first because armour names -- carry a material far more often. local noun = g.slot or g.weapon if not noun then return {} end local tailNoun = noun:match("(%S+)$") local singular if noun:sub(-1) == "s" and #noun > 3 and noun:sub(-2) ~= "ss" then singular = noun:sub(1, -2) end
if g.slot then -- Armour. The material prefix is the rule, so it leads. if g.material then add(g.material .. " " .. noun) -- chitin leggings if singular then add(g.material .. " " .. singular) end if tailNoun ~= noun then add(g.material .. " " .. tailNoun) end -- steel helm end if g.atype then add(g.atype .. " " .. noun) end -- studded leggings add(noun) -- leggings / full helm if singular then add(singular) end -- boot if tailNoun ~= noun then add(tailNoun) end -- helm else -- Weapon. Here the material prefix is only SOMETIMES right, so the type -- itself leads. Confirmed counter-example: "Steel elven long dagger with -- red runes" answers to `elven long dagger` — and `steel dagger` and -- `long dagger` both returned "You see no '...' around here." add(noun) -- throwing axe if tailNoun ~= noun then add(tailNoun) end -- axe if g.material then add(g.material .. " " .. noun) -- bone throwing axe if tailNoun ~= noun then add(g.material .. " " .. tailNoun) end -- bone axe end end return out end
-- Words that introduce a trailing descriptive clause. "of" is special: it -- produces the "<noun> of <qualifier>" handle rather than being discarded. local CLAUSE_MARK = { ["with"]=1, ["inscribed"]=1, ["bearing"]=1, ["engraved"]=1, ["covered"]=1, ["that"]=1, ["which"]=1, ["depicting"]=1, ["made"]=1, ["for"]=1, ["from"]=1, ["in"]=1, ["on"]=1, ["of"]=2, -- decorative participles: what follows describes, it does not identify ["decorated"]=1, ["adorned"]=1, ["studded"]=1, ["encrusted"]=1, ["etched"]=1, ["carved"]=1, ["embroidered"]=1, ["wrapped"]=1, ["painted"]=1, ["lined"]=1, ["tipped"]=1, ["infused"]=1, } -- Connectives that are never id words on their own. local CLAUSE_SKIP = { ["made"]=true, ["out"]=true, ["of"]=true, ["with"]=true, ["a"]=true, ["an"]=true, ["the"]=true, ["that"]=true, ["for"]=true, ["from"]=true, ["and"]=true, ["into"]=true, ["it"]=true, ["its"]=true, ["some"]=true, ["by"]=true, ["in"]=true, ["on"]=true, ["to"]=true, ["is"]=true, }
-- Measure words. In "heart of kobold" the noun is HEART and "heart of kobold" -- is a fine handle. In "a piece of rotten bread" the noun is BREAD — "piece" -- only counts the thing — and "piece of rotten bread" is a display name the -- parser does not know, which is why sacrificing it reported nothing to -- sacrifice while three of them sat in the bag. -- Deliberately conservative: "sack of oil" and "set of bandages" are real -- objects whose "of" form does work, so those words are NOT listed here. local PARTITIVE = { piece = true, pieces = true, chunk = true, chunks = true, slice = true, slices = true, hunk = true, lump = true, lumps = true, handful = true, pinch = true, portion = true, bunch = true, stack = true, glob = true, mound = true, heap = true, scrap = true, scraps = true, shred = true, sliver = true, fragment = true, morsel = true, bit = true, loaf = true, }
-- Split a type key into head noun, leading modifiers, clause-tail words, -- the full "<noun> of <qualifier>" form, and the measure word if the "of" -- was partitive. function inv.nameParts(key) local words = {} for w in key:gmatch("%S+") do words[#words+1] = w end if #words == 0 then return nil, {}, {}, nil end
-- A comma ends the identifying part of a name: "silver necklace, decorated -- with sapphires" is a necklace, and everything after the comma is prose. -- Commas are also the game's multi-target separator, so one left inside a -- handle is misparsed outright ("value necklace," reached nothing). for i, w in ipairs(words) do if w:find(",") then local trimmed = {} for j = 1, i do trimmed[j] = words[j]:gsub(",", "") end words = trimmed break end end for i, w in ipairs(words) do words[i] = w:gsub(",", "") end local cut, kind for i, w in ipairs(words) do -- "studded" is listed as a decorative participle, but 'help armour types' -- lists it as an armour TYPE. Cutting the name there turned "Chitin -- studded leather leggings" into a thing whose head noun was "chitin". if CLAUSE_MARK[w] and i > 1 and not inv.ARMOUR_TYPE_WORD[w] then cut = i; kind = CLAUSE_MARK[w]; break end end local head, rest = words, {} if cut then head = {} for j = 1, cut - 1 do head[j] = words[j] end for j = cut, #words do rest[#rest+1] = words[j] end end local tail = {} for _, w in ipairs(rest) do if not CLAUSE_SKIP[w] then tail[#tail+1] = w end end local noun = head[#head] local mods = {} for j = 1, #head - 1 do mods[j] = head[j] end local ofForm = (kind == 2) and table.concat(words, " ", cut - 1) or nil
-- Partitive: re-seat the head noun on the far side of "of". -- "piece of rotten bread" -> noun "bread", mods {"rotten"}, part "piece" local partWord if kind == 2 and noun and PARTITIVE[noun] and #tail >= 1 then partWord = noun noun = tail[#tail] local newMods = {} for j = 1, #tail - 1 do newMods[j] = tail[j] end mods, tail = newMods, {} end
return noun, mods, tail, ofForm, partWord end
-- Full candidate ladder, most specific first, bare head noun last. function inv.handleLadder(key) if not key or key == "" then return {} end if inv.isHeart(key) then return { inv.HEART_HANDLE } end local hit = inv._ladderCache[key] if hit then return hit end local noun, mods, tail, ofForm, partWord = inv.nameParts(key) if not noun then inv._ladderCache[key] = {}; return {} end
local out, seen = {}, {} local function add(s) if not s or s == "" or s == "it" or seen[s] then return end -- A candidate must not START with a connective. "Flint and steel" has no -- clause marker, so "and" survives as a leading modifier and the subset -- enumeration offers `and steel` — a string the parser cannot know, spent -- as a real command and then filed as a refused handle. The full form -- "flint and steel" is still generated and still probed; only the ones -- beginning mid-connective are dropped. if CLAUSE_SKIP[s:match("^(%S+)") or ""] then return end seen[s] = true; out[#out+1] = s end
-- 0. what the help files say this thing is called. Copied vocabulary beats -- a guessed word subset, so these go to the front of the probe order — -- which matters, because probeMax caps how many ever get tested. for _, c in ipairs(inv.vocabLadder(key)) do add(c) end
-- 1. the "<noun> of <qualifier>" form: proven reliable and very specific. add(ofForm)
-- 2. every order-preserving subset of the leading modifiers + the noun, -- largest subset first. Capped to the 5 modifiers nearest the noun -- (31 combinations) so pathological names can't explode. local m = mods if #m > 5 then local trimmed = {} for i = #m - 4, #m do trimmed[#trimmed+1] = m[i] end m = trimmed end local subs = {} for mask = 0, (2 ^ #m) - 1 do local parts = {} for i = 1, #m do if math.floor(mask / 2 ^ (i - 1)) % 2 == 1 then parts[#parts+1] = m[i] end end if #parts > 0 then parts[#parts+1] = noun subs[#subs+1] = { s = table.concat(parts, " "), n = #parts } end end table.sort(subs, function(a, b) if a.n ~= b.n then return a.n > b.n end return a.s < b.s end) for _, e in ipairs(subs) do add(e.s) end
-- 3. clause-tail words as adjectives on the noun: "caribou bone knife", -- "bone knife", "caribou knife". if #tail > 0 then local t = tail if #t > 3 then local trimmed = {} for i = #t - 2, #t do trimmed[#trimmed+1] = t[i] end t = trimmed end if #t > 1 then add(table.concat(t, " ") .. " " .. noun) end for i = #t, 1, -1 do add(t[i] .. " " .. noun) end end
-- 4. the measure word of a partitive name ("piece"), which some items do -- answer to, then the bare head noun, always last. add(partWord) add(noun)
inv._ladderCache[key] = out return out end
-- Back-compat name: several call sites still ask for "candidates". function inv.handleCandidates(key) return inv.handleLadder(key) end
-- The ladder above is for PROBING: it enumerates everything plausible, -- most specific first, and the game tells us which rungs are real. It is the -- wrong order for sending a command blind, because its most specific rung is -- the full display name — and the full display name is usually NOT a handle -- ("big" is not an id word in "big long smelly thing"). Sending it wastes the -- command. Until a type has proven handles we fall back to the three forms -- that are reliable across items: the "of" form, the compound-noun tail, and -- the bare head noun. function inv.blindLadder(key) if inv.isHeart(key) then return { inv.HEART_HANDLE } end local noun, mods, _, ofForm, partWord = inv.nameParts(key) if not noun then return {} end local out, seen = {}, {} local function add(x) if x and x ~= "" and not seen[x] then seen[x] = true; out[#out+1] = x end end -- Vocabulary first. This is the list sent WITHOUT probing, and it used to -- offer only {<nearest modifier> <noun>, <noun>} — for "Chitin studded -- leather leggings" that is "leather leggings" and "leggings", neither of -- which is the material the piece is named for. for _, c in ipairs(inv.vocabLadder(key)) do add(c) end -- The nearest modifier that is actually an id word. Taking mods[#mods] -- blindly sent `get and steel` for "Flint and steel" — a wasted command, and -- a nonsense string on the refused list forever after. local nearMod for j = #mods, 1, -1 do if not CLAUSE_SKIP[mods[j]] then nearMod = mods[j]; break end end if partWord then -- the "of" form here is a display name, not an id: try it only after the -- real noun and its adjective if nearMod then add(nearMod .. " " .. noun) end add(ofForm) else add(ofForm) if nearMod then add(nearMod .. " " .. noun) end end add(noun) -- always last: callers take the final entry as the bare noun return out end
-- A queue is built up front, so every job for a type carries the handle that -- was best at build time. When that handle turns out to be wrong, the other -- seventeen queued sales are still holding it — which is how one bad handle -- produced three identical failures and killed an eighteen-item run. function inv.requeueHandle(key) local n = 0 for _, q in ipairs(inv.shopQueue or {}) do if q.key == key then local ref, h = inv.bagRef(q.container, key) if ref and h and h ~= q.handle then q.handle = h if q.kind == "sell" then q.sellCmd = "sell " .. ref else q.getCmd = q.getCmd and ("get " .. ref) or nil q.vref = h end n = n + 1 end end end for _, e in ipairs(inv.sacQueue or {}) do if e.key == key then local ref, h = inv.bagRef(e.container, key) if ref and h and h ~= e.handle then e.ref, e.handle, n = ref, h, n + 1 end end end if n > 0 then inv.note(string.format("re-addressed %d queued command(s) for %s", n, (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key)) end return n end
-- The next handle worth trying for `key`, skipping everything in `tried`. -- Shortest first: `look` will accept a long display form that `get` and -- `sacrifice` refuse, so a probe-proven handle is not automatically an -- actionable one and the compact forms deserve the first try. function inv.nextHandleAfter(key, tried) if type(tried) == "string" then tried = { [tried] = true } end tried = tried or {} local h = inv.handlesOf(key) local function usable(c) return c and not tried[c] and not (h and h.bad[c]) end -- "all", deliberately: this is the RETRY ladder, so a look-proven string is -- exactly what we want next once the action-proven one has just failed. -- Filtering them out here would skip straight past the handles the prober -- mined from the item's description ("It most closely resembles a ..."), -- which exist nowhere else — the blind ladder can only recombine the words -- already in the display name. local proven = inv.handleList(key, "all") for i = #proven, 1, -1 do if usable(proven[i]) then return proven[i] end end local blind = inv.blindLadder(key) for i = #blind, 1, -1 do if usable(blind[i]) then return blind[i] end end return nil end
-- How many alternatives an action may burn before it concludes the item is -- simply not there. inv.HANDLE_RETRIES = 3
function inv.note(m) if inv.config.verbose then cecho("\n<cyan>[inv]<reset> "..m.."\n") end end function inv.warn(m) cecho("\n<yellow>[inv]<reset> "..m.."\n") end
-- ---- Learned handles (schema v3) -------------------------------------- -- An item answers to MANY handles, so we store a SET, not a winner. The two -- negative sets mean different things and must never be merged: -- ok = { handle -> confirmations } proven to name THIS type -- bad = { handle -> true } the game does not know the string at -- all ("Look at what?" / "You see no") -- amb = { handle -> true } a real string that reached a DIFFERENT -- item. Still valid for this type when -- qualified with an index; never bare. -- v2 stored ok as a single string. Migrated in place on first touch. function inv.handlesOf(key, create) local t = key and inv.types[key] if not t then return nil end if not t.handles then if not create then return nil end t.handles = {} end local h = t.handles if type(h.ok) == "string" then h.ok = { [h.ok] = 1 } end if type(h.ok) ~= "table" then h.ok = {} end h.bad = h.bad or {} h.amb = h.amb or {} -- Provenance: which VERB proved each handle. See inv.handleList. h.src = h.src or {} h.v = 4 return h end
local function handleWordCount(h) local n = 0 for _ in h:gmatch("%S+") do n = n + 1 end return n end
-- ---- Provenance: a `look` hit is not proof that `get` can reach it ----- -- The prober uses `look`, because it is free and non-destructive. But Icesus' -- `look` parser is MORE PERMISSIVE than the parsers behind `get`, `put`, -- `sell` and `sacrifice` — the package already admits as much in ihandle's -- "look is more permissive than get" hint. So a look hit proves only that the -- string names the item to the LOOK verb. Treating that as a proven handle is -- how the package talks itself into certainty about a string no action can -- use: `l cerbie's skin on ground` answers, `get cerbie's skin` does not, and -- every run afterwards sends the same dead string with full confidence. -- -- Each confirmed handle therefore carries the verb that proved it: -- "act" an action moved the item with it (get/put/sell/sacrifice, or a -- hand-entered `ihandle ... force`) — actionable, trust it -- "look" only the prober has seen it work — a CANDIDATE, not a handle -- "act" outranks "look" and never downgrades. -- `show id` gives the parser's TARGETING aliases ("Type any of those names to -- target this item"). Targeting is not handling: the parsers behind `get`, -- `put`, `sell` and `sacrifice` accept a NARROWER set. Proven in play -- -- `show id` lists "Murky grey scale mail" for an iron scale mail armour, and -- `get murky grey scale mail` answers "You see no ... around here" while -- `get scale mail` works. So a `show id` name is a strong CANDIDATE (the -- parser's own words, including ones the blind ladder can't derive), ranked -- ABOVE a look guess but BELOW a handle a real action has proven. Only "act" -- means "a handling verb moved the item with this string"; that alone is -- trustworthy for object handling, and that alone can clear a `bad`/`amb` -- verdict (see handleRecordOk / handleRecordBad). inv.HANDLE_SRC_ID = "id" -- from `show id` — targeting-proven, a candidate inv.HANDLE_SRC_ACT = "act" -- a handling verb moved the item with it — trust it inv.HANDLE_SRC_LOOK = "look" -- only `look` has seen it — the weakest candidate inv.HANDLE_RANK = { act = 3, id = 2, look = 1 }
function inv.handleSrc(key, handle) local h = inv.handlesOf(key) -- Absent provenance means the entry predates this bookkeeping; migrate() -- seeds those as "look", which is the pessimistic and therefore safe read. return (h and handle and h.src[handle]) or inv.HANDLE_SRC_LOOK end
function inv.handleActProven(key, handle) return inv.handleSrc(key, handle) == inv.HANDLE_SRC_ACT end
-- Confirmed handles, most specific (longest) first. -- -- Action-proven handles SHADOW look-proven ones entirely rather than merely -- sorting above them: once any string is known to work with a real verb, -- offering the ladder a string that has only ever survived `look` is offering -- it a guess. Callers that want the whole picture (iitem, ihandle) pass -- "all". This is the whole fix — every caller below prefers action evidence -- without any of them having to know that provenance exists. function inv.handleList(key, scope) local h = inv.handlesOf(key) if not h then return {} end local id, act, look = {}, {}, {} for s in pairs(h.ok) do local src = inv.handleSrc(key, s) if src == inv.HANDLE_SRC_ID then id[#id+1] = s elseif src == inv.HANDLE_SRC_ACT then act[#act+1] = s else look[#look+1] = s end end local function bySpecificity(t) table.sort(t, function(a, b) local wa, wb = handleWordCount(a), handleWordCount(b) if wa ~= wb then return wa > wb end if #a ~= #b then return #a > #b end return a < b end) return t end -- Preference: a handle a real action has proven first (the only kind trusted -- for handling), then `show id` targeting candidates, then look guesses. if scope == "all" then bySpecificity(act); bySpecificity(id); bySpecificity(look) local out = {} for _, s in ipairs(act) do out[#out+1] = s end for _, s in ipairs(id) do out[#out+1] = s end for _, s in ipairs(look) do out[#out+1] = s end return out end if #act > 0 then return bySpecificity(act) end if #id > 0 then return bySpecificity(id) end return bySpecificity(look) end
-- Most specific confirmed handle (the safest one to send blind), or nil. function inv.handleKnown(key) return inv.handleList(key)[1] end
-- Shortest confirmed handle, or nil. function inv.handleShortest(key) local l = inv.handleList(key) return l[#l] end
-- src is "act" or "look" (see above). Callers that omit it are the ones that -- observed a real action succeed, so it defaults to "act"; the prober is the -- only caller that must pass "look" explicitly. function inv.handleRecordOk(key, handle, src) local h = inv.handlesOf(key, true) if not h or not handle then return end src = src or inv.HANDLE_SRC_ACT local rank = inv.HANDLE_RANK -- Only a real ACTION disproves a handling verdict. A `show id` (targeting) or -- `look` recognition is the permissive parser talking, so it must NOT -- resurrect a handle a handling verb already ruled out (`bad`) -- otherwise -- every `show id` clears the very demotion the last failed `get` just learned, -- and the dead appearance-name is re-sent on every run forever. That -- re-adoption loop is exactly the "one of the handles does not move the item" -- report. A handle marked bad stays a candidate for nobody until an action -- proves otherwise. if src ~= inv.HANDLE_SRC_ACT and h.bad[handle] then return end local first = not h.ok[handle] local upgraded = (not first) and (rank[src] or 0) > (rank[h.src[handle]] or 0) h.ok[handle] = (h.ok[handle] or 0) + 1 -- never downgrade: keep the strongest evidence seen (act > id > look). A later -- look hit on an action-proven handle tells us nothing new; a `show id` -- reading upgrades a look guess to a targeting candidate but never past a -- handle a real action has moved the item with. if not h.src[handle] or (rank[src] or 0) > (rank[h.src[handle]] or 0) then h.src[handle] = src end -- Clearing the negative verdicts is act-only, for the same reason as the -- resurrection guard above: only a handling verb can retract "does not move -- this item" / "reached a different item". if src == inv.HANDLE_SRC_ACT then h.bad[handle] = nil h.amb[handle] = nil end if first then local t = inv.types[key] local how = (src == inv.HANDLE_SRC_ID) and "from show id" or (src == inv.HANDLE_SRC_ACT) and "confirmed" or "looks usable" inv.note(string.format("handle %s for %s: '%s'", how, (t and t.name) or key, handle)) inv.save() elseif upgraded then local t = inv.types[key] inv.note(string.format("handle confirmed by use for %s: '%s'", (t and t.name) or key, handle)) inv.save() end end
-- The game does not recognise this string for this item, ever. function inv.handleRecordBad(key, handle) -- `heart` is a known constant, not a guess. A failed `sacrifice heart` means -- the bag is empty of hearts (or a sibling got there first), never that the -- word is wrong — and demoting it would leave the type with no handle at all. if inv.isHeart(key) and handle == inv.HEART_HANDLE then return end local h = inv.handlesOf(key, true) if not h or not handle then return end if not h.bad[handle] then h.bad[handle] = true h.ok[handle] = nil h.src[handle] = nil inv.save() end end
-- An action refused a handle the prober had blessed. That is not bad luck, it -- is the look/act asymmetry showing itself, and it is the single most useful -- fact the package can learn about that string: `look` will keep answering to -- it forever, so nothing else will ever disprove it. Demote it and say so. -- An action-proven handle that fails is a different animal — the item is -- probably not where the map thinks — so that case is left to the caller. function inv.handleFailedAction(key, handle, verb) if not key or not handle then return false end local wasAct = inv.handleActProven(key, handle) inv.handleRecordBad(key, handle) if not wasAct then inv.warn(string.format("'%s' answers to `look` but not to `%s` — dropped for %s.", handle, verb or "get", (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key)) end return not wasAct end
-- The string is real but it reached a different item. NOT a bad handle — it -- just needs an index, and it may be the only short handle we have. -- -- Ambiguity is SCOPED, because Icesus' verbs are scoped: `get` only sees the -- ground, `put` only sees inventory, `look` sees both and searches inventory -- first. A handle shadowed by something you are carrying is still perfectly -- safe to `get` off the floor, so blanket-blocking it would throw away a good -- short handle for no reason. scope is one of: -- "inventory" something carried shadows it -- "ground" something on the floor shadows it -- "container:<k>" something in that bag shadows it -- "any" unknown context — blocks everywhere (legacy `true`) -- -- Scopes ACCUMULATE into a set. They used to collapse: a second, different -- scope rewrote the entry as "any", which blocks the handle everywhere and -- can never be walked back. Two ordinary observations — `skin` is shadowed in -- your pack, and `skin` is shadowed on the floor — were enough to permanently -- forbid `skin from "loot"`, a context neither observation said anything -- about. Stripping the last short handle that way is what leaves a type with -- nothing but a long look-artifact to send. Recording {inventory, ground} -- keeps both facts without inventing a third. local function ambSet(h, handle) local a = h.amb[handle] if a == nil then return nil end if type(a) == "table" then return a end local set = {} if a == true then set.any = true else set[a] = true end h.amb[handle] = set -- migrate the legacy string/boolean in place return set end
function inv.handleRecordAmb(key, handle, scope) -- Same reasoning as handleRecordBad: `heart` is the only string every heart -- answers to, so a collision between two kinds of heart is structural, not a -- handle mistake. There is nothing more specific to escalate to, and marking -- it merely blocks the one handle that works. That collision is resolved by -- taking both and dropping the surplus (see roomScanEnd), not by learning. if inv.isHeart(key) and handle == inv.HEART_HANDLE then return end local h = inv.handlesOf(key, true) if not h or not handle then return end scope = scope or "any" local set = ambSet(h, handle) if set and set[scope] then return end set = set or {} set[scope] = true h.amb[handle] = set inv.save() end
-- A successful action in a scope is evidence the shadow is not there (any -- more): clear that one scope, and the whole entry once none are left. Without -- this, ambiguity is still a one-way door, just a narrower one. function inv.handleClearAmb(key, handle, scope) local h = inv.handlesOf(key) if not h or not handle then return end local set = ambSet(h, handle) if not set then return end if not (set[scope] or set.any) then return end set[scope] = nil; set.any = nil if next(set) == nil then h.amb[handle] = nil end inv.save() end
-- The scopes an ambiguity has been observed in, sorted, for display. function inv.ambScopes(key, handle) local h = inv.handlesOf(key) local set = h and handle and ambSet(h, handle) if not set then return {} end local out = {} for s in pairs(set) do out[#out+1] = s end table.sort(out) return out end
function inv.handleIsBad(key, handle) local h = inv.handlesOf(key) return (h and handle and h.bad[handle]) and true or false end function inv.handleIsAmb(key, handle) local h = inv.handlesOf(key) return (h and handle and h.amb[handle]) and true or false end -- Does a recorded ambiguity actually block this handle in this context? -- ctx "ground" a room `get` — only ground items can answer -- ctx "inventory" `put` / `drop` / a loose reference -- ctx "container:<k>" a reference qualified with from "<sack>" function inv.ambBlocks(key, handle, ctx) local h = inv.handlesOf(key) local set = h and handle and ambSet(h, handle) if not set then return false end if set.any then return true end return set[ctx] == true end function inv.ambContext(container) if not container or container == "loose" or container == "keep" then return "inventory" end return "container:"..container end -- Has this type been through a probe run? function inv.handleProbed(key) -- Nothing to learn about a heart: the handle is known a priori. if inv.isHeart(key) then return true end local h = inv.handlesOf(key) return (h and h.probedAt) and true or false end
-- ---- Types the handle layer gave up on -------------------------------- -- Manual handle entry should be the last resort, so the package has to be -- honest about the exact moment it becomes necessary — which is when an -- action failed AND the retry ladder had nothing left to offer. That is not -- a transient miss: it is the structurally-unreachable case from the notes, -- where the working handle uses a word the display name does not contain -- ("Empty medium sized sack" answers to `sack of oil`). No amount of further -- guessing reaches it. -- -- Marked at the give-up points, cleared the moment an action provably works, -- and surfaced at the end of every ishop / isac / iprobe run. inv.stuck = inv.stuck or {}
function inv.markStuck(key, why, container) if not key or key == "" or not inv.types[key] then return end local s = inv.stuck[key] if not s then s = { key = key, n = 0 }; inv.stuck[key] = s end s.name = inv.types[key].name or key s.why = why or s.why s.container = container or s.container s.n = (s.n or 0) + 1 inv.save() end
function inv.clearStuck(key) if key and inv.stuck[key] then inv.stuck[key] = nil inv.save() end end
-- Where an instance of this type currently sits, or nil if the map says we no -- longer hold one anywhere. Loose and keep are checked first because those are -- the scopes `l <handle>` reaches without a container qualifier. -- `recorded` is the container the entry was raised against. "ground" is not a -- tracked location — the map models the pack, not the floor — so a ground -- entry cannot be confirmed or refuted by it and must be taken at face value. -- Without this, every request raised by iloot was pruned the instant it was -- created and the run then cheerfully reported "nothing is stuck". function inv.stuckWhere(key, recorded) if recorded == "ground" then return "ground" end if inv.locCount("loose", key) > 0 then return "loose" end if inv.locCount("keep", key) > 0 then return "keep" end return (inv.containersWith(key))[1] end
-- A stuck entry is only actionable while an instance survives to test a handle -- against. Both give-up sites prune that instance from the location map in the -- same breath as marking it stuck -- onSacNothing's locRemove runs immediately -- after its markStuck, and so does onNotCarried's -- so an entry raised on the -- LAST instance was born dead and then nagged at the tail of every run -- afterwards. The old filter here only asked whether inv.types[key] existed, -- which is permanent knowledge about the type and says nothing about whether -- we still carry one. -- -- Pruning here rather than at the failure sites covers every present and -- future caller of markStuck, and it is self-correcting in the direction that -- matters: markStuck fires at the point of failure, so an entry dropped -- because the map was stale simply comes back the next time an action misses. -- Nothing expensive is lost either way -- the refused-handle list lives on the -- type (handlesOf(key).bad) and is what stops the same dead guesses being -- offered back. function inv.stuckList() local out, pruned = {}, false for k, s in pairs(inv.stuck) do local where = inv.types[s.key] and inv.stuckWhere(s.key, s.container) if not where then inv.stuck[k] = nil -- gone: nothing left to fix pruned = true else s.container = where -- still here, but possibly moved bags out[#out+1] = s end end if pruned then inv.save() end table.sort(out, function(a, b) return (a.name or a.key) < (b.name or b.key) end) return out end
-- Print the list. Deliberately verbose: this is the one place the package -- asks for something, so it shows what it already tried (so the same guess is -- not offered back) and the two exact commands to run. function inv.stuckReport() local l = inv.stuckList() if #l == 0 then cecho("\n<green>[ihandle]<reset> nothing is stuck — every type an action touched has a working handle.\n") return 0 end cecho(string.format( "\n<yellow>[ihandle]<reset> %d type(s) need a handle from you:\n", #l)) for i, s in ipairs(l) do -- `look` is scoped like every other verb, so the hint has to name the -- right place: ' on ground' for a room item, ' in "bag"' for a stowed one. -- Printing 'l YOURGUESS in "ground"' just teaches the user a syntax error. local scope = "" if s.container == "ground" then scope = " on ground" elseif s.container and s.container ~= "loose" and s.container ~= "keep" then scope = string.format(' in "%s"', s.container) end cecho(string.format(" <white>%d.<reset> <cyan>%s<reset>%s\n", i, s.name or s.key, scope ~= "" and (" <grey>"..scope.."<reset>") or " <grey>(loose)<reset>")) local h = inv.handlesOf(s.key) local tried = {} if h then for b in pairs(h.bad) do tried[#tried+1] = b end end table.sort(tried) if #tried > 0 then local show = {} for j = 1, math.min(5, #tried) do show[j] = tried[j] end cecho(string.format(" <grey>refused:<reset> %s%s\n", table.concat(show, ", "), #tried > 5 and string.format(" (+%d more)", #tried - 5) or "")) end if s.why then cecho(string.format(" <grey>failed:<reset> %s\n", s.why)) end cecho(string.format( " <grey>probe it:<reset> <cyan>l YOURGUESS%s<reset> <grey>then:<reset> <cyan>ihandle %d YOURGUESS<reset>\n", scope, i)) end cecho(" <grey>Look at the item's description first — it often names a handle the\n" .. " display name cannot produce (\"It most closely resembles ...\").<reset>\n") return #l end
-- A request raised against the GROUND is only actionable while you are still -- standing in that room: its probe hint is `l YOURGUESS on ground`, which -- cannot work anywhere else. Two things follow. -- -- Drop such an entry the moment a room scan proves the item is not here. That -- is direct evidence, and it costs nothing to be wrong — markStuck fires at -- the point of failure, so the request comes straight back if the type is -- still unreachable somewhere it matters. function inv.stuckDropAbsentGround(presentKeys) local dropped = 0 for k, s in pairs(inv.stuck) do if s.container == "ground" and not presentKeys[s.key] then inv.stuck[k] = nil; dropped = dropped + 1 end end if dropped > 0 then inv.save() end return dropped end
-- And do not nag about one from a shop or altar run. The item is somewhere -- else entirely; naming it there is a phantom complaint about a room you left. function inv.stuckNag(context) if next(inv.stuck) == nil then return end if context ~= "loot" then local actionable = false for _, s in ipairs(inv.stuckList()) do if s.container ~= "ground" then actionable = true; break end end if not actionable then return end end inv.stuckReport() end
-- ihandle — the last resort. Verifies before recording, because a handle -- entered by hand that silently does not work is worse than no handle: it -- becomes the preferred one and every action for that type fails on it. function inv.handleCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") if arg == "" or arg == "list" then return inv.stuckReport() end
-- `ihandle reset <name>` — forget every refusal for a type. -- -- The bad list is deliberately permanent, which is right for one wrong guess -- and wrong for a whole burned ladder: once every rung is on it there is no -- command left to send, so no action can ever run, so nothing can ever be -- promoted. That is a dead end with no exit, and a type reaches it easily -- when refusals come from the item being GONE rather than the handle being -- wrong. This is the exit. local rs = arg:match("^reset%s+(.+)$") if rs then local key = inv.key(rs) if not (key and inv.types[key]) then local hit for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do if k:find(rs:lower(), 1, true) or (t.name and t.name:lower():find(rs:lower(), 1, true)) then hit = k; break end end key = hit end if not key then inv.warn(string.format("'%s' is not a tracked type — try 'iinv' for exact names.", rs)) return end local h = inv.handlesOf(key, true) local n = 0 for b in pairs(h.bad) do h.bad[b] = nil; n = n + 1 end h.probedAt = nil -- let iprobe have another go, too inv.clearStuck(key) inv.save() cecho(string.format( "\n<green>[ihandle]<reset> cleared %d refusal(s) for <white>%s<reset>. " .."<grey>Next iloot/iprobe will start the ladder over.<reset>\n", n, (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key)) return end
-- `ihandle forget <N|"name">` — a GHOST: the map lists the item but it is not -- actually there (a stale duplicate the pre-9.28 handle-poisoning left behind, -- or an item disposed of outside the package). Remove every phantom instance -- from the map and clear its stuck entry. Use when you KNOW you don't have it. local fg = arg:match("^forget%s+(.+)$") if fg then fg = fg:gsub('^"(.*)"$', "%1"):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") -- allow a quoted name local key local n = tonumber(fg) if n then local s = inv.stuckList()[n] if s then key = s.key end end if not key then key = inv.key(fg) if not (key and inv.types[key]) then for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do if k:find(fg:lower(), 1, true) or (t.name and t.name:lower():find(fg:lower(), 1, true)) then key = k; break end end end end if not key then inv.warn(string.format("'%s' is not a stuck item or tracked type — run 'ihandle' for the list.", fg)) return end local removed = 0 for cont in pairs(inv.loc) do if cont ~= "keep" then while inv.locRemove(cont, key, 1) do removed = removed + 1 end end end inv.clearStuck(key) inv.save() cecho(string.format( "\n<green>[ihandle]<reset> forgot <white>%s<reset> — removed %d phantom instance(s) from the map.\n", (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key, removed)) return end
local force = false if arg:match("%s+force$") then force = true arg = arg:gsub("%s+force$", "") end
local key, handle, s local idx, rest = arg:match("^(%d+)%s+(.+)$") if idx then local l = inv.stuckList() s = l[tonumber(idx)] if not s then inv.warn(string.format("there is no stuck item #%s — run 'ihandle' for the list.", idx)) return end key, handle = s.key, rest else local nm, rest2 = arg:match('^"([^"]+)"%s+(.+)$') if nm then key, handle = inv.key(nm), rest2 if not inv.types[key] then inv.warn(string.format("'%s' is not a tracked type — nothing was recorded. " .."Use the number from 'ihandle', or 'iinv' for exact names.", nm)) return end else inv.warn("usage: ihandle -- list types that need help") inv.warn(" ihandle 1 sack of oil -- by number from that list") inv.warn(' ihandle "Empty medium sized sack" sack of oil') inv.warn(" ...append force to record without the look check") inv.warn(" ihandle reset NAME -- forget every refusal for a type") inv.warn(" ihandle forget 1 -- drop a GHOST you don't actually have") return end end
handle = (handle or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", ""):lower() if handle == "" then inv.warn("no handle given."); return end local name = (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key
if force then inv.handleRecordOk(key, handle) inv.clearStuck(key) cecho(string.format( "\n<green>[ihandle]<reset> recorded '<cyan>%s<reset>' for <white>%s<reset> <grey>(unverified)<reset>\n", handle, name)) return end
if inv.probeBusy() then inv.warn("a probe is running — try again in a moment.") return end
cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[ihandle]<reset> testing '<cyan>%s<reset>' against <white>%s<reset>...\n", handle, name)) local started = inv.probeStart(key, { cands = { handle }, force = true, source = "ihandle", onDone = function() local h = inv.handlesOf(key) if h and h.ok[handle] then inv.clearStuck(key) cecho(string.format( "\n<green>[ihandle]<reset> learned: <white>%s<reset> answers to '<cyan>%s<reset>'.\n", name, handle)) else cecho(string.format( "\n<yellow>[ihandle]<reset> '%s' did not reach %s — nothing recorded. " .."<grey>(look is more permissive than get, so if you are sure, use: ihandle ... force)<reset>\n", handle, name)) end end, }) if not started then inv.warn("could not start the check (item not tracked, or the string is unusable).") end end
-- ---- Passive handle verification -------------------------------------- -- A "deliberate" single get registers what it intended; the next get-result -- or refusal reconciles it. Batch loot does NOT register (avoids the -- response-correlation desync). inv.pendingGet = nil -- { key=, handle=, container= } or nil
function inv.verifyArm(key, handle, container) inv.pendingGet = { key = key, handle = handle, container = container } end
-- Called from the "You get the <full name> [to a sack]" echo. function inv.verifyGotItem(fullName) local p = inv.pendingGet; if not p then return end inv.pendingGet = nil local gotKey = inv.key(fullName) if not gotKey then return end if gotKey == p.key then inv.handleRecordOk(p.key, p.handle) else -- WRONG item grabbed. The handle is REAL, it just collided with something -- else present. Record ambiguity, never badness — blacklisting here is -- what used to throw away the good short handles. -- the get was ground-scoped, so the shadow is another item on the floor inv.handleRecordAmb(p.key, p.handle, "ground") -- The handle demonstrably names the item we actually got, so that's a -- free positive for the other type. inv.handleRecordOk(gotKey, p.handle) inv.warn(string.format("'%s' reached the wrong item (%s) — marked ambiguous; putting it back.", p.handle, inv.cleanName(fullName) or fullName)) local back = p.container and p.container ~= "loose" and string.format('put %s in "%s"', p.handle, p.container) or nil if back then send(back, false) end end end
-- Called from "You see no '<handle>' around here." — a true non-match. function inv.verifyNoSuch(handle) local p = inv.pendingGet; if not p then return end if handle and p.handle and handle:lower() == p.handle:lower() then inv.handleRecordBad(p.key, p.handle) inv.pendingGet = nil end end
-- ---- Active handle probing via `look` --------------------------------- -- `look <handle>` is free, non-destructive, and reaches both the room and -- carried items. A hit prints the item's description; a miss prints exactly -- "Look at what?". Icesus answers commands chronologically and emits one -- prompt per command, so we probe SERIALLY and close each block on the -- prompt: immune to async room chatter interleaving into a batch. -- -- A hit alone is NOT proof. `look thing` may reach a different item that also -- answers to "thing". So the first hit — from the most specific candidate, -- the least likely to collide — becomes the ANCHOR, and every later hit is -- compared against it by line overlap. Same item -> ok. Different -> amb. inv.probe = nil inv.probeQueue = inv.probeQueue or {}
if C.probeAuto == nil then C.probeAuto = true end -- probe during iloot if C.probeRoom == nil then C.probeRoom = true end -- probe room items pre-get if C.probeQuiet == nil then C.probeQuiet = true end -- gag probe output if C.probeMax == nil then C.probeMax = 24 end -- candidates per run if C.probeRoomMax == nil then C.probeRoomMax = 10 end -- candidates when in-room -- `show id ground` is the parser's own handle oracle (9.19): one command yields -- the exact handle for every ground object, so it replaces the look-probe -- ladder for room items. The probe stays as a fallback for anything it misses. if C.useShowId == nil then C.useShowId = true end -- Corpses are never looted. When `show id ground` tags one (it answers to -- `corpse` whatever its display name), iloot digs the grave first -- which -- spills the contents onto the floor -- then re-loots the spill. if C.digCorpses == nil then C.digCorpses = true end -- Query `show id <item>` once per tracked room item (trash included) for the -- full alias set, so short-handle collisions can be separated by a longer name. if C.idFull == nil then C.idFull = true end
-- Lines that can drift into a capture from elsewhere (movement, autosave, -- channels). Dropped before fingerprinting. local PROBE_NOISE = { "^%s*$", "%d+/%d+HP", "^Autosave%.$", "^%[", "^%*", " walks ", " leaves ", " arrives", " enters ", " tells you", " shouts", "^You feel ", "^You are ", "^Beon ", } local function probeNoise(line) for _, p in ipairs(PROBE_NOISE) do if line:find(p) then return true end end return false end
-- Fraction of lines shared by two captures. Robust to a stray interleaved -- line in a way that an exact hash would not be. local function probeOverlap(a, b) if not a or not b or #a == 0 or #b == 0 then return 0 end local set = {} for _, l in ipairs(a) do set[l] = true end local hit = 0 for _, l in ipairs(b) do if set[l] then hit = hit + 1 end end return hit / math.max(#a, #b) end
function inv.probeBusy() return inv.probe ~= nil end
local function probeInCombat() local ok, st = pcall(function() return gmcp and gmcp.Char and gmcp.Char.Status and gmcp.Char.Status.state end) return ok and st == "combat" end
-- How should `look` be addressed to reach this item, and what can shadow it? -- Confirmed `look` behaviour: -- * `l <handle> in "<bag>"` scopes the search to one container -- * `l <handle> on ground` scopes the search to the room (index works too: -- `l <handle> 2 on ground`) -- * a bare `look` searches INVENTORY BEFORE THE GROUND -- Every probe is therefore addressed to exactly the place the item lives, so -- a description mismatch can only mean a genuine collision INSIDE that place. -- * loose/kept item -> bare look; inventory wins, so only another carried -- item can shadow it -- * bagged item -> `in "<bag>"`; only that bag's contents can shadow it -- * room item -> `on ground`; inventory can no longer mis-answer, so -- only another item on the floor can shadow it — and -- that is exactly the collision `get` would hit function inv.probeTarget(key) if inv.locCount("loose", key) > 0 or inv.locCount("keep", key) > 0 then return "", "inventory" end for _, c in ipairs(inv.containersWith(key)) do local meta = inv.contMeta[c] local sack = (meta and meta.name) or c return string.format(' in "%s"', sack), "container:"..c end if inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.lines then for _, it in ipairs(inv.roomScan.lines) do if inv.key(it.name) == key then return " on ground", "ground" end end end return "", "unknown" end
-- Given where we probed, what does a mismatched description mean was in the -- way? Each scope shadows only from within itself now that every probe is -- addressed explicitly. function inv.probeShadow(scope) if not scope then return "any" end if scope:find("^container:") then return scope end if scope == "inventory" or scope == "ground" then return scope end return "any" end
-- Begin a probe run for one type. -- opts = { max=, source=, onDone=, force= } function inv.probeStart(key, opts) opts = opts or {} if inv.probe then return false end if not key or key == "" then return false end local t = inv.types[key] local name = (t and t.name) or key if not t then return false end
local h = inv.handlesOf(key, true) local cands = {} -- opts.cands: test exactly these instead of the generated ladder. `ihandle` -- uses it to check ONE human-supplied string — the whole point of that -- command is that the ladder has already been exhausted. for _, c in ipairs(opts.cands or inv.handleLadder(key)) do -- commas and quotes are misparsed by the game's multi-target syntax if not c:find(",") and not c:find('"') and not (h.bad[c] and not opts.force) then cands[#cands+1] = c end end if #cands == 0 then return false end
local cap = opts.max or C.probeMax if #cands > cap then local kept = {} for i = 1, cap - 1 do kept[i] = cands[i] end kept[#kept+1] = cands[#cands] -- always keep the bare head noun cands = kept end
local suffix, scope = inv.probeTarget(key) inv.probe = { key = key, name = name, cands = cands, i = 0, anchor = nil, lines = {}, awaiting = false, miss = false, found = {}, tested = 0, mined = false, suffix = suffix, scope = scope, shadow = inv.probeShadow(scope), source = opts.source or "manual", onDone = opts.onDone, } inv.probeNext() return true end
function inv.probeNext() local p = inv.probe; if not p then return end p.i = p.i + 1 if p.i > #p.cands then return inv.probeFinish() end local cand = p.cands[p.i] p.lines, p.miss, p.awaiting = {}, false, true if p.timer then killTimer(p.timer); p.timer = nil end p.timer = tempTimer(8, function() if inv.probe == p and p.awaiting then inv.probeAbort("no reply") end end) send("l " .. cand .. (p.suffix or ""), false) end
-- Fed by the catch-all "Probe capture" trigger for every line while a probe -- is live. Returns true if it consumed the line. function inv.probeLine(line) local p = inv.probe; if not p then return false end if line:find("%d+/%d+HP") then -- prompt: already consumed by inv.onPrompt, just hide it if C.probeQuiet and deleteLine then deleteLine() end return true end if not p.awaiting then return false end if line == "This item is unidentified." then local t = inv.types[p.key] if t and not t.unidentified then t.unidentified = true; inv.save() end end if line == "Look at what?" then p.miss = true elseif not probeNoise(line) then p.lines[#p.lines+1] = line end if C.probeQuiet and deleteLine then deleteLine() end return true end
-- Called from inv.onPrompt: the response block for the current candidate is -- complete. Classify it, then fire the next candidate. function inv.probeBlockEnd() local p = inv.probe; if not (p and p.awaiting) then return end p.awaiting = false if p.timer then killTimer(p.timer); p.timer = nil end local cand = p.cands[p.i] p.tested = p.tested + 1
if p.miss or #p.lines == 0 then inv.handleRecordBad(p.key, cand) elseif not p.anchor then p.anchor = p.lines -- LOOK-proof only. `look` accepts strings `get` and `sacrifice` refuse, -- so this is a candidate for the ladder, not a handle to trust. inv.handleRecordOk(p.key, cand, inv.HANDLE_SRC_LOOK) p.found[#p.found+1] = cand inv.probeMine() elseif probeOverlap(p.anchor, p.lines) >= 0.8 then inv.handleRecordOk(p.key, cand, inv.HANDLE_SRC_LOOK) p.found[#p.found+1] = cand else inv.handleRecordAmb(p.key, cand, p.shadow) end inv.probeNext() end
-- The description itself advertises handles that the NAME never contains: -- "It most closely resembles a executioner's sword." and "It looks like some -- sort of slashing weapon." Both were confirmed in play. Mined once, from the -- anchor, and appended to the live candidate list. function inv.probeMine() local p = inv.probe; if not p or p.mined or not p.anchor then return end p.mined = true local extra = {} local function push(s) if not s then return end s = s:lower():gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", ""):gsub("^an?%s+", "") if s ~= "" then extra[#extra+1] = s end end for _, l in ipairs(p.anchor) do local r = l:match("^It most closely resembles (.+)%.$") if r then push(r) push(r:match("(%S+)$")) local t = inv.types[p.key] if t then t.resembles = r:gsub("^an?%s+", "") end -- 'help weapon types' names the type; the item is usually reachable as -- <material> <type> too ("steel executioner's sword", "steel sword"). -- The material comes from the name, which the resembles-line never -- repeats, so neither source produces this pair on its own. local g = inv.gearParts(p.key) if g and g.material then local bare = r:gsub("^an?%s+", "") push(g.material .. " " .. bare) local tailNoun = bare:match("(%S+)$") if tailNoun and tailNoun ~= bare then push(g.material .. " " .. tailNoun) end end end local w = l:match("^It looks like some sort of (.+)%.$") if w then push(w:match("(%S+)$")) -- "weapon" push(w) -- "piercing weapon" end -- The prose names the object generically even while it is unidentified: -- "This steel long dagger is definitely made by elven smiths..." gives -- both "steel long dagger" and the adjective "elven", and `elven long -- dagger` is the handle that actually works. local base = l:match("^This%s+(.-)%s+is%s") or l:match("^This%s+(.-)%s+has%s") if base and #base < 40 then local bw = {} for x in base:gmatch("%S+") do bw[#bw+1] = x end if #bw >= 1 and #bw <= 5 then for i = 1, #bw do push(table.concat(bw, " ", i)) end p.baseWords = bw end end local adj = l:match("made by (%a+)") or l:match("by (%a+) smiths") or l:match("of (%a+) make") if adj and p.baseWords then local bw = p.baseWords push(adj .. " " .. bw[#bw]) if #bw >= 2 then push(adj .. " " .. bw[#bw-1] .. " " .. bw[#bw]) end end end local h = inv.handlesOf(p.key, true) local have = {} for _, c in ipairs(p.cands) do have[c] = true end local added = 0 for _, e in ipairs(extra) do if not have[e] and not h.bad[e] and not e:find(",") and not e:find('"') then have[e] = true p.cands[#p.cands+1] = e added = added + 1 end end if added > 0 then inv.note(string.format("description suggests %d more handle(s) to test", added)) end end
function inv.probeFinish() local p = inv.probe; inv.probe = nil if not p then return end if p.timer then killTimer(p.timer); p.timer = nil end local h = inv.handlesOf(p.key, true) if #p.found > 0 then if h then h.probedAt = os.time() end cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[iprobe]<reset> <white>%s<reset>: <green>%d<reset> handle(s) — <cyan>%s<reset> <grey>(%d tested)<reset>\n", p.name, #p.found, table.concat(p.found, ", "), p.tested)) else -- Nothing was visible at all: the item is bagged, gone, or we are blind. -- Every "miss" we just recorded is untrustworthy, so roll them back -- rather than permanently blacklisting a whole ladder. if h then for _, c in ipairs(p.cands) do h.bad[c] = nil end end cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[iprobe]<reset> <white>%s<reset>: <yellow>not visible<reset> — nothing learned (needs to be loose or in the room).\n", p.name)) end inv.save() if p.onDone then local f = p.onDone; f() end end
function inv.probeAbort(why) local p = inv.probe; inv.probe = nil if not p then return end if p.timer then killTimer(p.timer); p.timer = nil end inv.warn("probe aborted ("..(why or "?")..") after "..p.tested.." test(s).") inv.save() if p.onDone then local f = p.onDone; f() end end
-- ---- Probe queue ------------------------------------------------------ function inv.probeEnqueue(key) if not key or key == "" then return end if inv.handleProbed(key) then return end for _, k in ipairs(inv.probeQueue) do if k == key then return end end inv.probeQueue[#inv.probeQueue+1] = key end
-- Drain the queue one type at a time, then call onDone (always exactly once). function inv.probeQueueRun(onDone, opts) opts = opts or {} local finished = false local function done() if finished then return end finished = true if onDone then onDone() end end local function step() if probeInCombat() then inv.warn("probing paused: in combat.") return done() end local key = table.remove(inv.probeQueue, 1) if not key then return done() end local started = inv.probeStart(key, { source = opts.source, max = opts.max, onDone = step, }) if not started then return step() end end step() end
-- ---- Stat helpers ----------------------------------------------------- function inv.ema(stat, x) if type(stat) ~= "table" or not tonumber(stat.avg) then return { avg = x, min = x, max = x, n = 1 } end stat.avg = inv.emaAlpha * x + (1 - inv.emaAlpha) * stat.avg stat.min = math.min(stat.min, x) stat.max = math.max(stat.max, x) stat.n = (stat.n or 0) + 1 return stat end function inv.blend(old, new) if not old then return new end return inv.emaAlpha * new + (1 - inv.emaAlpha) * old end
-- Two items can display the SAME name and be different objects — "Steel -- dagger <intense chartreuse glow>" and "Steel dagger <intense yellow glow>" -- came off the same corpse and are not the same dagger. The glow survives in -- every listing, so it is the one discriminator available without paying to -- identify. -- -- Handles stay shared (the parser matches the words, and both answer to the -- same ones); VALUES are kept per variant, because that is what actually -- differs. Storing them together produced "sell ~13641 range 2704-19308". function inv.glowTag(raw) local g = inv.parseGlow(raw) if not g then return nil end local parts = {} if g.intensity then parts[#parts+1] = g.intensity end if g.color then parts[#parts+1] = g.color end if #parts == 0 then return nil end return table.concat(parts, " ") end
-- The value record to read/write for this item, given the raw name it was -- seen under. Falls back to the type itself when there is no glow. function inv.variantOf(key, rawname, create) local t = inv.types[key] if not t then return nil end local g = rawname and inv.glowTag(rawname) or nil if not g then return t end if not t.variants then if not create then return t end t.variants = {} end if not t.variants[g] then if not create then return t.variants[g] or t end t.variants[g] = {} end return t.variants[g], g end
function inv.variantCount(key) local t = inv.types[key] if not (t and t.variants) then return 0 end local n = 0 for _ in pairs(t.variants) do n = n + 1 end return n end
function inv.getType(key, name) local t = inv.types[key] if not t then t = { name = inv.cleanName(name) or name }; inv.types[key] = t end if name then t.name = inv.cleanName(name) or t.name -- record glow attribute (collected as a candidate high-DF signal) local g = inv.parseGlow(name) if g then t.glow = g local tag = inv.glowTag(name) if tag then t.variants = t.variants or {} t.variants[tag] = t.variants[tag] or {} end end if inv.isHeart(key) then inv.heartSeed(key) end -- auto-tag well-known sac-only categories from name patterns if not t.sellCat then local n = (inv.cleanName(name) or ""):lower() if n:find("heart") and n:find("bloodstained") then t.sellCat = "food" end if n:find("%s*meat%s*") or n:find("waybread") or n:find("lard") or n:find("kidney") then t.sellCat = "food" end end end return t end
-- ---- Location map operations ----------------------------------------- -- Each container holds an ordered list of type-keys (index 1 = newest stowed). -- We track multiplicity by repeating the key, so counts fall out naturally.
local function listOf(container) inv.loc[container] = inv.loc[container] or {} return inv.loc[container] end
-- Add an instance of `key` to `container` as the NEWEST (front = index 1). function inv.locAdd(container, key) local l = listOf(container) table.insert(l, 1, key) end
-- Remove one instance of `key` from `container` at a given index (1-based among -- that key's instances). Returns true if removed.
