If idx is nil, removes the -- newest (index 1) of that key. function inv.locRemove(container, key, idx) local l = listOf(container) local seen = 0 for pos = 1, #l do if l[pos] == key then seen = seen + 1 if not idx or seen == idx then table.remove(l, pos) return true end end end return false end
-- Count instances of `key` in `container`. function inv.locCount(container, key) local n = 0 for _, k in ipairs(listOf(container)) do if k == key then n = n + 1 end end return n end
-- The per-container positional index of the (newest) instance of `key`: -- among instances of that key, 1 = newest. Returns the index to use in a -- command for the NEWEST one, or nil if absent. (Newest = lowest number, -- matching Icesus.) function inv.locIndexNewest(container, key) return inv.locCount(container, key) >= 1 and 1 or nil end
-- Move one instance of `key` from `src` to `dst` (front of dst). -- A failed source removal must NOT swallow the arrival. The game has just said -- "You get the X", so X is demonstrably in hand; if the map disagreed about -- where it came from, the map was already wrong and dropping the item on the -- floor of the model makes it worse. Everything that asks "where is this -- held?" then answers "nowhere" — which is how an unambiguous fetch (one -- item loose, its rivals not held at all) still came out ambiguous. function inv.locMove(src, dst, key, idx) if inv.locRemove(src, key, idx) then inv.locAdd(dst, key); return true end inv.locAdd(dst, key) return false end
-- List the containers (excluding loose/keep) an item key currently appears in. function inv.containersWith(key) local out = {} for cont, l in pairs(inv.loc) do if cont ~= "loose" and cont ~= "keep" then for _, k in ipairs(l) do if k == key then out[#out+1] = cont; break end end end end return out end
-- ---- Reference generation -------------------------------------------- -- Choose the handle to send for `key` with no container context. -- Proven handles win; the most specific proven handle is the safest to send -- blind, because specificity is what prevents collisions. function inv.bestHandle(key) local confirmed = inv.handleList(key) if confirmed[1] then return confirmed[1] end local h = inv.handlesOf(key) for _, cand in ipairs(inv.blindLadder(key)) do if not (h and (h.bad[cand] or h.amb[cand])) then return cand end end return inv.blindLadder(key)[1] or key end
-- Choose the handle to send for `key` inside `container`. Prefer the SHORTEST -- proven handle that is unambiguous among that container's contents; fall -- back to the most specific proven handle; fall back to the unprobed ladder. function inv.shortestHandle(container, key) local l = listOf(container) local ctx = inv.ambContext(container) local function uniqueIn(cand) local matchKeys = {} local pat = "%f[%a]"..cand:gsub("(%W)","%%%1").."%f[%A]" for _, k in ipairs(l) do if k == cand or k:find(pat) then matchKeys[k] = true end end local distinct = 0 for _ in pairs(matchKeys) do distinct = distinct + 1 end return distinct <= 1 end
local confirmed = inv.handleList(key) if #confirmed > 0 then -- Prefer the game's own show-id pick over any SHORTER generic alias: it is -- unambiguous in scope by construction, so it can't collide with a worn item -- that uniqueIn() (which only sees the location map) is blind to. local sid = inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].showIdHandle if sid and not inv.handleIsBad(key, sid) and not inv.ambBlocks(key, sid, ctx) and uniqueIn(sid) then for _, c in ipairs(confirmed) do if c == sid then return sid end end end for i = #confirmed, 1, -1 do -- shortest first local c = confirmed[i] -- ...but never a bare handle a WORN item also answers to (it would reach -- the worn item under an inventory-scoped verb); skip it while a more -- specific handle remains, which the loop keeps looking for. if not inv.ambBlocks(key, c, ctx) and uniqueIn(c) and not inv.wornClash(c) then return c end end return confirmed[1] -- most specific proven end
local h = inv.handlesOf(key) local best for _, cand in ipairs(inv.blindLadder(key)) do if not (h and h.bad[cand]) and not inv.ambBlocks(key, cand, ctx) then if not best then best = cand end if uniqueIn(cand) then return cand end end end return best or inv.blindLadder(key)[1] or key end
-- Build the command target for the NEWEST instance of `key` in `container`. -- loose: `<handle>` or `<handle> <idx>` if duplicates -- in sack: `<handle> from "<sack>"` or `<handle> <idx> from "<sack>"` -- Returns the target string, or nil + reason if not safely referenceable. function inv.refFor(container, key) if inv.locCount(container, key) < 1 then return nil, "not present" end local meta = inv.contMeta[container] if container ~= "loose" and container ~= "keep" and meta and meta.trusted == false then return nil, "container order not established (re-stow once)" end local handle = inv.shortestHandle(container, key) local dupCount = inv.locCount(container, key) local idxPart = (dupCount > 1) and (" 1") or "" -- newest = 1 if container == "loose" or container == "keep" then return handle .. idxPart else local sackName = (inv.contMeta[container] and inv.contMeta[container].name) or container return string.format('%s%s from "%s"', handle, idxPart, sackName) end end
-- A reference to ANY instance of `key` inside `container`. -- -- refFor() above is for operations where WHICH instance matters, so it -- refuses whenever a container's stow order is untrusted — and a scan that -- reconciles any count sets untrusted routinely. Appraising, selling and -- sacrificing do not care which of three identical breads they get, so going -- through refFor meant they silently got no reference at all, and `value` -- was then sent at an item still sitting in the bag ("You do not have ..."). -- No index is used here, so stow order is irrelevant. -- ---- Positional disambiguation ---------------------------------------- -- When two TYPES in one bag answer to the same handle, no string separates -- them and the shortest-unambiguous search has nothing left to offer: it -- returns the colliding handle anyway, and `get stone cap from "loot"` fetches -- whichever of the two caps the game reaches first — every time, so the other -- is never appraised at all. -- -- The remaining lever is the positional index. Two things make it usable: -- -- * the index counts items answering the HANDLE, in stow order, newest = 1. -- It is NOT an index among instances of one type, which is what refFor -- has always emitted — and that is why the case needing an index never -- got one: with one cap of each kind, each type's own count is 1. -- * inv.loc is already maintained in stow order (locAdd inserts at the -- front), so the position is a lookup, not a guess. -- -- Where it stays honest: the order desyncs silently (a hand-typed put, a -- corpse dump, an item destroyed) and no listing can restore it, because `i`, -- a container look and `i weight` are all alphabetical. So the index is treated as -- a FIRST GUESS, not as truth. The get echo names what actually arrived, and -- a mismatch walks to the next index instead of recording against the wrong -- item — see inv.onGetEcho. That converges in at most one try per rival even -- when the order is completely wrong.
-- An indexed fetch came back with the wrong type. The index is a claim about -- stow order, and the game has just refuted it, so reorder inv.loc to match -- what we observed: the type we actually got occupies the position we asked -- for. Doing this makes the NEXT attempt informed rather than another shot in -- the dark, and it repairs the order for every later reference to that bag — -- which is the only repair available, since every listing is alphabetical. function inv.noteIndexMiss(j) if not (j and j.container and j.key and j.heldKey and j.handle) then return end local c = j.container if c == "loose" or c == "keep" then return end local want = tonumber((j.ref or j.vref or ""):match("%s(%d+)$")) or 1 local list = inv.loc[c] if not list then return end -- find the position, in the FULL list, of the want-th handle answerer local seen, at = 0, nil for pos, k in ipairs(list) do if inv.keyAnswersTo(k, j.handle) then seen = seen + 1 if seen == want then at = pos; break end end end if not at then return end -- move the type we actually received into that slot for pos, k in ipairs(list) do if k == j.heldKey and pos ~= at then table.remove(list, pos) table.insert(list, math.min(at, #list + 1), j.heldKey) break end end local meta = inv.contMeta[c] if meta then meta.trusted = false end -- the order was wrong; say so inv.save() end
-- Does this type answer to this handle? Same three tests used elsewhere: -- a proven handle, a rung of its blind ladder, or the word appearing in its -- name. Over-counting and under-counting are equally harmful here, so all -- three sources are consulted rather than the cheapest one. function inv.keyAnswersTo(k, handle) if not (k and handle) then return false end local hs = inv.handlesOf(k) if hs and hs.ok[handle] then return true end for _, c in ipairs(inv.blindLadder(k)) do if c == handle then return true end end local pat = "%f[%a]"..handle:gsub("(%W)","%%%1").."%f[%A]" return k == handle or k:find(pat) ~= nil end
-- Every distinct type in `container` that answers to `handle`, in stow order. function inv.handleRivalsIn(container, handle) local out = {} for _, k in ipairs(inv.loc[container] or {}) do if inv.keyAnswersTo(k, handle) then out[#out+1] = k end end return out end
-- 1-based position of `key` among them, or nil. Positions count instances, -- not types: two breads ahead of the cap push the cap to 3. function inv.handleIndexIn(container, key, handle) local pos = 0 for _, k in ipairs(inv.loc[container] or {}) do if inv.keyAnswersTo(k, handle) then pos = pos + 1 if k == key then return pos end end end return nil end
-- How many positions this handle could refer to in that bag (the retry cap). function inv.handleRivalCount(container, handle) return #inv.handleRivalsIn(container, handle) end
-- Append a positional index when, and only when, the handle is shared. A -- lone match needs no index and adding one is a chance to be wrong for free. function inv.indexedHandle(container, key, handle) if not (container and key and handle) then return handle end if container == "loose" or container == "keep" then return handle end if inv.handleRivalCount(container, handle) <= 1 then return handle end local n = inv.handleIndexIn(container, key, handle) if not n or n < 1 then return handle end return (n > 1) and (handle .. " " .. n) or handle end
function inv.bagRef(container, key, wantIndex) if not container or container == "loose" or container == "keep" then -- container-aware here as well: two kinds of skin loose at once made -- `sell skin` reach the wrong one, and the reply was about an item we had -- not asked for. local h = inv.shortestHandle(container or "loose", key) h = inv.safeHandle(h, key, container or "loose", false) or h return h, h end if inv.locCount(container, key) < 1 then return nil end local meta = inv.contMeta[container] local sackName = (meta and meta.name) or container -- Container-aware: the shortest proven handle that is unambiguous among the -- OTHER types in this bag. `look` accepts long display forms that `get` and -- `sacrifice` reject, so preferring the longest proven handle sends the -- least likely one to work. local h = inv.shortestHandle(container, key) h = inv.safeHandle(h, key, container, false) or h if not h or h == "" then return nil end -- `wantIndex` is opt-in, and today only the shop's fetch asks for it. `get` -- is the one verb whose reply names the object it moved, so an index sent -- there is checked; `sell` and `sacrifice` would be sending an unverified -- guess, and their echoes are short forms that cannot confirm it. The -- second return stays the BARE handle: `put` has no positional form at all, -- and shopPutBack builds its command from it. local ref = wantIndex and inv.indexedHandle(container, key, h) or h return string.format('%s from "%s"', ref, sackName), h, ref end
-- ---- Identification ---------------------------------------------------- -- An unidentified item wears a generic name. "Steel dagger" turned out to be -- BOTH "Steel elven long dagger with red runes" and "...with blue runes" — -- one display name standing for several real items, each with its own value. -- -- Identification renames the object in place. Keyed on the display name, that -- orphans everything already learned about it: weight, volume, and above all -- the proven handles. But it is the same object, so those facts transfer. inv.identifyPending = nil
-- Which loose type does this handle name? Prefer one we know is unidentified. function inv.resolveLooseHandle(handle) if not handle or handle == "" then return nil end local h = handle:lower() local hit, unid local seen = {} for _, key in ipairs(inv.loc.loose or {}) do if not seen[key] then seen[key] = true local match = false local hs = inv.handlesOf(key) if hs and hs.ok[h] then match = true end if not match then for _, c in ipairs(inv.blindLadder(key)) do if c == h then match = true; break end end end if not match and (" "..key.." "):find("%f[%a]"..h:gsub("(%W)","%%%1").."%f[%A]") then match = true end if match then hit = hit or key if inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].unidentified then unid = unid or key end end end end return unid or hit end
-- "You give dagger and 550 silver to Driixtr." function inv.noteIdentifyGive(handle) inv.identifyPending = inv.resolveLooseHandle(handle) end
-- "Driixtr tells you: This item is <TrueName>." function inv.noteIdentified(trueRaw) local pend = inv.identifyPending; inv.identifyPending = nil local trueKey = inv.key(trueRaw) if not trueKey then return end local t2 = inv.getType(trueKey, inv.cleanName(trueRaw) or trueRaw) if not t2 then return end t2.identified = true
if not pend or pend == trueKey then return end local t1 = inv.types[pend] if not t1 then return end t1.unidentified = true
-- the same physical object, so the physical facts are shared t2.weight = t2.weight or t1.weight t2.volume = t2.volume or t1.volume t2.weightN = t2.weightN or t1.weightN t2.volumeN = t2.volumeN or t1.volumeN
-- Proven handles transfer BOTH ways. The parser matched the object, not the -- label, so a handle found after identifying is worth trying on the next -- unidentified one — which is the whole point of recording this. local h1 = inv.handlesOf(pend, true) local h2 = inv.handlesOf(trueKey, true) for str, n in pairs(h1.ok) do h2.ok[str] = math.max(h2.ok[str] or 0, n) end for str, n in pairs(h2.ok) do h1.ok[str] = math.max(h1.ok[str] or 0, n) end
-- and the provenance if t1.origins then t2.origins = t2.origins or {} for mob, n in pairs(t1.origins) do t2.origins[mob] = (t2.origins[mob] or 0) + n end end
t1.identifiesAs = t1.identifiesAs or {} t1.identifiesAs[trueKey] = (t1.identifiesAs[trueKey] or 0) + 1 t2.unidentifiedAs = pend
-- One generic name can hide several real items ("Steel dagger" is both the -- red-runed and the blue-runed elven dagger). They are different items with -- different values, but the parser matches them all by the same words, so -- pool the proven handles across the whole family. inv.mergeFamilyHandles(pend)
-- the instance we handed over is now the identified type inv.locRemove("loose", pend, 1) inv.locAdd("loose", trueKey) inv.save() inv.warn(string.format("'%s' identified as '%s' — handles and measurements carried over.", t1.name or pend, t2.name or trueKey)) end
-- Union the proven handles of an unidentified type and every identified item -- it has been seen to become. function inv.mergeFamilyHandles(unidKey) local t1 = inv.types[unidKey] if not (t1 and t1.identifiesAs) then return end local pool = {} local hs = inv.handlesOf(unidKey, true) for str, n in pairs(hs.ok) do pool[str] = math.max(pool[str] or 0, n) end for k2 in pairs(t1.identifiesAs) do if inv.types[k2] then local h2 = inv.handlesOf(k2, true) for str, n in pairs(h2.ok) do pool[str] = math.max(pool[str] or 0, n) end end end for str, n in pairs(pool) do if not hs.bad[str] then hs.ok[str] = math.max(hs.ok[str] or 0, n) end end for k2 in pairs(t1.identifiesAs) do if inv.types[k2] then local h2 = inv.handlesOf(k2, true) for str, n in pairs(pool) do if not h2.bad[str] then h2.ok[str] = math.max(h2.ok[str] or 0, n) end end end end inv.save() end
-- ---- Scan parsing: i, i weight, look in sack ------------------------- -- Scans are alphabetical: authoritative for membership/counts, NOT order. -- We use them to (a) learn weight/volume from `i weight`, (b) set keep flags, -- (c) validate live-tracked counts and flag disagreements.
inv.scan = nil -- active scan accumulator
-- Begin a scan. kind = "i" | "iweight" | "sack". For sacks, pass sackKey. function inv.scanStart(kind, sackKey) inv.scan = { kind = kind, sack = sackKey, inKeep = false, counts = {}, order = {}, weights = {} } end
function inv.scanKeepMark() if inv.scan then inv.scan.inKeep = true end end
-- Feed one item line during a scan. For i weight, mass/vol are stack totals. -- Coins/money are auto-managed by the game and must never be tracked as -- inventory items (they appear in i/i-weight listings and get/drop lines). function inv.isMoney(name) if not name then return false end local n = name:lower() return n:match("coins?$") ~= nil or n:match("pile of %a+ coins") ~= nil or n:match("%a+ coins?$") ~= nil or n:match("^%d+ %a+ coins?$") ~= nil end
function inv.scanItem(rawname, qty, massKg, volL) if not inv.scan then return end -- defensive: never capture a prompt or status line as an item if rawname:find("%d+/%d+HP") or rawname:find("Skill:") then return end local key = inv.key(rawname) if not key then return end qty = qty or 1 -- A coin line carries its own count, so it measures the denomination's -- density directly — the only place that figure is ever visible. inv.coinLearnVol(key, volL) local t = inv.getType(key, rawname) t.seen = true -- appeared in a real listing, so it genuinely exists t.keep = inv.scan.inKeep -- learn weight/volume (per item) from i weight -- -- `i weight` prints one decimal, so anything under 0.05 displays as 0.0 — -- and a stored volume of zero is indistinguishable from no volume at all: -- classify's `t.volume > 0` test rejects both, so the type is "unknown" -- forever however valuable it is. A Bloodstone appraised at 22,973 silver -- sat in "loot" doing exactly that, re-appraised on every ishop run and -- never routed. Read 0.0 as "below the display resolution" and record the -- top of that range (0.05), which is the CONSERVATIVE choice: the largest -- possible volume gives the smallest possible value-per-litre, so anything -- that still clears the cutoff on this figure genuinely clears it. local SUBRES = 50 -- grams / millilitres: half of the 0.1 display quantum if massKg then local perW = (massKg * 1000) / qty if perW <= 0 then perW = SUBRES end t.weight = inv.blend(t.weight, perW); t.weightN = (t.weightN or 0) + 1 end if volL then local perV = (volL * 1000) / qty if perV <= 0 then perV = SUBRES t.volumeApprox = true -- an upper bound, not a measurement else t.volumeApprox = nil end t.volume = inv.blend(t.volume, perV); t.volumeN = (t.volumeN or 0) + 1 end -- tally counts for this scan local bucket = inv.scan.inKeep and "keep" or (inv.scan.sack or "loose") inv.scan.counts[bucket] = inv.scan.counts[bucket] or {} inv.scan.counts[bucket][key] = (inv.scan.counts[bucket][key] or 0) + qty end
-- Finish a scan: reconcile counts against the live location map. function inv.scanEnd() local sc = inv.scan; inv.scan = nil if not sc then return end
-- A SIZING scan (see inv.shopSizeIfNeeded) is fired mid-run purely to -- capture mass and bulk, which scanItem has already recorded by the time we -- get here. Its COUNTS must not be applied: the listing was generated -- before the put that follows it and before the next item's get, so -- reconciling it against a map that has moved on would prune entries that -- are simply in flight. Take the measurements, drop the census. if sc.sizing then return end
-- Which buckets did this scan actually enumerate? -- sack look -> just that sack -- i / iweight -> loose + keep (top level), NOT sack interiors local covered = {} if sc.kind == "sack" then -- A container scan we cannot attribute is WORSE than useless: scanItem -- files unattributed rows under "loose", so applying it would import the -- bag's contents into your inventory map and prune everything really -- loose against them. Drop it and say so. if not sc.sack then inv.warn("scanned a container but I don't know which one — the look wasn't captured, " .."so nothing was applied. Let ishop/isac scan for you.") return end -- A key carrying a quote or a look verb is a parse failure, not a bag -- name. Applying it invents a container nothing else ever reads. if inv.isCorpseText(sc.sack) then -- a corpse is emptied, not kept: note what it held, track nothing inv.note(string.format("corpse of %s: %d type(s) seen", inv.lastMob or "?", (function() local n = 0 for _ in pairs(sc.counts[sc.sack] or {}) do n = n + 1 end; return n end)())) for k in pairs(sc.counts[sc.sack] or {}) do inv.noteOrigin(k) end return end if sc.sack:find('"') or sc.sack:find("^l%s") or sc.sack:find("^look%s") then inv.warn(string.format( "container key '%s' looks like a command, not a bag name — scan discarded.", sc.sack)) return end covered[sc.sack] = true -- mark disposal sacks as scanned (contents verified) after a look-in if inv.config.disposalSacks[sc.sack] then inv.scannedSacks[sc.sack] = true end else covered["loose"] = true covered["keep"] = true end
for bucket, keys in pairs(sc.counts) do for key, n in pairs(keys) do local live = inv.locCount(bucket, key) if live ~= n then local firstSight = (live == 0) -- discovering items we'd never tracked inv.reconcileCount(bucket, key, n) if bucket ~= "loose" and bucket ~= "keep" then inv.contMeta[bucket] = inv.contMeta[bucket] or { name = bucket } inv.contMeta[bucket].trusted = false end -- Only warn on a genuine DISAGREEMENT (we thought we knew the count and -- were wrong). First-sight discovery is normal and silent. if inv.config.verbose and not firstSight then inv.warn(string.format("'%s' in %s: tracked %d, scan shows %d — re-synced; order needs a re-stow.", inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name or key, bucket, live, n)) end end end end
-- Items we think are present but a scan that COVERS their bucket didn't list -- => they were removed. Never touch buckets the scan didn't cover. for bucket, l in pairs(inv.loc) do if covered[bucket] then local seen = {} for _, key in ipairs(l) do seen[key] = (seen[key] or 0) + 1 end for key, had in pairs(seen) do local scanned = (sc.counts[bucket] or {})[key] or 0 if scanned == 0 then inv.reconcileCount(bucket, key, 0) if inv.config.verbose then inv.warn(string.format("'%s' no longer in %s (was tracking %d) — removed.", inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name or key, bucket, had)) end end end end end
-- Always report what a container scan concluded. Silence here is how a map -- that disagrees with the bag went unnoticed for a whole session. if sc.kind == "sack" and sc.sack then local types, items = 0, 0 local seenK = {} for _, k in ipairs(inv.loc[sc.sack] or {}) do items = items + 1 if not seenK[k] then seenK[k] = true; types = types + 1 end end cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[inv]<reset> \"%s\": %d type(s), %d item(s) now tracked.\n", sc.sack, types, items)) end
-- release a loose refresh that ensureFresh is waiting on if sc.kind ~= "sack" and inv.looseScanWaiting then inv.looseScanWaiting = false if inv.looseScanTimer then killTimer(inv.looseScanTimer); inv.looseScanTimer = nil end local f = inv.looseScanDone; inv.looseScanDone = nil if f then return f() end end
-- release a scan that ensureSacksScanned is waiting on if sc.sack and inv.sackScanWaiting == sc.sack then inv.sackScanWaiting = nil local f = inv.sackScanDone; inv.sackScanDone = nil if f then f() end end end
-- Force a container's instance-count of `key` to exactly n (append/trim). function inv.reconcileCount(container, key, n) local cur = inv.locCount(container, key) if cur < n then for _ = 1, n - cur do inv.locAdd(container, key) end elseif cur > n then for _ = 1, cur - n do inv.locRemove(container, key) end end end
-- ---- Live movement events -------------------------------------------- -- Parse the container out of an action line and update the location map. -- "You get the X." -> loose gains X (from world) -- "You get the X from a <sack>." -> sack -> loose -- "You get the X to a <sack>." -> world -> sack -- "You put the X into a <sack>." -> loose -> sack -- "You drop the X." -> loose loses X -- "You drop the X from a <sack>." -> sack loses X -- sackName arrives as a display string; map to its key. function inv.sackKeyFromText(txt) if not txt then return nil end -- a sack reference like 'huge leather sack named "looties"' or 'looties' local named = txt:match('named%s+"([^"]+)"') or txt:match("named%s+'([^']+)'") if named then return named:lower() end return inv.key(txt) end
-- The in-game name to put in a command like `sell all from "<name>"`. For the -- standard disposal sacks the container key IS the name ("loot", "treasure"); -- a learned container carries its real name in contMeta. function inv.sackName(container) if not container or container == "loose" or container == "keep" then return container end local meta = inv.contMeta[container] return (meta and meta.name) or container end
function inv.evGet(itemRaw, fromSack, toSack) local key = inv.key(itemRaw); if not key then return end if fromSack then inv.locMove(inv.sackKeyFromText(fromSack), "loose", key) elseif toSack then local sackKey = inv.sackKeyFromText(toSack) -- echo loses sack name ("a huge leather sack") — use pending queue if not inv.contMeta[sackKey] then for i, p in ipairs(inv.pendingPuts) do if p.key == key then sackKey = p.sackKey; table.remove(inv.pendingPuts, i); break end end end inv.locAdd(sackKey, key) else inv.locAdd("loose", key) end end -- Queue of (key, sackKey) pairs for puts the system issued but whose echo -- won't carry the sack name. Consumed FIFO in evPut. inv.pendingPuts = inv.pendingPuts or {}
function inv.evPut(itemRaw, toSack) local key = inv.key(itemRaw); if not key then return end inv.lootNotePut(key) local descKey = inv.sackKeyFromText(toSack) local sackKey = inv.resolveSackText(toSack) -- If the echo lost the sack name (e.g. "a huge leather sack"), use the -- first pending put whose key matches, and remember the description. if sackKey and not inv.contMeta[sackKey] then for i, p in ipairs(inv.pendingPuts) do if p.key == key then sackKey = p.sackKey table.remove(inv.pendingPuts, i) if descKey and descKey ~= sackKey then inv.contDesc[descKey] = sackKey end break end end end if sackKey and inv.isDescriptionKey(sackKey) then inv.locRemove("loose", key, 1) inv.markBagsDirty(descKey) if inv.moveInFlight then inv.moveOnPut(key) end return end if sackKey then inv.locMove("loose", sackKey, key) end if inv.moveInFlight then inv.moveOnPut(key) end end -- Handle both single and multi-item drops: -- "You drop the X." -- "You drop the X, the Y and the Z from a huge leather sack." function inv.evDropBatch(line) local fromSack = line:match(" from a (.+)%.$") local sackKey = fromSack and inv.sackKeyFromText(fromSack) or nil -- strip the "You drop " prefix and trailing period local body = line:match("^You drop (.+)%.$") or "" -- strip " from a <sack>" suffix body = body:gsub(" from a .+$","") for _, it in ipairs(inv.splitItemList(body)) do local key = inv.key(it.name) if key then -- If sackKey is a known named container, remove from there. -- Otherwise (echo lost the name), search all containers for the key. local removed = false if sackKey and inv.contMeta[sackKey] then inv.locRemove(sackKey, key); removed = true end if not removed then -- find it in any container for cont, _ in pairs(inv.loc) do if inv.locCount(cont, key) > 0 then inv.locRemove(cont, key); break end end end end end end
function inv.evDrop(itemRaw, fromSack) local key = inv.key(itemRaw); if not key then return end if fromSack then inv.locRemove(inv.sackKeyFromText(fromSack), key) else inv.locRemove("loose", key) end end
-- ---- Value (sell / appraise) ----------------------------------------- -- Resolve a fragment the game echoed (e.g. "carrion crawler skin") to a known -- full type key: prefer exact, else the type whose name ends with / contains -- the fragment, most-recently-seen winning. -- Resolve a fragment the game echoed (e.g. "stone") to a known type key. -- A bare fragment can match several types, so we DISAMBIGUATE BY CONTEXT: -- prefer a type the player is currently holding (loose first, then any sack), -- since value/sell/sacrifice act on held items. If still tied among held -- items, it's genuinely ambiguous -> return nil + the candidates, and the -- caller warns instead of guessing (guessing corrupts value data). function inv.resolveFragment(fragment) -- clean the fragment first (strips glow tags, named clauses, etc.) local cleaned = inv.cleanName(fragment) or fragment local key = inv.key(cleaned) if inv.types[key] then return key end -- Articles are not identifying words, and leaving them in breaks the match -- on the article alone: "You retrieve a clod of snake lard" against a stored -- "Clod of raw snake lard" failed because the type's name has no "a" in it. -- Same flaw nameFits had against the shop's "…for the boots". local ARTICLE = { a=true, an=true, the=true, some=true } local function words(s) s = s:lower():gsub("'s%f[%A]",""):gsub("[^%a%s]"," ") local w = {} for tok in s:gmatch("%a+") do if not ARTICLE[tok] then w[#w+1] = tok end end return w end local fw = words(cleaned) if #fw == 0 then return nil end -- get the head noun via handleCandidates (handles clause-trimming, compound nouns) local fkey = inv.key(cleaned) local fcands = inv.handleCandidates(fkey) local fheadNoun = fcands[#fcands] or fw[#fw] -- bare noun from ladder
-- All types whose words contain every fragment word and share the head noun. -- Also match if the stored type name is a SUBSET of the fragment (room -- descriptions are often shorter than the game's canonical item name). local matches = {} local fwset = {}; for _,w in ipairs(fw) do fwset[w]=true end for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do local kw = words(t.name or k) local kwset = {}; for _,w in ipairs(kw) do kwset[w]=true end -- get type's head noun via its own handleCandidates local tcands = inv.handleCandidates(k) local theadNoun = tcands[#tcands] or kw[#kw] -- forward match: all fragment words in type name, same head noun local allFwIn = true for _,w in ipairs(fw) do if not kwset[w] then allFwIn=false; break end end -- reverse match: all type words in fragment (room name is subset of full name) local allKwIn = true for _,w in ipairs(kw) do if not fwset[w] then allKwIn=false; break end end local sameNoun = (theadNoun == fheadNoun) if (sameNoun and allFwIn) or (sameNoun and allKwIn) then matches[#matches+1] = { k=k, d=math.abs(#kw-#fw) } end end if #matches == 0 then return nil end if #matches == 1 then return matches[1].k end
-- Ambiguous: rank by where the item is held. Loose=3, in a sack=2, not -- held=0. The held score is the ONLY decider — word-count closeness is not -- a principled tiebreak and silently guessing corrupts data. If the top two -- share the same held score, it's genuinely ambiguous. local function heldScore(k) if inv.locCount("loose", k) > 0 then return 3 end if #inv.containersWith(k) > 0 then return 2 end return 0 end table.sort(matches, function(a,b) return heldScore(a.k) > heldScore(b.k) end) local top, second = matches[1], matches[2] if heldScore(top.k) > heldScore(second.k) then return top.k end return nil, matches -- equally-held (or both unheld): ambiguous end
-- Does this short name plausibly describe that type? ("Spider skin" vs -- "piece of spider's skin": every word of the name appears in the key.) local ARTICLE = { the = true, a = true, an = true, some = true } function inv.nameFits(nameRaw, key) if not (nameRaw and key) then return false end local hay = " " .. key .. " " for w in nameRaw:lower():gmatch("[%a]+") do -- "the" is three letters, so the length guard let it through and every -- comparison against a shop's "…for the boots" failed on the article -- alone. if #w > 2 and not ARTICLE[w] and not hay:find(w, 1, true) then return false end end return true end
function inv.onValueRaw(itemRaw, silver) -- The shop quotes its own SHORT form ("...for the boots"), which resolves -- against the type list only by luck: three tracked types end in "boots". -- But we are not guessing — a `value` during ishop follows a `get` whose -- echo named the item in full, and inv.shopJob.heldKey records exactly what -- came out of the bag. That is the strongest evidence available and it beats -- fragment matching outright. Note heldKey, NOT j.key: if the handle -- collided, the thing in hand is not the thing we asked for, and recording -- the price against what we MEANT to fetch would be the corrupting answer. -- The quoted name is NOT required to match. Andolal priced an "aluminium -- chain mail byrnie" at 48,691 and called it "the bracers" — the shop's -- short form need not share a single word with the item's display name, and -- insisting on one threw away the most valuable appraisal of the run. We -- know what we are holding because we watched it come out of the bag; the -- quote line adds nothing to that and cannot overrule it. local j = inv.shopJob local held = j and j.heldKey if held and inv.types[held] then if not inv.nameFits(itemRaw, held) then inv.note(string.format("the shop calls %s '%s' — noted, price recorded anyway.", inv.types[held].name or held, tostring(itemRaw))) end local t = inv.getType(held, inv.types[held].name or itemRaw) t.sell = inv.ema(t.sell, tonumber(silver) or 0) inv.shopNoteDeal(held, silver) inv.note(string.format("sell %s: ~%.0f silver (n=%d, %d-%d)", t.name, t.sell.avg, t.sell.n, t.sell.min, t.sell.max)) return end
local key, amb = inv.resolveFragment(itemRaw) if not key then if amb then local names = {} for _, m in ipairs(amb) do names[#names+1] = inv.types[m.k] and inv.types[m.k].name or m.k end inv.warn(string.format("'%s' is ambiguous (%s) — value not recorded. Use a more specific handle.", itemRaw, table.concat(names, " / "))) elseif inv.types[inv.key(itemRaw)] then key = inv.key(itemRaw) else -- The quote line carries the shop's SHORT form ("...for the skin"), not -- the item's name. Creating a type from it filled the database with -- handle-shaped ghosts — "symbol", "platinum dagger" — that no listing -- ever matches. Only accept an unknown name when it looks like a real -- display name: several words, and not merely one of our own handles. local k = inv.key(itemRaw) local words = 0 for _ in (k or ""):gmatch("%S+") do words = words + 1 end if k and words >= 3 then key = k else inv.note(string.format("'%s' is the shop's short form for something untracked — " .."value not recorded.", tostring(itemRaw))) return end end if not key then return end end local t = inv.getType(key, inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name or itemRaw) t.sell = inv.ema(t.sell, tonumber(silver) or 0) local v = inv.variantOf(key, itemRaw, true) if v and v ~= t then v.sell = inv.ema(v.sell, tonumber(silver) or 0) end inv.shopNoteDeal(key, silver) inv.note(string.format("sell %s: ~%.0f silver (n=%d, %d-%d)", t.name, t.sell.avg, t.sell.n, t.sell.min, t.sell.max)) end
-- A real sale also removes the instance. We remove the newest matching one, -- preferring loose, else any disposal sack it was sold from. function inv.onSoldRaw(itemRaw, silver, fromSack) -- Sales echo the FULL canonical name, so resolution is reliable here. -- If we matched a stored short name to the full name, update the stored name. -- Raw form deliberately: a sale must not advance the appraisal queue. inv.onValueRaw(itemRaw, silver) local key, amb = inv.resolveFragment(itemRaw) if not key then key = inv.key(itemRaw) end if not key then return end -- update stored name to the canonical full name from the sale local t = inv.types[key] if t and t.name then local fullClean = inv.cleanName(itemRaw) if fullClean and #fullClean > #(t.name) then t.name = fullClean end end if fromSack then inv.locRemove(inv.sackKeyFromText(fromSack), key) elseif inv.locCount("loose", key) > 0 then inv.locRemove("loose", key) else local cs = inv.containersWith(key) if cs[1] then inv.locRemove(cs[1], key) end end end
-- ---- Sacrifice parsing (favour from text; per-item only for singles) -- -- ---- Sacrifice pipeline ---------------------------------------------- -- The altar echoes its OWN short form of the item ("sacrifice dagger on the -- altar") whatever handle we sent, and dozens of types can share that form. -- Parsing the echo to decide what we had just sacrificed meant a favour -- reading was silently discarded whenever the short form was ambiguous — and -- a learning sacrifice is irreversible, so that data never came back. -- -- Icesus answers commands chronologically with exactly one outcome each, so -- identity comes from POSITION instead: send one sacrifice, attribute its -- outcome to the entry we sent, then send the next. Outcomes are: -- "You perform a quiet ritual in order to sacrifice X on the altar." -- followed by "... you gained N divine favour(s)." -> record N -- "There was nothing to sacrifice." -> the instance we -- thought was there is not; prune it from the map (free correction). -- One command can produce SEVERAL outcome lines ("You cannot sacrifice items -- from your keeplist." is immediately followed by "You have nothing to -- sacrifice."; a vendor's refusal also carries a price, matching both the -- quote and the rejection pattern). Every one of those lines fires its -- trigger synchronously, so advancing the queue inline sent the next command -- once per line and desynchronised replies from requests. -- -- Deferring the send by one event-loop pass fixes it: the first outcome -- clears the in-flight entry, every later line on the same reply finds -- nothing in flight and does nothing, and the next command goes out after -- the line is fully processed. function inv.deferStep(fn) if tempTimer then tempTimer(0, fn) else fn() end end
inv.sacQueue = inv.sacQueue or {} inv.sacInFlight = nil inv.sacMisses = 0 inv.sacStats = nil inv.sacTimer = nil
if C.sacMaxMiss == nil then C.sacMaxMiss = 3 end
function inv.sacReset() inv.sacQueue, inv.sacInFlight, inv.sacMisses = {}, nil, 0 if inv.sacTimer then killTimer(inv.sacTimer); inv.sacTimer = nil end end
function inv.sacEnqueue(e) inv.sacQueue[#inv.sacQueue+1] = e end function inv.sacBusy() return inv.sacInFlight ~= nil or #inv.sacQueue > 0 end
function inv.sacSendNext() if inv.sacTimer then killTimer(inv.sacTimer); inv.sacTimer = nil end local e = table.remove(inv.sacQueue, 1) if not e then return inv.sacFinish() end inv.sacInFlight = e local cmd = "sacrifice " .. e.ref cecho("\n" .. (e.learning and "<grey>[isac]<reset> <yellow>(learning)<reset> <cyan>" or "<grey>[isac]<reset> <cyan>") .. cmd .. "<reset>") send(cmd, false) inv.sacTimer = tempTimer(8, function() if inv.sacInFlight == e then inv.warn(string.format("no reply sacrificing '%s' — skipping it.", tostring(e.handle))) inv.sacInFlight = nil inv.sacMisses = (inv.sacMisses or 0) + 1 if inv.sacMisses >= (inv.config.sacMaxMiss or 3) then inv.sacReset(); return inv.sacFinish() end inv.sacSendNext() end end) end
-- "You perform a quiet ritual in order to sacrifice <short> on the altar." -- The short form cannot tell us WHICH type was consumed (many share it), but -- it can prove we hit the wrong one: if it contains a word that appears -- nowhere in the queued type's name or proven handles, the handle reached -- something else and the favour reading must not be attributed. function inv.sacRitual(short) -- Bulk sacrifice: this line names every item at once and the outcome is read -- off the single favour line instead. Nothing per-item to record. if inv.sacBulk then return end local e = inv.sacInFlight if not e then return end e.hit = true inv.clearStuck(e.key) -- the altar took it, so the handle works inv.sacMisses = 0 if not short then return end short = short:gsub("%s+on the.*$", ""):gsub("%s+$", ""):lower() if short ~= "" then e.echo = short end end
local SAC_STOPWORDS = { a = true, an = true, the = true, of = true, on = true, ["and"] = true, with = true, made = true, out = true, from = true, some = true, }
-- The altar's short form NAMES THE MOB: "sacrifice heart of guard dog on the -- altar". That is a discriminator, not just a veto — when it resolves to one -- tracked type, that type is what was consumed, whatever the queue thought it -- was asking for. Position is the weaker evidence here and loses. -- -- Returns key, or nil plus a reason: -- "unknown" nothing tracked answers to it -> fall back to the queued type -- "ambiguous" two or more types IN THIS BAG answer to it -> record nothing. -- This is the case that quietly poisoned the data: the reply -- line wraps ("...sacrifice heart of guard dog on the\naltar."), -- so the captured short form can come through as bare "heart", -- which fits every heart in the bag. Crediting the queued type -- anyway is how one heart ended up averaging 81 favour on other -- hearts' readings. function inv.resolveSacEcho(echo, container) if not echo or echo == "" then return nil, "unknown" end local words = {} for w in echo:gmatch("[%a']+") do w = w:lower():gsub("'s$", "") if w ~= "" and not SAC_STOPWORDS[w] then words[#words+1] = w end end if #words == 0 then return nil, "unknown" end
local hits = {} for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do local hay = " " .. k .. " " .. ((t.name or ""):lower()) .. " " local all = true for _, w in ipairs(words) do if not hay:find("%f[%a]" .. w:gsub("(%W)", "%%%1") .. "%f[%A]") then all = false; break end end if all then hits[#hits+1] = k end end if #hits == 0 then return nil, "unknown" end if #hits == 1 then return hits[1] end
-- Several types answer to the short form. Only the ones actually present -- where we took from could have been consumed. local here = {} for _, k in ipairs(hits) do if (container and inv.locCount(container, k) > 0) or inv.locCount("loose", k) > 0 then here[#here+1] = k end end if #here == 1 then return here[1] end if #here == 0 then return nil, "unknown" end return nil, "ambiguous", here end
-- Does every meaningful word of the altar's short form appear in this type? -- Returns false plus the offending word when it does not. function inv.sacEchoMatches(key, echo) local hay = " " .. (key or "") .. " " local h = inv.handlesOf(key) if h then for str in pairs(h.ok) do hay = hay .. str .. " " end end hay = hay:lower() for w in echo:gmatch("[%a']+") do if not SAC_STOPWORDS[w] then if not hay:find("%f[%a]" .. w:gsub("(%W)", "%%%1") .. "%f[%A]") then return false, w end end end return true end
-- "The god ... You feel like you gained N divine favour(s)." (may line-wrap) function inv.onSacFavour(n) n = tonumber(n) -- Bulk sacrifice completion: one lump favour for the whole stage bag. if inv.sacBulk then return inv.onSacBulkFinish(n) end local e = inv.sacInFlight; inv.sacInFlight = nil if not e then return end -- a hand-typed sacrifice we never queued -- veto: the altar named something this type cannot be. Skipped when the -- echo positively resolves to a tracked type — then it is not a misfire to -- discard, it is a correction to apply (see below). local preResolved = e.echo and inv.resolveSacEcho(e.echo, e.container) or nil if n and e.echo and not preResolved and not inv.sacEchoMatches(e.key, e.echo) then local _, bad = inv.sacEchoMatches(e.key, e.echo) local handle = e.ref and (e.ref:match('^(.-)%s+from%s+"') or e.ref) or nil inv.warn(string.format( "'%s' sacrificed '%s' instead of %s (no '%s' in it) — %d favour NOT recorded.", tostring(handle), e.echo, (inv.types[e.key] and inv.types[e.key].name) or e.key, tostring(bad), n)) if handle then inv.handleRecordAmb(e.key, handle, (e.container and e.container ~= "loose") and ("container:"..e.container) or "inventory") end if inv.sacStats then inv.sacStats.misfired = (inv.sacStats.misfired or 0) + 1 end if e.container then inv.locRemove(e.container, e.key, 1) end inv.save() return inv.deferStep(inv.sacSendNext) end local credited = e.key if n then if e.tried then -- A retry worked, so the item was there all along and every handle that -- reached nothing genuinely does not name it. `look` accepting one of -- them is not evidence enough to keep it. for bad in pairs(e.tried) do if bad ~= e.handle then inv.handleRecordBad(e.key, bad) end end if e.handle then inv.handleRecordOk(e.key, e.handle) end end
-- Believe the altar over the queue: it names what it took. local resolved, why, rival = inv.resolveSacEcho(e.echo, e.container) if why == "ambiguous" then local names = {} for _, k in ipairs(rival or {}) do names[#names+1] = (inv.types[k] and inv.types[k].name) or k end inv.warn(string.format( "the altar said '%s', which fits %d things you are carrying (%s) — " .."%d favour NOT recorded rather than credited to a guess.", tostring(e.echo), #names, table.concat(names, " / "), n)) if inv.sacStats then inv.sacStats.pooled = (inv.sacStats.pooled or 0) + 1 end n = nil elseif resolved and resolved ~= e.key then inv.note(string.format("altar took %s, not %s — favour credited where it belongs.", (inv.types[resolved] and inv.types[resolved].name) or resolved, (inv.types[e.key] and inv.types[e.key].name) or e.key)) credited = resolved end end
if n then local t = inv.getType(credited, (inv.types[credited] and inv.types[credited].name) or credited) if t then t.sac = inv.ema(t.sac, n) inv.note(string.format("sacrifice %s: %d favour (avg ~%.0f over n=%d, range %d-%d)", t.name or credited, n, t.sac.avg, t.sac.n, t.sac.min, t.sac.max)) end if inv.sacStats then inv.sacStats.done = inv.sacStats.done + 1 inv.sacStats.favour = inv.sacStats.favour + n end end -- the instance is gone from wherever we took it — remove the one the ALTAR -- named, not the one we asked for, or the map drifts by one every time. if not (e.container and inv.locRemove(e.container, credited, 1)) then inv.locRemove("loose", credited, 1) end inv.save() inv.deferStep(inv.sacSendNext) end
-- "There was nothing to sacrifice." — proof that a tracked instance is not -- actually there. Prune it, and give up once the map is clearly stale rather -- than grinding through dozens of phantom entries. -- Build the same reference with a different handle. local function reref(e, handle) if e.container and e.container ~= "loose" and e.container ~= "keep" then local meta = inv.contMeta[e.container] return string.format('%s from "%s"', handle, (meta and meta.name) or e.container) end return handle end
function inv.onSacNothing() -- Bulk sacrifice against an empty/all-refused stage bag: just finish. if inv.sacBulk then return inv.onSacBulkFinish(nil) end local e = inv.sacInFlight; inv.sacInFlight = nil if not e then return end
-- "Nothing to sacrifice" has two causes: the item is not there, or the handle -- does not name it. An ACTION-PROVEN handle already names the item, so this is -- the first case: the item is not in e.container -- a phantom map entry. Prune -- it and move on WITHOUT trying other handles or demoting (same rule as the -- staging mover). Only an UNPROVEN handle earns a retry down the ladder -- a -- display name like "piece of rotten bread" that `look` blessed but the altar -- rejects, while three of them sit in the bag. if e.handle and not inv.handleActProven(e.key, e.handle) then local tried = e.tried or {} tried[e.handle] = true local n = 0 for _ in pairs(tried) do n = n + 1 end local alt = (n <= inv.HANDLE_RETRIES) and inv.nextHandleAfter(e.key, tried) or nil if not alt then inv.markStuck(e.key, string.format("sacrifice reached nothing, last tried '%s'", e.handle), e.container) end if alt then inv.note(string.format("'%s' reached nothing — retrying as '%s'", e.handle, alt)) table.insert(inv.sacQueue, 1, { key = e.key, container = e.container, ref = reref(e, alt), handle = alt, learning = e.learning, tried = tried, }) return inv.deferStep(inv.sacSendNext) end end
if e.container then inv.locRemove(e.container, e.key, 1) end inv.sacMisses = inv.sacMisses + 1 if inv.sacStats then inv.sacStats.missing = inv.sacStats.missing + 1 end -- The stale-map guard stops us grinding through a long tail of phantoms -- but -- it must NOT strand the freshly-staged, known-present items in the stage bag. -- Bail only once no un-attempted stage-bag entry remains in the queue; until -- then keep going so those get their sacrifice. (Each phantom miss above prunes -- itself from the map, so the run still terminates.) local dst = inv.config.sacStageBag or "treasure" local stageLeft = false for _, q in ipairs(inv.sacQueue) do if q.container == dst then stageLeft = true; break end end if inv.sacMisses >= (inv.config.sacMaxMiss or 3) and not stageLeft then local left = #inv.sacQueue inv.sacReset(); inv.save() inv.warn(string.format( "%d sacrifices in a row found nothing — the location map is stale. Stopped and dropped %d queued.", inv.config.sacMaxMiss or 3, left)) return inv.sacFinish() end inv.deferStep(inv.sacSendNext) end
-- "You cannot sacrifice items from your keeplist." — a permanent property of -- the item, not a map error. Remember it and stop offering it to the altar. function inv.onSacKeeplist() local e = inv.sacInFlight; inv.sacInFlight = nil if not e then return end if inv.sacTimer then killTimer(inv.sacTimer); inv.sacTimer = nil end local t = inv.types[e.key] if t and not t.noSac then t.noSac = true inv.warn(string.format("%s is on your keeplist — it will not be offered to the altar again.", t.name or e.key)) inv.save() end -- not a miss: the item is demonstrably there inv.sacMisses = 0 inv.deferStep(inv.sacSendNext) end
-- "That is not worthy of sacrifice!" — the altar looked at the item and -- refused it. Unlike "There was nothing to sacrifice." this is NOT a handle -- or map problem: the item was found, identified and rejected on its merits, -- so retrying with another handle just burns commands. Like the keeplist -- refusal it is a property of the type, so remember it. -- -- Untracked, this line matched no trigger at all: the queue sat on its -- 8-second no-reply timer and reported "no reply sacrificing 'skin'", which -- reads like a lost packet rather than a definite answer from the game. function inv.onSacUnworthy() local e = inv.sacInFlight; inv.sacInFlight = nil if not e then return end if inv.sacTimer then killTimer(inv.sacTimer); inv.sacTimer = nil end local t = inv.types[e.key] if t and not t.noSac then t.noSac = true t.noSacWhy = "unworthy" inv.warn(string.format( "the altar refuses %s as not worthy — it will not be offered again. " .."(clear with: lua inv.types[%q].noSac=nil; inv.save())", t.name or e.key, e.key)) inv.save() end -- Not a miss: the item is demonstrably there, the altar simply said no. inv.sacMisses = 0 inv.deferStep(inv.sacSendNext) end
function inv.sacFinish() if inv.sacTimer then killTimer(inv.sacTimer); inv.sacTimer = nil end local s = inv.sacStats; inv.sacStats = nil if not s then return end inv.save() local extra = (s.misfired or 0) > 0 and string.format(", %d misfired (wrong item reached)", s.misfired) or "" if (s.pooled or 0) > 0 then extra = extra .. string.format(", %d unattributable (altar's wording fit several)", s.pooled) end cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[isac]<reset> done: <green>%d<reset> sacrificed for <green>%d<reset> favour, %d phantom entr%s pruned%s.\n", s.done, s.favour, s.missing, s.missing == 1 and "y" or "ies", extra)) -- worthless items collected during isacGo get dropped once the altar is done if inv.pendingDrops and #inv.pendingDrops > 0 then inv.dropRun() end inv.stuckNag() end
-- ---- Provenance ------------------------------------------------------- -- A corpse is a source, not a place we keep things. Treating one as a -- container invented a "corpse" bucket that outlived the corpse, and worse, -- `locMove("corpse", ...)` fell through to "find this key in ANY container" -- and decremented a real bag. -- -- It is also the one moment we know where an item came from: the kill report -- and the corpse header both name the monster, and the get echo says "from a -- corpse". Origin is the thread that ties an unidentified drop to the -- identified item it turns into. inv.lastMob = nil
function inv.isCorpseText(txt) if not txt then return false end txt = txt:lower() return txt:find("corpse") ~= nil or txt:find("dead body") ~= nil end
-- A `show id ground` handle names a corpse when it is `corpse` or a numbered -- `corpse 1`/`corpse 2`... (multi-corpse rooms number them). Some corpses show a -- body-part noun here instead ("cadaver", "yolk", "entrails") and are only -- revealed by the `show id <item>` Names list -- see inv.namesAreCorpse. function inv.handleIsCorpse(handle) return handle ~= nil and handle:match("^corpse%s*%d*$") ~= nil end
-- A corpse's full alias set (`show id <item>` -> "Names: corpse, remains, body, -- dead body, <noun>") always carries these generic body words. Any of them, -- standing alone as one of the comma-separated names, marks the item a corpse. -- (A real item named "... body ..." keeps that inside a longer name, so it is -- the standalone name that discriminates.) function inv.namesAreCorpse(list) if not list then return false end for name in list:gmatch("[^,]+") do name = name:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", ""):lower() if name == "corpse" or name == "dead body" or name == "remains" or name == "body" or name == "carcass" or name == "carrion" then return true end end return false end
-- "| Goblin's death report (1473 exp)" / "This is the dead body of goblin." function inv.noteKill(mob) if not mob or mob == "" then return end inv.lastMob = mob:lower():gsub("^the%s+", ""):gsub("^an?%s+", "") end
function inv.noteOrigin(key, mob) mob = mob or inv.lastMob if not (key and mob) then return end local t = inv.types[key] if not t then return end t.origins = t.origins or {} local first = not t.origins[mob] t.origins[mob] = (t.origins[mob] or 0) + 1 if first then inv.note(string.format("%s dropped by %s", t.name or key, mob)) inv.save() end end
-- Everything a monster of this name has been seen to drop. function inv.dropsOf(mob) local out = {} for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do if t.origins and t.origins[mob] then out[#out+1] = { key = k, n = t.origins[mob] } end end table.sort(out, function(a, b) return a.n > b.n end) return out end
-- ---- Container identity ---------------------------------------------- -- Game echoes name a container by DESCRIPTION ("a huge leather sack"), never -- by the name you gave it, so an unattributed get/put used to invent a -- phantom container keyed on the description. We learn desc -> name whenever -- both are known (a scan we initiated, or a get we queued) and use it after. inv.contDesc = inv.contDesc or {}
-- "loot" and "gear" are both huge leather sacks, so a description can name -- more than one container. When that happens the mapping is worthless and -- must not be guessed at — mark it ambiguous and fall back to the queue. function inv.noteContDesc(desc) local d = inv.key(desc) local k = inv.sackScanWaiting or inv.curSackKey if not (d and k) or d == k then return end local prev = inv.contDesc[d] if prev == k then return end if prev and prev ~= "?" then inv.contDesc[d] = "?" inv.note(string.format("'%s' describes both \"%s\" and \"%s\" — " .."echoes naming it can no longer be attributed by description.", d, prev, k)) else inv.contDesc[d] = k inv.note(string.format("container '%s' is \"%s\"", d, k)) end inv.save() end
-- Is this key a bag DESCRIPTION rather than a bag name? "huge leather sack" -- describes both "loot" and "gear", so it can never be a place to file -- anything — yet an unattributable put used to create a bucket under it, -- which no scan ever covered and nothing ever pruned. That is how 39 iron -- scale mail armours accumulated in a container that does not exist. function inv.isDescriptionKey(k) if not k then return false end if inv.contDesc[k] ~= nil then return true end -- a bag you named is one word or a short label; a description is prose return k:find("%s") ~= nil and (k:find("sack") or k:find("bag") or k:find("pouch") or k:find("backpack") or k:find("container")) ~= nil end
-- Mark the bags a description could refer to as needing a fresh look, so the -- next ishop/isac re-reads them instead of guessing. function inv.markBagsDirty(descKey) local any = false for k, v in pairs(inv.contDesc or {}) do if k == descKey and v and v ~= "?" then inv.scannedSacks[v] = nil; any = true end end if not any then for sack in pairs(inv.config.disposalSacks or {}) do inv.scannedSacks[sack] = nil end end end
-- Resolve a sack reference out of a game echo to a tracked container key. function inv.resolveSackText(txt) local sk = inv.sackKeyFromText(txt) if not sk then return nil end if inv.contMeta[sk] then return sk end local mapped = inv.contDesc[sk] if mapped and mapped ~= "?" then return mapped end return sk end
-- ---- Inline annotation (strict gate) --------------------------------- -- Annotation only happens while inv.annotMode is a non-nil string set by an -- opening marker and cleared by its closer (or the prompt). No heuristics. -- "iweight" : between the mass|bulk header rule and the closing rule -- "sack" : between "It contains:" and the summary line -- The main `i` listing is NOT annotated (no weights there); use `i weight`. inv.annotMode = nil
-- ---- Route-aware annotation (9.16) ----------------------------------- -- Old form: [ 68 s| 3 df| 85 s/l| 4 df/l] -- four columns, both per-litre -- figures side by side, no indication of what the item will actually DO. -- New form: [ 68 s| 3 df| 85 s/l] -- the third column is the per-litre -- metric of the route the item is HEADED for (s/l coloured green when it will -- be sold, df/l coloured cyan when sacrificed, "drop"/"learn"/"coin" for the -- rest), so one glance at a listing shows every disposal decision. Fixed field -- widths keep the column aligned once the whole block is right-justified. inv.ANNOT_W = 29 -- total plain width of one annotation, for alignment
-- Resolve the figures to display for a sighting: a variant's own numbers win. function inv.annotFigures(key, rawname) local t = inv.types[key] if not t then return nil end local v = inv.variantOf(key, rawname, false) local src = t if v and v ~= t and (v.sell or v.sac) then src = { sell = v.sell or t.sell, sac = v.sac or t.sac, volume = t.volume, noSell = t.noSell, noSac = t.noSac, sellCat = t.sellCat } end local sell = src.sell and src.sell.avg or nil local sac = src.sac and src.sac.avg or nil local voll = src.volume and src.volume > 0 and (src.volume/1000) or nil return sell, sac, voll end
-- The third column: the route's own per-litre metric, plus its colour. function inv.annotRoute(key, sell, sac, voll) local W = 10 local function pad(s) return string.rep(" ", math.max(0, W-#s))..s end if inv.coinInfo(key) then return pad("coin"), "ansi_yellow" end local route = inv.disposeRoute(key) local sl = (sell and voll) and (sell/voll) or nil local dl = (sac and voll) and (sac /voll) or nil if route == "sell" then return pad((sl and string.format("%.0f", sl) or "?").." s/l"), "ansi_green" elseif route == "sac" then return pad((dl and string.format("%.0f", dl) or "?").." df/l"), "ansi_cyan" elseif route == "drop" then return pad("drop"), "ansi_light_black" else -- "unknown": needs an appraisal and/or a favour reading return pad("learn"), "ansi_yellow" end end
-- Segments to insert: {text, color}. Kept separate so annotateLine can colour -- the route column without inline colour codes throwing off the width maths. function inv.annotSegments(key, rawname) local sell, sac, voll = inv.annotFigures(key, rawname) local function rj(v, w) local s = v and string.format("%.0f", v) or "?" return string.rep(" ", math.max(0, w-#s))..s end local field, color = inv.annotRoute(key, sell, sac, voll) return { { text = string.format("[%s s|%s df|", rj(sell, 5), rj(sac, 5)), color = "ansi_white" }, { text = field, color = color }, { text = "]", color = "ansi_white" }, } end
function inv.annotateLine(rawname, isKeep) if not inv.config.annotate then return end if isKeep then return end -- kept items are not disposal candidates if not (insertText and moveCursor and getLineNumber and getCurrentLine) then return end local key = inv.key(rawname); if not key then return end local cur = getCurrentLine() or ""
-- Right-justify to the window's right edge (as far right as it fits), or to -- an explicit column if the player pinned one with `inv.config.annotRightCol`. local rightCol = inv.config.annotRightCol if not rightCol and getWindowWrap then local ok, w = pcall(getWindowWrap, "main") if ok and type(w) == "number" and w > 40 then rightCol = w - 1 end end rightCol = rightCol or 100 local pad = math.max(2, rightCol - #cur - inv.ANNOT_W)
moveCursor(#cur, getLineNumber()) -- insertText inserts AT the cursor and does NOT advance it, so successive -- inserts stack in REVERSE. Insert the coloured segments back-to-front, then -- the leading pad last, so the block lands in forward order: -- <pad>[ s| df| route]. local segs = inv.annotSegments(key, rawname) for i = #segs, 1, -1 do if fg then fg(segs[i].color or "ansi_white") end insertText(segs[i].text) end if resetFormat then resetFormat() end insertText(string.rep(" ", pad)) if moveCursorEnd then moveCursorEnd() end end
-- Prompt resets all multi-line modes — hard safety net against leaks. function inv.onPrompt() -- A live probe owns the prompt: it delimits one candidate's response block. if inv.probe and inv.probe.awaiting then return inv.probeBlockEnd() end -- A room scan may only be closed by the prompt belonging to ITS OWN look. -- Anything already in flight when iloot starts answers first, and its prompt -- used to close the scan while the room block was still on its way: type -- `dig grave` and `iloot` together and iloot reported "no items here" a -- moment before the room listed nine of them. The exits line is the marker — -- it means our look's room block has begun — so a prompt before it belongs -- to somebody else's command and is ignored. if inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.active then if inv.roomScan.sawRoom then inv.roomScanEnd() end end if inv.scan then inv.scanEnd() end -- close a show id block on the prompt that follows it — but only once its -- header has arrived, so a prompt from a PRIOR command cannot abort it early. if inv.showId and inv.showId.active then inv.showIdFinish() end inv.annotMode = nil inv.sacArming = false -- The shopkeeper's identity deliberately SURVIVES the prompt: a sale never -- names them, so clearing it here left every sale unattributable. It is -- reset when a shop run starts instead. end
-- ---- Trigger entry points (strict, marker-bounded) ------------------- -- i weight: " mass | bulk |" opens; rule line "----+----" after header is -- ignored; each " N.Nkg N.Nl name" is an item; footer "N.Nkg |N.Nl" or a -- second rule closes. function inv.iwStart() inv.annotMode = "iweight" inv.scanStart("iweight") -- consume the one-shot flag set when this `i weight` was fired only to -- measure something (inv.shopSizeIfNeeded) if inv.sizingScan then inv.scan.sizing = true; inv.sizingScan = nil end end function inv.iwKeep() inv.scanKeepMark() end -- returns true if it consumed the line as an item function inv.iwLine(raw) if inv.annotMode ~= "iweight" then return end -- footer "152.7kg |108.7l" -> close if raw:match("^%s*[%d.]+kg%s*|%s*[%d.]+l%s*$") then inv.scanEnd(); inv.annotMode = nil if inv.loot.active and inv.loot.pendingSort and inv.loot.sortGen == inv.loot.gen then inv.lootSort() end return end -- rule line if raw:match("^%s*%-+%+%-+") then return end -- header if raw:match("mass") and raw:match("bulk") then return end local mass, vol, name = raw:match("^%s*([%d.]+)kg%s+([%d.]+)l%s+(.+)$") if not (mass and name) then return end local qty = tonumber(name:match("^(%d+)%s*x%s")) or 1 inv.scanItem(name, qty, tonumber(mass), tonumber(vol)) -- Loose inventory lists carried items AND the keep section; only the loose, -- non-keep items are disposal candidates, so keep items go un-annotated. inv.annotateLine(name, inv.scan and inv.scan.inKeep) end
-- sack contents: "It contains:" opens; bare item lines; summary closes. -- sack contents: "It contains:" opens; bare item lines; summary closes. -- The sack we're looking in is captured from the look COMMAND (the game's -- response doesn't echo the custom name), via inv.noteLook below. -- Record which container a `look` was aimed at. The reply never names the bag -- (see the "This is a huge leather sack." header), so this is the only source -- of the key — which makes it worth being paranoid about. -- -- The alias hands us a capture group, and a wrapped regex can hand over the -- whole command instead of its argument. Getting `l "loot"` here rather than -- `loot` silently created a phantom container that nothing else ever looked -- in, so strip any leading look verb and preposition defensively. function inv.noteLook(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") arg = arg:gsub("^[Ll][Oo][Oo][Kk]%s+", ""):gsub("^[Ll]%s+", "") arg = arg:gsub("^[Ii][Nn]%s+", ""):gsub("^[Aa][Tt]%s+", "") arg = arg:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") arg = arg:gsub('^"(.*)"$', "%1"):gsub("^'(.*)'$", "%1") arg = arg:gsub('"', ""):gsub("'", "") arg = arg:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") if arg ~= "" then inv.curSackKey = arg:lower() else inv.curSackKey = nil end end
function inv.sackStart(sackKey) -- prefer the key of a scan we issued ourselves over whatever the alias saw sackKey = inv.sackScanWaiting or sackKey inv.annotMode = "sack" inv.scanStart("sack", sackKey) end function inv.sackLine(raw) if inv.annotMode ~= "sack" then return end if raw:find("^It contains:") then return end -- summary/closers end the block if raw:find("^The .* sack is ") or raw:find("^There [ai]re ") or raw:find("^It seems ") or raw:find("^It looks ") or raw:find("^This is ") or raw:find("%.%s*$") then inv.scanEnd(); inv.annotMode = nil; return end local qty = tonumber(raw:match("^(%d+)%s*x%s")) or 1 inv.scanItem(raw, qty, nil, nil) inv.annotateLine(raw) end
-- plain `i` listing: sets keep flags + validates counts. It carries no weights, -- so per-litre figures come from the stored volume of a prior `i weight`; a type -- never weighed simply shows `?` in the s/l column. Loose (non-keep) items are -- annotated here too, so a bare `i` shows the same route info as `i weight`. function inv.iStart() inv.scanStart("i") end function inv.iKeep() inv.scanKeepMark() end function inv.iLine(raw) if not inv.scan or inv.scan.kind ~= "i" then return end -- reject non-item lines that can appear in the listing if raw:find("^You are carrying") or raw:find("^Money:") or raw:find("^Keep:") or raw:match("^%s*$") then return end local qty = tonumber(raw:match("^%s*(%d+)%s*x%s")) or 1 inv.scanItem(raw, qty, nil, nil) inv.annotateLine(raw, inv.scan and inv.scan.inKeep) end
-- ---- show id: the parser's own handle oracle (9.19) ------------------ -- `show id ground` lists every object on the floor with the exact handle to -- type -- its "Name to type" column -- so it replaces the whole look-probe -- ladder for room items with ONE command. Its handles are recorded at the top -- HANDLE_SRC_ID tier and preferred over every guess. It does NOT flag NPCs or -- fixtures, so the what-to-loot decision stays with the room scan + classify + -- nonItems filter; show id only supplies the handle for items we already chose -- to take, and a handle is recorded ONLY for a type we already track (so the -- fountain/lamp/NPC rows do not invent junk types). -- -- Names recognized by the parser, on the ground: -- Item Name to type -- Scrolled letter scrolled letter -- Ereldon, the local sage ereldon -- Use 'show id <object>' to see every name for a single item. inv.showId = nil inv.showIdTimer = nil
function inv.showIdRun(scope, onDone, report) if inv.showId then if onDone then onDone() end; return end -- one at a time scope = scope or "ground" inv.showId = { active = false, scope = scope, onDone = onDone, n = 0, report = report, sawCorpse = false, corpses = {} } local cmd = (scope == "inventory") and "show id inventory" or "show id ground" cecho("\n<grey>[iid]<reset> <cyan>"..cmd.."<reset>") send(cmd, false) if inv.showIdTimer then killTimer(inv.showIdTimer) end inv.showIdTimer = tempTimer(6, function() if inv.showId then inv.showIdFinish() end end) end
function inv.showIdStart() if inv.showId then inv.showId.active = true end end
function inv.showIdLine(raw) if not (inv.showId and inv.showId.active) then return end if raw:find("^Use 'show id") then return inv.showIdFinish() end -- footer if raw:match("^%s*$") or raw:find("^Names recognized") then return end if raw:match("^%s*Item%s%s+Name to type") then return end -- column header -- "<display> <handle>": split on the column gap (2+ spaces). The handle may -- itself be several single-spaced words ("scrolled letter"). local disp, handle = raw:match("^%s*(.-)%s%s+(%S.*)$") if not (disp and handle) then return end disp = disp:gsub("%s+$", "") handle = handle:gsub("%s+$", ""):lower() if disp == "" or handle == "" then return end -- A corpse's ground handle is `corpse`, or `corpse 1`/`corpse 2`... when the -- room holds several. We never loot corpses: flag the room so iloot digs the -- grave (which spills the contents) instead, mark the type persistently so a -- later scan knows without re-querying, and do NOT adopt the handle. (Corpses -- that show a body-part noun here instead -- "cadaver", "yolk" -- are caught -- from their Names list in idNamesLine.) if inv.handleIsCorpse(handle) then inv.showId.sawCorpse = true local ck = inv.key(disp) if ck then inv.showId.corpses[ck] = true if inv.types[ck] then inv.types[ck].corpse = true end end return end local key = inv.key(disp) -- adopt the handle only for a type we already track (an item we scanned); -- fixtures and NPCs listed here are not turned into tracked types. if key and inv.types[key] then inv.handleRecordOk(key, handle, inv.HANDLE_SRC_ID) -- Remember the game's OWN disambiguated pick for this object. `show id` -- chose a handle that is unambiguous in its scope -- it lists "cloth cloak", -- not the shared "cloak", precisely because a worn (or other) cloak also -- answers to "cloak". Prefer this pick for actions so a shorter generic alias -- can't send an inventory-scoped verb (sell/sacrifice/put) at the wrong item -- -- e.g. the WORN keeplist cloak, which the map-only ambiguity check cannot -- see. Skip numbered picks ("coat 2"): those are positional and go stale. if not handle:match("%d$") then inv.types[key].showIdHandle = handle end inv.showId.n = inv.showId.n + 1 end end
function inv.showIdFinish() local s = inv.showId; inv.showId = nil if inv.showIdTimer then killTimer(inv.showIdTimer); inv.showIdTimer = nil end if not s then return end if s.n > 0 and s.report then cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[iid]<reset> learned/updated handles for <green>%d<reset> tracked item(s).\n", s.n)) end if s.n > 0 then inv.save() end local cb = s.onDone if cb then inv.deferStep(function() cb(s) end) end end
-- iid: run `show id ground` by hand to refresh handles for the current room. function inv.iidCmd(arg) if inv.showId then inv.warn("a show-id read is already in progress."); return end inv.showIdRun("ground", nil, true) end
-- ---- minventory: the game's own categorised, keep-aware census (9.31) -- -- `minventory deep weight worn` lists every carried item -- loose, in every bag -- (nested), and worn/wielded -- grouped by the GAME's category (Weapons, Armour, -- Hearts, Food, Skins, ...), each flagged +/-/~ for keep status. That is a -- direct, authoritative source for two things the package used to reverse- -- engineer: an item's disposal CATEGORY, and which handles are OCCUPIED by worn -- gear (so an inventory verb can't misfire on them -- the 9.30 cloak problem). -- -- Phase 1 is deliberately READ-ONLY: it learns categories and worn nouns and -- reports, but does NOT rebuild the location map (that nesting reconcile is a -- larger, riskier follow-up). The existing l-scan census stays in charge.
-- Head noun of a display name, matching the game's handle ("Fabled silk cloak of -- barbarian lords" -> "cloak"): drop named "..."/<glow>/(parenthetical) and the -- "of ..." qualifier, take the last remaining word. function inv.headNounOf(name) local n = (name or ""):lower() n = n:gsub('%s+named%s+".-"', ""):gsub("%s*<[^>]*>", ""):gsub("%s*%b()", "") n = n:gsub("%s+of%s+.*$", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") return n:match("(%S+)%s*$") or n end
-- minventory category -> the package's sellCat, using the SAME strings the shop -- refusals produce ("I don't buy armours") so shop.accepts/rejects still match. -- Hearts and Food both map to "food" (sac-only, per config.sacOnlyCats). inv.minvCatMap = { weapons="weapons", armour="armours", ammo="ammo", food="food", hearts="food", skins="skins", drink="drink", treasure="treasure", }
function inv.minvStart() inv.minv = { active=true, cat=nil, section="pre", catN=0, wornNouns={}, wornN=0 } end
-- Parse one minventory line into its fields (see minv_proto for the grammar). function inv.minvParse(raw, st) local line = raw line = line:gsub("%s*%[[^%]]-df|[^%]]-%]%s*$", "") -- strip our annotation local div = line:match("^%s*%-+%s*(%a+)%s*%-+%s*$") if div then st.section = div:lower(); return { divider = div:lower() } end if line:match("^You are carrying") or line:match("^Of that,") or line:match("^Money:") or line:match("%d+/%d+HP") or line:match("^%s*$") then return nil end local cat = line:match("^%s*(%a+):") local rest if cat then st.cat = cat:lower(); rest = line:gsub("^%s*%a+:%s*", "") else rest = line:gsub("^%s+", "") end local body = rest:match("^[%so%.]*%d[%d%.]*kg%s+%d[%d%.]*l%s+(.*)$") -- weight cols if body then rest = body end local keep = rest:match("^([%+%-~])") if keep then rest = rest:gsub("^[%+%-~]%s*", "") end local depth = 0 local bar = rest:match("^|%s*") if bar then depth = 1; rest = rest:sub(#bar + 1) while true do local d = rest:match("^%.%s*"); if not d then break end depth = depth + 1; rest = rest:sub(#d + 1) end end local qty = tonumber(rest:match("^(%d+)x%s+")) or 1 rest = rest:gsub("^%d+x%s+", "") local container = rest:match("%[[=%s]*%]%s*$") ~= nil rest = rest:gsub("%s*%[[=%s]*%]%s*$", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") if rest == "" then return nil end local worn = (st.section=="wielded" or st.section=="worn" or st.cat=="wielded" or st.cat=="worn") return { cat=st.cat, keep=keep, depth=depth, qty=qty, name=rest, container=container, worn=worn } end
function inv.minvLine(raw) local st = inv.minv; if not (st and st.active) then return end local prompt = raw:match("%d+/%d+HP") local r = inv.minvParse(raw, st) if not r then if prompt then inv.minvFinish() end; return end if r.divider then return end if r.worn then -- a worn/wielded item: its head noun is a handle an inventory verb could -- reach, so record it as OCCUPIED. Do not touch its category or the map. local noun = inv.headNounOf(r.name) if noun and noun ~= "" and not st.wornNouns[noun] then st.wornNouns[noun] = true; st.wornN = st.wornN + 1 end return end if r.container then return end -- a bag, not a disposable item -- category learning: fill sellCat for a type we already track. minventory is -- the game's own answer, so it also overrides a merely INFERRED category, but -- never an appraisal-confirmed one (leave that alone). local sc = inv.minvCatMap[r.cat or ""] if sc then local key = inv.key(r.name) local t = key and inv.types[key] if t and (not t.sellCat or t.sellCatInferred) and t.sellCat ~= sc then t.sellCat = sc; t.sellCatInferred = nil st.catN = st.catN + 1 elseif t and not t.sellCat then t.sellCat = sc; t.sellCatInferred = nil; st.catN = st.catN + 1 end end end
function inv.minvFinish() local st = inv.minv; inv.minv = nil if not st then return end if inv.minvTimer then killTimer(inv.minvTimer); inv.minvTimer = nil end -- commit the worn-noun set (replace, so unequipped gear stops blocking) inv.config.wornNouns = st.wornNouns inv.save() cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[imv]<reset> categorised <green>%d<reset> item type(s); noted <green>%d<reset> worn handle(s).\n", st.catN, st.wornN)) local cb = st.onDone; if cb then inv.deferStep(cb) end end
-- imv: run `minventory deep worn` and apply the learning above. function inv.minvRun(onDone) if inv.minv then if onDone then onDone() end; return end inv.minvStart(); inv.minv.onDone = onDone local cmd = "minventory deep worn" cecho("\n<grey>[imv]<reset> <cyan>"..cmd.."<reset>") send(cmd, false) if inv.minvTimer then killTimer(inv.minvTimer) end inv.minvTimer = tempTimer(6, function() if inv.minv then inv.minvFinish() end end) end
function inv.minvCmd() inv.minvRun() end
-- Is `handle` a bare string a WORN item also answers to? Sending it to an -- inventory-scoped verb (sell/sacrifice/put/look) would risk hitting the worn -- item, so disposal avoids it when a more specific handle exists (9.30/9.31). function inv.wornClash(handle) return inv.config.wornNouns and handle and inv.config.wornNouns[handle] == true end
-- ---- Full handle registration: `show id <item>` (9.21) --------------- -- `show id ground` gives ONE handle per object; `show id <item>` gives the -- WHOLE set: -- Stone studded heavy cloth gloves -- Names: gloves, stone gloves -- We query it once per type (idFull flag) for every tracked room item -- trash -- included -- so the full alias set is on file. That is what can finally -- separate items that share a short handle: if a heart's set turns out to hold -- a specific "heart of troll", collisions on bare `heart` are solvable. inv.idQueue = {} inv.idInFlight = nil inv.idTimer = nil inv.idOnDone = nil
function inv.handleIdFull(key) local h = inv.handlesOf(key); return h and h.idFull == true end
function inv.idFullRun(keys, onDone) inv.idQueue = {} if inv.config.idFull then local seen = {} for _, k in ipairs(keys or {}) do if not seen[k] and not inv.coinInfo(k) and not inv.config.nonItems[k] and not inv.handleIdFull(k) then local h = inv.handleKnown(k) -- a handle to address `show id` with if h then seen[k] = true; inv.idQueue[#inv.idQueue+1] = { key = k, handle = h } end end end end if #inv.idQueue == 0 then if onDone then onDone() end; return end inv.idOnDone = onDone inv.idSendNext() end
function inv.idSendNext() if inv.idTimer then killTimer(inv.idTimer); inv.idTimer = nil end local e = table.remove(inv.idQueue, 1) if not e then inv.idInFlight = nil local cb = inv.idOnDone; inv.idOnDone = nil inv.save() if cb then cb() end return end inv.idInFlight = e send("show id " .. e.handle, false) inv.idTimer = tempTimer(4, function() if inv.idInFlight == e then inv.idInFlight = nil; inv.deferStep(inv.idSendNext) end end) end
-- " Names: a, b, c" — record every name for the in-flight type and mark it -- fully registered so it is never re-queried. function inv.idNamesLine(raw) local e = inv.idInFlight if not e then return end local list = raw:match("Names:%s*(.+)$") or raw if not list then return end -- The Names list is the reliable corpse tell: a body-part-named corpse -- ("cadaver"/"yolk") whose ground handle gave nothing away still lists -- "corpse, remains, body, dead body" here. Flag the type as a corpse and adopt -- NONE of these as handles -- they are generic and shared across every corpse, -- and iloot digs corpses rather than handling them. if inv.namesAreCorpse(list) then if inv.types[e.key] then inv.types[e.key].corpse = true end local h = inv.handlesOf(e.key, true); if h then h.idFull = true end inv.idInFlight = nil return inv.deferStep(inv.idSendNext) end for name in list:gmatch("[^,]+") do name = name:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", ""):lower() if name ~= "" and name ~= "corpse" then inv.handleRecordOk(e.key, name, inv.HANDLE_SRC_ID) end end local h = inv.handlesOf(e.key, true); if h then h.idFull = true end inv.idInFlight = nil inv.deferStep(inv.idSendNext) end
