-- ---- Reporting -------------------------------------------------------- function inv.fmtWt(g) if not g then return "?" end return g>=1000 and string.format("%.2fkg",g/1000) or string.format("%.0fg",g) end function inv.fmtVol(ml) if not ml then return "?" end return ml>=1000 and string.format("%.2fl",ml/1000) or string.format("%.0fml",ml) end
function inv.report(filter) local rows = {} for k,t in pairs(inv.types) do if not filter or (t.name and t.name:lower():find(filter:lower(),1,true)) then rows[#rows+1] = {k=k,t=t} end end table.sort(rows, function(a,b) return (a.t.sell and a.t.sell.avg or -1) > (b.t.sell and b.t.sell.avg or -1) end) cecho("\n<white>Item Weight Volume Sell Sac Where<reset>\n") cecho(string.rep("-",82).."\n") for _,r in ipairs(rows) do local t=r.t local where = {} local loose = inv.locCount("loose", r.k) if loose > 0 then where[#where+1] = loose.." loose" end for _,c in ipairs(inv.containersWith(r.k)) do where[#where+1] = inv.locCount(r.k and c, r.k).." "..c end cecho(string.format("%-36s %-9s %-9s %-7s %-6s %s\n", (t.name or "?"):sub(1,36), inv.fmtWt(t.weight), inv.fmtVol(t.volume), t.sell and string.format("%.0f",t.sell.avg) or "-", t.sac and string.format("%.0f",t.sac.avg) or "-", table.concat(where,","))) end cecho(string.rep("-",82).."\n") end
function inv.detail(filter) for k,t in pairs(inv.types) do if t.name and t.name:lower():find(filter:lower(),1,true) then cecho(string.format("\n<white>%s<reset>\n", t.name)) cecho(string.format(" weight %s (n=%d) volume %s (n=%d)\n", inv.fmtWt(t.weight), t.weightN or 0, inv.fmtVol(t.volume), t.volumeN or 0)) if t.sell then cecho(string.format(" sell ~%.0f range %d-%d (n=%d)\n", t.sell.avg,t.sell.min,t.sell.max,t.sell.n)) end if t.sac then cecho(string.format(" sacrifice ~%.0f range %d-%d (n=%d)\n", t.sac.avg,t.sac.min,t.sac.max,t.sac.n)) end -- "all" here, not the action-filtered list: the point of iitem is to -- show what is known, including which handles are still only look-deep. local hl = inv.handleList(k, "all") if #hl > 0 then local shown = {} for _, x in ipairs(hl) do shown[#shown+1] = inv.handleActProven(k, x) and ("<green>"..x.."<reset>") or ("<yellow>"..x.."<reset> <grey>(look only)<reset>") end cecho(" handles: "..table.concat(shown, ", ").."\n") else cecho(" handles: <grey>none proven<reset> — run 'iprobe "..(t.name or k).."'\n") end local hh = inv.handlesOf(k) if hh and next(hh.amb) then local a = {} for x in pairs(hh.amb) do local sc = inv.ambScopes(k, x) if #sc == 0 or sc[1] == "any" then a[#a+1] = x else a[#a+1] = string.format("%s (shadowed in %s)", x, table.concat(sc, ", ")) end end table.sort(a) cecho(" ambiguous: <yellow>"..table.concat(a, ", ").."<reset>\n") end if t.resembles then cecho(" resembles: "..t.resembles.."\n") end if t.sellCat then cecho(" category: "..t.sellCat.."\n") end if t.unidentified then cecho(" <yellow>unidentified<reset>\n") end if inv.variantCount(k) > 1 then cecho(string.format(" <yellow>%d variants share this name<reset> " .."— the figures above pool all of them:\n", inv.variantCount(k))) local gs = {} for g in pairs(t.variants) do gs[#gs+1] = g end table.sort(gs) for _, g in ipairs(gs) do local v = t.variants[g] local sv = v.sell and string.format("%.0f s", v.sell.avg) or "? s" local sc = v.sac and string.format("%.0f df", v.sac.avg) or "? df" cecho(string.format(" <%s>%-28s<reset> %10s %8s (n=%d)\n", "grey", "<"..g.." glow>", sv, sc, (v.sell and v.sell.n) or (v.sac and v.sac.n) or 0)) end end if t.unidentifiedAs then cecho(" drops as: <grey>".. ((inv.types[t.unidentifiedAs] and inv.types[t.unidentifiedAs].name) or t.unidentifiedAs).."<reset>\n") end if t.identifiesAs and next(t.identifiesAs) then local a = {} for k2, n2 in pairs(t.identifiesAs) do a[#a+1] = string.format("%s (x%d)", (inv.types[k2] and inv.types[k2].name) or k2, n2) end table.sort(a) cecho(" identifies as: <cyan>"..table.concat(a, ", ").."<reset>\n") end if t.origins and next(t.origins) then local o = {} for mob, n2 in pairs(t.origins) do o[#o+1] = string.format("%s (x%d)", mob, n2) end table.sort(o) cecho(" dropped by: "..table.concat(o, ", ").."\n") end local bn, bp = inv.bestShopFor(k) if bn then cecho(string.format(" best price: <green>%d<reset> s at %s\n", bp, bn)) end cecho(" locations: ") local loose=inv.locCount("loose",k); local keep=inv.locCount("keep",k) local parts={} if loose>0 then parts[#parts+1]=loose.." loose" end if keep>0 then parts[#parts+1]=keep.." keep" end for _,c in ipairs(inv.containersWith(k)) do parts[#parts+1]=inv.locCount(c,k).." in "..c end cecho((#parts>0 and table.concat(parts,", ") or "none known").."\n") return end end inv.warn("no item matching '"..filter.."'.") end
-- ---- Divine favour exchange rate -------------------------------------- -- What one favour is worth in silver is not published anywhere, and it is -- half of every route decision classify() makes. The only honest source is -- our own data: a type with BOTH a sale price and a favour reading implies a -- rate of sell/sac silver per favour. -- -- Samples where sell == 0 are excluded on purpose. "No shop pays for this" is -- a fact about the shop route, not about the price of favour; counting them -- drags the estimate toward zero and would eventually send everything to the -- altar for entirely the wrong reason. function inv.dfCalibrate() local ratios = {} for key, t in pairs(inv.types) do local sell = t.sell and t.sell.avg local sac = t.sac and t.sac.avg if sell and sac and sell > 0 and sac > 0 then ratios[#ratios+1] = { r = sell / sac, name = t.name or key, sell = sell, sac = sac } end end table.sort(ratios, function(a, b) return a.r < b.r end) local n = #ratios if n == 0 then return nil, ratios end -- median, not mean: one absurd outlier should not move the rate local med if n % 2 == 1 then med = ratios[(n + 1) / 2].r else med = (ratios[n / 2].r + ratios[n / 2 + 1].r) / 2 end return med, ratios end
function inv.dfCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") local C = inv.config local measured, samples = inv.dfCalibrate()
if arg == "" or arg == "show" then cecho(string.format( "\n<white>Divine favour rate<reset> 1 DF = <cyan>%g<reset> silver\n", C.dfToSilver)) cecho(string.format( " keep at or above <cyan>%g<reset> silver-equiv per litre; permanent trash below <cyan>%g<reset>\n", C.cutoffSL, C.cutoffSL / C.trashDiv)) if measured then cecho(string.format( " measured from <white>%d<reset> type(s) with both numbers: median <cyan>%.1f<reset> silver per DF\n", #samples, measured)) local show = math.min(6, #samples) for i = 1, show do local x = samples[i] cecho(string.format(" %-30s %8.0f s / %6.1f DF = %7.1f\n", (x.name or "?"):sub(1, 30), x.sell, x.sac, x.r)) end if #samples > show then cecho(string.format(" <grey>...%d more<reset>\n", #samples - show)) end cecho(" <grey>'idf auto' adopts the median; 'idf 250' sets it by hand.<reset>\n") else cecho(" <grey>nothing measured yet: no type has both a sale price and a favour reading.\n" .. " isac spends one of each new type at the altar, so this fills in on its own.<reset>\n") end return end
if arg == "auto" then if not measured then inv.warn("nothing measured yet — no type has both a sale price and a favour reading.") return end if #samples < 3 then inv.warn(string.format( "only %d sample(s) — a median off that is noise. Use 'idf auto' again once isac has " .."priced a few more, or set it by hand.", #samples)) return end local old = C.dfToSilver C.dfToSilver = math.floor(measured * 10 + 0.5) / 10 inv.save() cecho(string.format( "\n<green>[idf]<reset> 1 DF = <cyan>%g<reset> silver <grey>(was %g; median of %d measured type(s))<reset>\n", C.dfToSilver, old, #samples)) return end
local n = tonumber(arg) if not n or n <= 0 then inv.warn("usage: idf -- show the rate and what the data implies") inv.warn(" idf 100 -- 1 divine favour is worth 100 silver") inv.warn(" idf auto -- adopt the measured median") return end local old = C.dfToSilver C.dfToSilver = n inv.save() cecho(string.format("\n<green>[idf]<reset> 1 DF = <cyan>%g<reset> silver <grey>(was %g)<reset>\n", C.dfToSilver, old)) if measured then cecho(string.format(" <grey>your own data implies %.1f<reset>\n", measured)) end end
-- ---- Disposal advisor: suggest exact commands ------------------------ function inv.worth(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") -- `iworth rate N` used to set favourPerSilver, a SECOND conversion constant -- that only this advisor read, while classify() used dfToSilver — so the -- table could recommend a route the router would never take. One constant -- now; the old spelling forwards to it, with its meaning inverted (silver -- per favour, not favour per silver). local rate = arg:match("^rate%s+([%d.]+)$") if rate then return inv.dfCmd(rate) end
-- gather instances sitting in the disposal sacks (and loose) local rate2 = inv.config.dfToSilver local rows = {} local function consider(container) local seen = {} for _,key in ipairs(inv.loc[container] or {}) do if not seen[key] then seen[key]=true local t = inv.types[key]; if t then local sell=t.sell and t.sell.avg or nil local sac =t.sac and t.sac.avg or nil local sacEq = sac and (sac * rate2) or nil local route,best = "-",nil if sell and sacEq then if sell>=sacEq then route,best="sell",sell else route,best="sac",sacEq end elseif sell then route,best="sell",sell elseif sacEq then route,best="sac",sacEq end local ref = inv.refFor(container, key) rows[#rows+1]={t=t,container=container,count=inv.locCount(container,key), sell=sell,sac=sac,route=route,best=best,ref=ref} end end end end consider("loose") for sack in pairs(inv.config.disposalSacks) do consider(sack) end if #rows==0 then inv.warn("nothing in loose or disposal sacks (looties/loot/treasure). Run 'i weight' and 'l \"loot\"' to populate."); return end table.sort(rows, function(a,b) return (a.best or -1)*a.count > (b.best or -1)*b.count end)
cecho(string.format( "\n<white>Disposal advisor<reset> <grey>(1 DF = %g silver; keep at/above %g s/l)<reset>\n", rate2, inv.config.cutoffSL)) cecho(string.format("<white>%-28s %3s %-8s %-8s %-5s %s<reset>\n","Item","Qty","Sell","Sac","Best","Command")) cecho(string.rep("-",92).."\n") for _,r in ipairs(rows) do local cmd = r.ref and ((r.route=="sac" and "sacrifice " or "sell ")..r.ref) or "<grey>(re-stow to index)<reset>" cecho(string.format("%-28s %3d %-8s %-8s %s%-5s<reset> %s\n", (r.t.name or "?"):sub(1,28), r.count, r.sell and string.format("%.0f",r.sell) or "-", r.sac and string.format("%.0f",r.sac) or "-", r.route=="sell" and "<yellow>" or (r.route=="sac" and "<cyan>" or ""), r.route, cmd)) end cecho(string.rep("-",92).."\n") end
function inv.containerReport() cecho("\n<white>Containers:<reset>\n") for cont,l in pairs(inv.loc) do if cont~="loose" and cont~="keep" and #l>0 then local meta=inv.contMeta[cont] cecho(string.format(" %-16s %d items %s\n", cont, #l, (meta and meta.trusted==false) and "<yellow>(order untrusted — re-stow)<reset>" or "")) end end end
-- ---- Location-map maintenance ---------------------------------------- -- Over time the location map can drift from reality (manual sells/drops, -- items consumed, pre-tracking contents). iclean wipes the WHERE-map (not the -- learned value/weight stats) so it rebuilds cleanly from observation: -- `i weight` repopulates loose+keep, and `look in <sack>` each sack. function inv.clean(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") local j = arg:match("^junk%s*(.*)$") if j then return inv.cleanJunk(j) end local g = arg:match("^ghosts?%s*(.*)$") if g then return inv.cleanGhosts(g) end if arg == "loose" then inv.loc.loose = {} cecho("\n<green>[inv]<reset> cleared loose; run <cyan>i weight<reset> to repopulate.\n") inv.save(); return end if arg ~= "confirm" then local total = 0 for _, l in pairs(inv.loc) do total = total + #l end cecho(string.format("\n<yellow>[inv]<reset> This wipes the location map (%d tracked entries) but KEEPS " .."learned values/weights.\nAfter cleaning, run <cyan>i weight<reset> and <cyan>look in<reset> each sack to rebuild.\n" .."Type <cyan>iclean confirm<reset> to proceed.\n", total)) return end inv.loc = { loose = {}, keep = {} } inv.contMeta = {} inv.scannedSacks = {} inv.save() cecho("\n<green>[inv]<reset> location map cleared. Run <cyan>i weight<reset>, then <cyan>look in<reset> " .."each disposal sack to rebuild what's where.\n")end
-- ---- Shop rejection learning ----------------------------------------- -- Vendors only buy what they peddle. When a vendor refuses a category -- ("I don't buy food stuff"), we record it per shopkeeper and skip those -- items next visit. -- inv.shops[npcKey] = { rejects = { food=true, ... } } inv.shops = inv.shops or {} inv.currentShopNPC = nil -- set from "You show the item to X." echo
function inv.shopNPCKey(name) return name and name:lower():gsub("%s+","_") or nil end
-- Record that this shop dealt with this item, and at what price. Rejections -- were already remembered; without the positive side there was no way to know -- WHERE to take something, only where not to. function inv.shopNoteDeal(key, silver) local npc = inv.currentShopNPC if not (npc and key) then return end local k = inv.shopNPCKey(npc) local sh = inv.shops[k] or { rejects = {} } inv.shops[k] = sh sh.name = npc sh.rejects = sh.rejects or {} sh.accepts = sh.accepts or {} sh.price = sh.price or {} local t = inv.types[key] -- accepts is built from CONFIRMED categories only (appraisal- or name-tagged), -- never from an inferred one, so the inference below can't feed itself. if t and t.sellCat and not t.sellCatInferred then sh.accepts[t.sellCat] = true sh.rejects[t.sellCat] = nil end silver = tonumber(silver) if silver and silver > 0 and (sh.price[key] or 0) < silver then sh.price[key] = silver end -- Learn the item's category from the sale itself (what `sell all` actually -- sold). Only safe at a SPECIALISED shop: its confirmed `accepts` is exactly -- one category AND it has refused at least one other, so an item it just -- BOUGHT can only be that one category. Sold items are real (the game said -- "You sell X"), so this carries no phantom risk, unlike guessing from what -- stayed in the bag. Marked inferred so a later per-item appraisal -- which -- names item AND category unambiguously -- still overrides it. if t and not t.sellCat then local only, n = nil, 0 for c in pairs(sh.accepts) do only = c; n = n + 1 end if n == 1 and next(sh.rejects) then t.sellCat = only t.sellCatInferred = true inv.note(string.format("inferred %s is '%s' — the only category %s buys.", t.name or key, only, sh.name or k)) end end inv.save() end
-- Where has this item fetched the most? Returns shop display name and price. function inv.bestShopFor(key) local bestN, bestP for _, sh in pairs(inv.shops or {}) do local p = sh.price and sh.price[key] if p and (not bestP or p > bestP) then bestP, bestN = p, sh.name end end return bestN, bestP end
-- Does this shop's learned profile suggest it deals in this item's category? function inv.shopAcceptsItem(key) local npc = inv.currentShopNPC if not npc then return nil end local t = inv.types[key] if not (t and t.sellCat) then return nil end local sh = inv.shops[inv.shopNPCKey(npc)] if not sh then return nil end if sh.rejects and sh.rejects[t.sellCat] then return false end if sh.accepts and sh.accepts[t.sellCat] then return true end return nil end
function inv.shopsCmd() local ks = {} for k in pairs(inv.shops or {}) do ks[#ks+1] = k end if #ks == 0 then inv.warn("no shops learned yet — run ishop somewhere."); return end table.sort(ks) cecho("\n<cyan>Shops learned so far<reset>\n") for _, k in ipairs(ks) do local sh = inv.shops[k] cecho(string.format("\n <white>%s<reset>\n", sh.name or k)) local buys, refuses = {}, {} for c in pairs(sh.accepts or {}) do buys[#buys+1] = c end for c in pairs(sh.rejects or {}) do refuses[#refuses+1] = c end table.sort(buys); table.sort(refuses) if #buys > 0 then cecho(" buys: <green>"..table.concat(buys, ", ").."<reset>\n") end if #refuses > 0 then cecho(" refuses: <yellow>"..table.concat(refuses, ", ").."<reset>\n") end local rows = {} for key, p in pairs(sh.price or {}) do rows[#rows+1] = { key = key, p = p } end table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a.p > b.p end) for i = 1, math.min(4, #rows) do local t = inv.types[rows[i].key] cecho(string.format(" %-44s <green>%d<reset> s\n", ((t and t.name) or rows[i].key):sub(1, 44), rows[i].p)) end end cecho("\n") end
-- Called when "You show the item to <NPC>." fires. function inv.onShowItem(npc) inv.currentShopNPC = npc end
-- Called when "I don't buy <cat> stuff" fires. -- Also tags the item type being valued with its sell category. function inv.onVendorRejectRaw(catRaw) local cat = catRaw:lower():gsub("%s+stuff.*",""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") -- tag the pending value item's type with this category if inv.shop and inv.shop.pendingValueKey then local t = inv.types[inv.shop.pendingValueKey] -- An appraisal names item AND category unambiguously, so it is authoritative -- and overrides a category the sale-inference only guessed (sellCatInferred). if t and (not t.sellCat or t.sellCatInferred) then t.sellCat = cat t.sellCatInferred = nil inv.note(string.format("tagged %s as category '%s'", t.name or inv.shop.pendingValueKey, cat)) inv.save() end -- For a category nobody buys, the refusal is the answer: stop showing "?" -- in the silver column and route the item on divine favour alone. This is -- NOT recorded as sell=0, because another shop may well buy the category — -- it only marks that appraisal here told us what we needed. if t and t.sellCat and inv.config.sacOnlyCats[t.sellCat] then t.noSell = true inv.save() end end -- record that this shop rejects this category local npc = inv.currentShopNPC if npc then local k = inv.shopNPCKey(npc) inv.shops[k] = inv.shops[k] or { rejects={} } if not inv.shops[k].rejects[cat] then inv.shops[k].rejects[cat] = true inv.note(string.format("%s won't buy '%s' — skipping that category here in future.", npc, cat)) inv.save() end end end
-- "<Keeper> says: I don't buy <cat>." — the plain refusal form, with no price -- and no comma (unlike "I don't buy food stuff, but a shop that does..."). It -- is the form a bulk `sell all` produces for a category the shop won't take, so -- without this the category rejection went unlearned during bulk sales. Names -- the keeper too, so capture that first, then record the rejection. function inv.onVendorSaysNoBuy(name, catRaw) if name and name ~= "" then inv.currentShopNPC = name end inv.onVendorRejectRaw(catRaw) end
-- Does the current shop reject this item's category? function inv.shopRejectsItem(key) local npc = inv.currentShopNPC if not npc then return false end local t = inv.types[key] if not t or not t.sellCat then return false end local k = inv.shopNPCKey(npc) return inv.shops[k] and inv.shops[k].rejects[t.sellCat] or false end
function inv.save() local t = { types=inv.types, loc=inv.loc, contMeta=inv.contMeta, config=inv.config, lastFavor=inv.lastFavor, shops=inv.shops, stuck=inv.stuck } pcall(table.save, getMudletHomeDir().."/icesus_inventory2.lua", t) end function inv.load() local path = getMudletHomeDir().."/icesus_inventory2.lua" if io.exists and not io.exists(path) then inv.migrate(); return end local t={}; local ok=pcall(table.load, path, t) if ok and t.types then inv.types=t.types or {}; inv.loc=t.loc or {loose={},keep={}} inv.contMeta=t.contMeta or {} if type(t.config)=="table" then for k,v in pairs(t.config) do inv.config[k]=v end end inv.lastFavor=t.lastFavor inv.shops=t.shops or {} inv.stuck=t.stuck or {} end inv.migrate() -- run migrations AFTER restoring saved config (not before) end
-- Config migrations. Must run after load() so they fix saved values, not just -- the defaults (which load would otherwise overwrite). function inv.migrate() local C = inv.config
-- Handle provenance (v4). Every handle recorded before this existed was -- confirmed by the prober, by an action, or by hand, and the record does not -- say which. Seed them all as "look", the pessimistic read: nothing is lost, -- because a type with no action-proven handle still offers its whole -- look-proven list, and the first successful get/put/sell/sacrifice promotes -- the string that worked. Claiming "act" here would instead bless exactly -- the strings this release exists to stop trusting. -- Money on the non-item or exclude list. It cannot have got there honestly -- (coins are never fetched by their own handle) and it makes iloot report a -- skip that `get all money` then contradicts on the next line. local coinsFreed = 0 for _, tbl in ipairs({ C.nonItems or {}, C.excludes or {} }) do for k in pairs(tbl) do if inv.coinInfo(k) or inv.isMoney(k) then tbl[k] = nil; coinsFreed = coinsFreed + 1 end end end if coinsFreed > 0 then inv.note(string.format("%d coin type(s) were on the non-item/exclude list — removed; " .."money is handled by 'get all money'.", coinsFreed)) inv.save() end
-- A stored volume of exactly 0 came from an `i weight` line that printed -- 0.0l because the item is smaller than the display resolution. Zero is -- rejected by every `volume > 0` test, so those types were stuck at -- "unknown" no matter how well priced. Lift them to the sub-resolution -- upper bound, same as scanItem now does on the way in. local zeroed = 0 for _, t in pairs(inv.types or {}) do if t.volume == 0 then t.volume = 50; t.volumeApprox = true; zeroed = zeroed + 1 end if t.weight == 0 then t.weight = 50 end end if zeroed > 0 then inv.note(string.format("%d type(s) had a zero volume from a 0.0l reading — " .."recorded as under 0.05l so they can be routed.", zeroed)) inv.save() end
local seeded, upgraded = 0, 0 for key, t in pairs(inv.types or {}) do local h = t.handles if h and type(h.ok) == "table" then h.src = h.src or {} for s in pairs(h.ok) do if not h.src[s] then h.src[s] = inv.HANDLE_SRC_LOOK; seeded = seeded + 1 end end -- ambiguity scopes: collapse legacy string/boolean entries into sets for s, a in pairs(h.amb or {}) do if type(a) ~= "table" then local set = {} if a == true then set.any = true else set[a] = true end h.amb[s] = set upgraded = upgraded + 1 end end h.v = 4 end end if seeded > 0 or upgraded > 0 then inv.note(string.format( "handle provenance added: %d handle(s) marked look-proven until an action confirms them" ..(upgraded > 0 and (", %d ambiguity record(s) rescoped"):format(upgraded) or ""), seeded)) inv.save() end -- Buckets keyed on a bag's description rather than its name. Nothing ever -- scanned them, so their counts only ever grew. local ghosts = {} for cont in pairs(inv.loc or {}) do if cont ~= "loose" and cont ~= "keep" and type(cont) == "string" and inv.isDescriptionKey(cont) then ghosts[#ghosts+1] = cont end end for _, cont in ipairs(ghosts) do inv.loc[cont] = nil inv.contMeta[cont] = nil inv.scannedSacks[cont] = nil end if #ghosts > 0 then inv.warn(string.format( "dropped %d container(s) keyed on a description (%s) — those counts were never real. " .."Re-scan each bag once.", #ghosts, table.concat(ghosts, ", "))) inv.save() end
-- A "non-item" that has a measured weight, a price or a sacrifice value is -- obviously an item: it got there from a failed handle, not from scenery. local freed = 0 for k in pairs(C.nonItems or {}) do local t = inv.types[k] if t and (t.sell or t.sac or t.weight or t.volume) then C.nonItems[k] = nil freed = freed + 1 end end if freed > 0 then inv.warn(string.format("%d item(s) were wrongly marked un-lootable (a failed handle, " .."not scenery) — restored.", freed)) inv.save() end
-- Container buckets keyed from a mis-parsed look command (e.g. `l "loot"`) -- held the real contents while ishop/isac read the empty real bucket. Drop -- them; one rescan rebuilds the truth. local bogus = {} for cont in pairs(inv.loc or {}) do if cont ~= "loose" and cont ~= "keep" and type(cont) == "string" and (cont:find('"') or cont:find("^l%s") or cont:find("^look%s")) then bogus[#bogus+1] = cont end end for _, cont in ipairs(bogus) do inv.loc[cont] = nil inv.contMeta[cont] = nil inv.scannedSacks[cont] = nil end if #bogus > 0 then inv.warn(string.format( "dropped %d mis-keyed container bucket(s): %s. Re-scan each bag once (l \"loot\") to rebuild.", #bogus, table.concat(bogus, ", "))) inv.save() end C.disposalSacks = C.disposalSacks or { ["loot"]=true, ["treasure"]=true } -- drop the retired "looties" bag wherever it appears local hadLooties = C.disposalSacks["looties"] ~= nil if C.bagOrder then for _, b in ipairs(C.bagOrder) do if b == "looties" then hadLooties = true end end end if C.treasureBag == "looties" then hadLooties = true end if hadLooties or not C.bagOrder then C.disposalSacks["looties"] = nil C.disposalSacks["loot"] = true C.disposalSacks["treasure"] = true C.bagOrder = { "loot", "treasure" } if C.treasureBag == "looties" or C.treasureBag == nil then C.treasureBag = "treasure" end inv.save() end -- 2026-08 rebalance. Only applied when the value is still the old default, -- so a deliberately tuned setting is never clobbered. if (C.cfgVer or 0) < 1 then local changed = {} if C.cutoffSL == 100 then C.cutoffSL = 1000; changed[#changed+1] = "cutoff 100 -> 1000 s/l" end if C.dfToSilver == 10 then C.dfToSilver = 100; changed[#changed+1] = "1 DF 10 -> 100 silver" end if C.trashDiv == 5 then C.trashDiv = 10; changed[#changed+1] = "trash line cutoff/5 -> cutoff/10" end C.cfgVer = 1 if #changed > 0 then inv.save() cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[inv]<reset> rebalanced: %s. <grey>'idf' to see the favour rate, " .."'iworth' to see what it does to what you are carrying.<reset>\n", table.concat(changed, "; "))) end end
-- 1 DF = 150 silver (was seeded at 100). Only moves a value still sitting -- at the previous default. if (C.cfgVer or 0) < 2 then if C.dfToSilver == 100 then C.dfToSilver = 150 end -- Heart favour averages up to this point were built while the altar's -- reply was used only as a veto, and a wrapped reply line can arrive as a -- bare "heart" that passes the veto for every heart type. So the numbers -- are provably contaminated across types (a guard dog heart reading 81 -- favour, then sacrificing for 3) and cannot be repaired, only discarded. -- One isac run relearns them, now attributed by what the altar names. local wiped = 0 for key, t in pairs(inv.types) do if inv.isHeart(key) and t.sac then t.sac = nil; wiped = wiped + 1 end end C.cfgVer = 2 inv.save() if wiped > 0 then inv.warn(string.format( "cleared favour averages on %d heart type(s): they were pooled across types by a " .."wrapped altar reply. One isac run relearns them correctly.", wiped)) end end
-- Hearts: one handle, known in advance. Backfill every type already on -- disk and throw away whatever the ladder guessed for them. local hearts = 0 for key in pairs(inv.types) do if inv.isHeart(key) and inv.heartSeed(key) then hearts = hearts + 1 end end if hearts > 0 then inv.save() inv.note(string.format("%d heart type(s) set to the single handle 'heart'.", hearts)) end
-- backfill food sellCat on any existing types that match the auto-tag patterns -- (types loaded from disk won't have sellCat if they were saved before v4.5) local tagged = 0 for key, t in pairs(inv.types) do if not t.sellCat and t.name then local n = t.name:lower() if n:find("heart") and n:find("bloodstained") then t.sellCat = "food"; tagged = tagged + 1 elseif n:find("%s*meat%s*") or n:find("waybread") or n:find("lard") or n:find("kidney") then t.sellCat = "food"; tagged = tagged + 1 end end end if tagged > 0 then inv.save() end end
-- ---- Char.Vitals: track favour baseline (for safety/back-compat) ----- function inv.onVitals() local v = gmcp.Char and gmcp.Char.Vitals or {} if v.dfavor then inv.lastFavor = tonumber(v.dfavor) end end
-- Mute/unmute passive tracking chatter (value learned, handle learned, scan -- reconciliation). Command echoes (iloot/ishop/ibank) and warnings are NOT -- affected. `iquiet on` = mute (verbose off); `iquiet off` = show (verbose on). function inv.quietCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if arg == "off" then inv.config.verbose = true; inv.save() cecho("\n<green>[inv]<reset> tracking messages ON.\n") elseif arg == "on" or arg == "" then inv.config.verbose = false; inv.save() cecho("\n<green>[inv]<reset> tracking messages muted (commands & warnings still show).\n") else cecho("\n<cyan>[inv]<reset> iquiet on | iquiet off\n") end end
function inv.logCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if arg == "off" then inv.config.autolog = false; inv.save(); inv.setLog(false) elseif arg == "on" or arg == "" then inv.config.autolog = true; inv.save(); inv.setLog(true) else cecho("\n<cyan>[inv]<reset> ilog on | ilog off\n") end end
-- ---- Bootstrap -------------------------------------------------------- pcall(inv.load) if inv.vitalsHandler then killAnonymousEventHandler(inv.vitalsHandler) end inv.vitalsHandler = registerAnonymousEventHandler("gmcp.Char.Vitals","inv.onVitals") if inv.saveTimer then killTimer(inv.saveTimer) end inv.saveTimer = tempTimer(120, function() pcall(inv.save) end, true)
-- Auto-start session logging (uses the format/location set in Preferences). -- startLogging(true) returns true if it actually started, nil if already on. -- Guarded so a Mudlet without the function (or already-logging) is harmless. -- Controllable via `ilog on|off`; respects inv.config.autolog (default on). if inv.config.autolog == nil then inv.config.autolog = true end function inv.setLog(on) if not startLogging then inv.warn("this Mudlet has no startLogging()."); return end local ok, changed = pcall(startLogging, on and true or false) if not ok then return end if on then cecho(changed and "\n<green>[inv]<reset> session logging started.\n" or "\n<grey>[inv]<reset> logging already on.\n") else cecho("\n<yellow>[inv]<reset> session logging stopped.\n") end end if inv.config.autolog then pcall(inv.setLog, true) end
cecho("\n<green>[Icesus inventory v2 loaded]<reset> iloot | iinv | iworth | ishop | isac | ibank | igroup | icont | iclean | idf | ihandle | ilog | iquiet\n")
-- ---- Item classification (disposition) ------------------------------- -- The value metric is silver-equivalent per litre, where 1 favour = dfToSilver. -- Returns disposition and the metric value: -- "unknown" : no sell AND no sac data -> must be valued first -- "trash" : has >=1 sample and best metric <= cutoff/trashDiv -- "leave" : established (n>=estN on best route) and metric < cutoff -- "sell" : keep, sell route best (metric >= cutoff) -- "sac" : keep, sacrifice route best (metric >= cutoff) -- Silver value of one coin of a given denomination. inv.coinSilver = { silver = 1, gold = 10, platinum = 100, mithril = 1000 }
-- ---- Coin density ----------------------------------------------------- -- Coins were the one thing exempt from the rule the package applies to -- everything else: coinInfo short-circuits classify to "sell" before any -- cutoff test, so every denomination was always taken. Measured from `i -- weight`, silver runs about 500 silver per litre — HALF the default 1000 s/l -- keep line, and the only denomination that fails it. Nearly 10,000 silver -- coins is 19.8 litres, an eighth of a full pack, for less value than the same -- space in ordinary loot. -- -- Millilitres per coin. Seeded from measurement (all denominations are ~1ml -- except silver at ~2ml) and refined from every `i weight` line that shows a -- count and a bulk, so these self-correct if the game differs. inv.coinVol = inv.coinVol or { silver = 2.0, gold = 1.0, platinum = 1.05, mithril = 1.0 }
-- Silver-per-litre for one denomination. function inv.coinPerLitre(denom) local v = inv.coinSilver[denom] local ml = inv.coinVol[denom] if not (v and ml and ml > 0) then return nil end return v * 1000 / ml end
-- Is this denomination worth the space it displaces? function inv.coinWorthTaking(denom) if not inv.config.coinCutoff then return true end -- feature off: take all local sl = inv.coinPerLitre(denom) if not sl then return true end -- unmeasured: take it return sl >= (inv.config.cutoffSL or 1000) end
-- Learn ml-per-coin from an `i weight` line like "19.8kg 19.8l 9892 silver coins". function inv.coinLearnVol(key, volL) local denom, count = inv.coinInfo(key) if not (denom and count and count > 0 and volL and volL > 0) then return end local ml = (volL * 1000) / count inv.coinVol[denom] = inv.blend(inv.coinVol[denom], ml) end
-- If `key` is a coin pile, return its denomination and count (count may be nil -- for vague piles like "pile of gold coins"). Else nil. function inv.coinInfo(key) local count, denom = key:match("^(%d+)%s+(%a+)%s+coins?$") if denom and inv.coinSilver[denom] then return denom, tonumber(count) end denom = key:match("([a-z]+)%s+coins?$") if denom and inv.coinSilver[denom] then return denom, nil end return nil end
-- Should we spend one pickup to find out what this type is worth at the altar? -- -- Across every type that has both numbers, divine favour is a near-constant -- fraction of silver — measured on this profile at 17.3 to 21.6 silver per -- favour, median 18. The exception is the class the shop prices at ZERO: -- hearts carry 13-88 favour and no silver at all, so their ratio is infinite -- and no silver figure predicts it. That is the whole argument for measuring -- rather than assuming: the items where favour matters most are precisely the -- ones where the silver column says nothing. -- -- So: one instance, once, for a type we have never held. After that we own -- stock to learn from and the lesson is paid for. Bounded by construction — -- holding one makes the next copy skippable, and a measured type never -- returns here. function inv.dfWorthLearning(key) local t = inv.types[key] if not t then return true end -- unknown everything: worth a look if t.sac then return false end -- already priced at an altar if t.noSac then return false end -- the altar refuses it; nothing to learn if inv.config.excludes[key] then return false end if inv.locCount("loose", key) > 0 or inv.locCount("keep", key) > 0 then return false end if #inv.containersWith(key) > 0 then return false end return true end
function inv.classify(key) local t = inv.types[key] if not t then -- a coin type we haven't stored yet still classifies as keep/sell if inv.coinInfo(key) then return "sell", nil end return "unknown", nil end local C = inv.config
-- Coins: known value, never appraised. Always worth keeping (route "sell" -- only in the sense that they hold silver value); iloot/shop treat as keep. local cd = inv.coinInfo(key) if cd then return "sell", nil end
local voll = t.volume and t.volume > 0 and (t.volume/1000) or nil local sell = t.sell and t.sell.avg or nil local sac = t.sac and t.sac.avg or nil local sellN = t.sell and t.sell.n or 0 local sacN = t.sac and t.sac.n or 0
-- For sac-only categories (e.g. food/hearts), sell value is irrelevant — -- these items are never sold, only sacrificed. Evaluate purely on sac data. if t.sellCat and C.sacOnlyCats and C.sacOnlyCats[t.sellCat] then if not sac then return "unknown", nil end -- no sac data yet → take it, sacrifice to learn local sacEq = sac * C.dfToSilver if not voll then if sacEq <= (C.cutoffSL / C.trashDiv) and sacN >= 1 then return "trash", sacEq end return "unknown", sacEq end local metric = sacEq / voll if metric <= (C.cutoffSL / C.trashDiv) and sacN >= 1 then return "trash", metric elseif metric >= C.cutoffSL then return "sac", metric else return "leave", metric end end
if not sell and not sac then return "unknown", nil end
-- Sell data only, divine favour never measured. A low silver price is NOT -- evidence of low altar worth: an item the shop appraises at ZERO is exactly -- the one whose only remaining value can be divine favour. The old gate here -- trashed on the sell figure alone after a single sample, so "Piece of -- spider's skin [0 s]" was declared trash and became invisible to both ishop -- and isac — it could never acquire a DF number, so it could never be -- reclassified out of trash. Spend exactly one at the altar to get that -- number; the both-known branch below then decides for good. -- -- Two sell-only trash calls are still safe without a DF reading: -- * the altar refuses the type outright (noSac) — there is nothing to learn -- * an ESTABLISHED cheap-but-nonzero price (n >= estN), which is the -- "clearly junk, don't haul it across the map" case the old gate meant -- to catch. Zero never qualifies: zero is the altar's signal. if sell and not sac then local metric = voll and (sell / voll) or sell
-- The altar refuses this type outright ("not worthy of sacrifice", or it -- is on the keeplist), so a DF number is unobtainable and waiting for one -- is a deadlock. Decide on the sell figure alone, exactly as the -- both-known branch below would with sell as the only route. NOTE: this -- must NOT collapse to "trash" — an altar refusing a 3900-silver skin -- says nothing about its sale price. if t.noSac then if metric <= (C.cutoffSL / C.trashDiv) and sellN >= 1 then return "trash", metric end if not voll then return "unknown", metric end -- needs weighing to place if metric >= C.cutoffSL then return "sell", metric end if sellN >= C.estN then return "leave", metric end return "sell", metric -- not established yet end
if sell > 0 and metric <= (C.cutoffSL / C.trashDiv) and sellN >= C.estN then return "trash", metric end return "sac", metric -- learning sacrifice: measure DF, then reclassify end
-- silver-equivalents local sellEq = sell local sacEq = sac and (sac * C.dfToSilver) or nil
-- Sell-only is already handled above and always returns, so there is no -- second sell-only branch here any more. There used to be one, with a -- STRICTER threshold (n >= estN rather than n >= 1) — it was unreachable, -- and having two disagreeing copies of the same rule is how the loose one -- survived. That rule now lives once, in the block above. if not sellEq and sacEq then return "unknown", sacEq -- defer: value at shop to learn silver, then reclassify end
-- best route by silver-equiv (both known) local bestEq, route, bestN if sellEq >= sacEq then bestEq,route,bestN = sellEq,"sell",sellN else bestEq,route,bestN = sacEq,"sac",sacN end
-- metric is per-litre if we know volume; if not, treat raw value as metric -- (can't compute per-litre yet -> still needs weighing, treat as unknown vol) if not voll then -- value known but volume unknown: needs weighing before keep/leave call. -- but we CAN already call trash if absurdly cheap in absolute terms. if bestEq <= (C.cutoffSL / C.trashDiv) and bestN >= 1 then return "trash", bestEq end return "unknown", bestEq -- needs weighing to place end
local metric = bestEq / voll -- silver-equiv per litre -- estN, not 1: `trash` is permanent, and the trash line moved with the -- cutoff. One unlucky appraisal should not blacklist a type for good. if metric <= (C.cutoffSL / C.trashDiv) and bestN >= C.estN then return "trash", metric elseif metric >= C.cutoffSL then return route, metric else -- below cutoff: "leave" only if established; else still worth a look if bestN >= C.estN then return "leave", metric else return route, metric end -- not yet established -> still grab to refine end end
-- Disposal routing for ishop/isac. classify()'s keep/trash/leave verdicts are -- a PICK-UP rule -- "should iloot grab this off the floor?" -- and the cutoff -- that drives them is measured per litre against the value of the pack space it -- would cost. That is the wrong question for something already sitting in a -- disposal bag or loose: it is here to LEAVE, not to be carried. So disposal -- ignores the cutoff and asks only "what is the way out?". -- -- FAVOUR-FIRST (9.14, config.favourFirst, default on). The old rule was "any -- sale value at all -> sell", which sold an item on its silver figure while its -- divine favour was still UNMEASURED — the very thing classify() refuses to do -- on the other side of the ledger, and a contradiction with "favour is the -- scarce side". So a 936-silver iron club sold blind, its favour never learned, -- when the altar might have valued it higher. Now: -- * favour not measured, altar not refused -> sac (learn favour ONCE first; -- a learning sacrifice costs one item, not the stack — the rest route on -- the next pass once the reading is in). Exception: a sale price at/below -- `sellBlindMaxSilver` (default 0 -> never) sells without the ceremony. -- * both measured -> the better silver-equivalent -- wins (sac when sac*dfToSilver > sell), exactly like classify(). -- * favour measured, price not -> learn the price (or altar if -- favour is the only positive value). -- * altar refused the type (noSac) -> decide on silver alone. -- * measured worth of zero on both sides -> drop. -- Set config.favourFirst = false to restore the pre-9.14 sell-leaning rule. function inv.disposeRoute(key) local t = inv.types[key] if not t then return "unknown" end if inv.coinInfo(key) then return "coin" end -- ibank handles money local C = inv.config local sell = t.sell and t.sell.avg local sac = t.sac and t.sac.avg local sellKnown, sacKnown = (t.sell ~= nil), (t.sac ~= nil) local sacOnly = t.sellCat and C.sacOnlyCats and C.sacOnlyCats[t.sellCat] local function pos(x) return x and x > 0 end
-- Sac-only category (food, hearts): never sold, so silver is irrelevant. if sacOnly then if not sacKnown then return "unknown" end -- learn favour at the altar if pos(sac) then return "sac" end return "drop" -- measured 0 favour, unsellable end
if not sellKnown and not sacKnown then return "unknown" end
if not C.favourFirst then -- Legacy sell-leaning disposal (pre-9.14). if pos(sell) then return "sell" end if pos(sac) then return "sac" end if not sacKnown then return "sac" end -- "[0 s| ? df]" -> altar once if not sellKnown then return "unknown" end return "drop" end
-- Favour not measured yet: never conclude "sell" while the altar side is -- unmeasured. Learn favour first with a single sacrifice, unless the number -- is unobtainable (noSac) or the price is cheap enough to sell blind. if not sacKnown then local blind = t.noSac or (pos(sell) and sell <= (C.sellBlindMaxSilver or 0)) if blind then if pos(sell) then return "sell" end if sellKnown then return "drop" end -- price measured 0, altar refuses -> junk return "unknown" -- price not yet known end return "sac" -- "[N s| ? df]" -> altar once to learn favour end
-- Favour is known. If the price is not, learn it (or altar if favour-only). if not sellKnown then if pos(sac) then return "sac" end return "unknown" -- favour measured 0, price unknown -> appraise end
-- Both measured: the better silver-equivalent wins, exactly like classify(). local sellEq = sell or 0 local sacEq = (sac or 0) * (C.dfToSilver or 100) if pos(sac) and sacEq > sellEq then return "sac" end if pos(sell) then return "sell" end if pos(sac) then return "sac" end return "drop" -- both measured zero end
-- ---- Paced bag-to-bag mover (staging) -------------------------------- -- Moving an item between bags is a get followed by a put, and `put` only sees -- LOOSE inventory, so the two are dependent exactly like a shop cycle: fired as -- a burst, a bad handle files the wrong object away (this is how a sack of lamp -- oil once landed in the disposal bag). So it is a queue, one item at a time, -- advanced by the get/put echoes with an 8s backstop. Map-keeping is left to -- the existing "Action get"/"Action put" triggers (onGetEcho/evPut); this only -- sequences the commands and, for a bagged source, chains get -> put. inv.moveQueue = inv.moveQueue or {} inv.moveInFlight = nil inv.moveTimer = nil inv.moveOnDone = nil inv.moveStats = nil
function inv.moveBusy() return inv.moveInFlight ~= nil or #inv.moveQueue > 0 end function inv.moveEcho(c) cecho("\n<grey>[istage]<reset> <cyan>"..c.."<reset>") end
function inv.moveClearTimer() if inv.moveTimer then killTimer(inv.moveTimer); inv.moveTimer = nil end end
function inv.moveEnqueue(key, src, dst, count) for _ = 1, (count or 1) do inv.moveQueue[#inv.moveQueue+1] = { key = key, src = src, dst = dst } end end
function inv.moveArmTimeout(e, why) inv.moveTimer = tempTimer(8, function() if inv.moveInFlight == e then inv.moveFail(e, why or "no reply") inv.deferStep(inv.moveSendNext) end end) end
function inv.moveFail(e, why) inv.moveInFlight = nil inv.moveClearTimer() if inv.moveStats then inv.moveStats.failed = (inv.moveStats.failed or 0) + 1 end inv.warn(string.format("could not stage %s (%s).", (inv.types[e.key] and inv.types[e.key].name) or e.key, why or "?")) end
-- Send the put that finishes a move; the item is loose by now. function inv.movePut(e) local dstName = inv.sackName(e.dst) local h = e.handle or inv.shortestHandle("loose", e.key) or inv.handleShortest(e.key) or e.key h = inv.safeHandle(h, e.key, "loose", true) or h e.phase = "put" table.insert(inv.pendingPuts, { key = e.key, sackKey = e.dst }) local cmd = string.format('put %s in "%s"', h, dstName) inv.moveEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) inv.moveClearTimer() inv.moveArmTimeout(e, "put timed out") end
function inv.moveSendNext() inv.moveClearTimer() local e = table.remove(inv.moveQueue, 1) if not e then inv.moveInFlight = nil local cb = inv.moveOnDone; inv.moveOnDone = nil local s = inv.moveStats; inv.moveStats = nil if s and (s.moved > 0 or s.failed > 0) then cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[istage]<reset> staged <green>%d<reset> item(s) into \"%s\"%s.\n", s.moved, s.dst or (inv.config.sacStageBag or "treasure"), s.failed > 0 and string.format(", <yellow>%d<reset> could not be moved", s.failed) or "")) end inv.save() if cb then cb() end return end inv.moveInFlight = e if e.src == "loose" or e.src == "keep" then inv.movePut(e) -- already loose: one put else -- Bag -> bag in ONE command: `get <h> from "<src>" to "<dst>"` (bagRef -- gives the `<h> from "<src>"` part). Half the commands of get-then-put. local ref, hnd = inv.bagRef(e.src, e.key) if not ref then inv.moveFail(e, "no fetch handle") return inv.deferStep(inv.moveSendNext) end e.phase = "get2bag"; e.handle = hnd table.insert(inv.pendingPuts, { key = e.key, sackKey = e.dst }) -- resolves the dst desc local cmd = string.format('get %s to "%s"', ref, inv.sackName(e.dst)) inv.moveEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) inv.moveArmTimeout(e, "move timed out") end end
-- Hooked from the tail of onGetEcho: the fetched item is loose, send the put. function inv.moveOnGet(keys) local e = inv.moveInFlight if not e then return end local hit = false for _, k in ipairs(keys or {}) do if k == e.key then hit = true; break end end if not hit then return end if e.phase == "get2bag" then -- onGetEcho already moved it src->dst in the map; the move is done. The get -- also just moved a real object with e.handle, which is the only proof that -- promotes a handle to action-proven -- so a working bag handle stops being -- a mere show-id candidate and shadows the ones still unproven. if e.key and e.handle then inv.handleRecordOk(e.key, e.handle) end inv.moveInFlight = nil inv.moveClearTimer() if inv.moveStats then inv.moveStats.moved = (inv.moveStats.moved or 0) + 1 end inv.deferStep(inv.moveSendNext) elseif e.phase == "get" then if e.key and e.handle then inv.handleRecordOk(e.key, e.handle) end inv.movePut(e) end end
-- Hooked from the tail of evPut: the move completed. function inv.moveOnPut(key) local e = inv.moveInFlight if not (e and e.phase == "put" and key == e.key) then return end inv.moveInFlight = nil inv.moveClearTimer() if inv.moveStats then inv.moveStats.moved = (inv.moveStats.moved or 0) + 1 end inv.deferStep(inv.moveSendNext) end
-- Hooked from onNoSuchHandle: the game refused the handle the staging mover just -- sent -- "You see no 'X' around here.", the SAME string a bag get returns -- (`get axe from "loot" to "treasure"` -> "You see no 'axe' around here."). The -- mover otherwise only had the 8s timeout, so a bad bag handle stalled the whole -- staging run instead of ruling itself out and retrying. This mirrors -- lootHandleRefused: demote the refused handle for the type we deliberately -- tried to move (never the item -- the get-echo attribution rule), then re-send -- the move with the next candidate down the ladder, bounded by HANDLE_RETRIES. -- Because handleFailedAction moves the refused string to `bad`, the rebuilt -- fetch in moveSendNext picks a fresh handle on its own; the tries counter is -- the backstop for a handle that cannot be demoted (a heart's `heart`). function inv.moveHandleRefused(handle) local e = inv.moveInFlight if not e or not handle then return false end if e.phase ~= "get2bag" and e.phase ~= "get" then return false end -- Only claim the refusal if it names the string we actually sent; a stray -- "You see no" from something else must not derail an in-flight move. if not (e.handle and e.handle:lower() == handle:lower()) then return false end inv.moveClearTimer() inv.moveInFlight = nil
-- CASE 1 -- the handle is ACTION-PROVEN. A handle a real verb has already moved -- the item with does not stop naming it, so "You see no X" means the item is -- NOT in e.src: the map entry is a stale duplicate (the item was staged/sold -- but a phantom copy lingered in a sale bag). Prune that phantom and move on -- WITHOUT demoting -- demoting a good handle here is what destroyed the real -- copy's handles in play (a scimitar/half plate sat fine in "treasure" yet -- showed every handle "refused", because failed `get ... from "loot"` on the -- loot phantom marked those very handles bad, then the altar could not reach -- the real one either). if inv.handleActProven(e.key, e.handle) then if e.src and e.src ~= "loose" and e.src ~= "keep" then inv.locRemove(e.src, e.key, 1) end inv.moveEcho(string.format("%s is not in \"%s\" -- pruned a stale entry (handle '%s' is fine).", (inv.types[e.key] and inv.types[e.key].name) or e.key, tostring(e.src), e.handle)) if inv.moveStats then inv.moveStats.pruned = (inv.moveStats.pruned or 0) + 1 end inv.deferStep(inv.moveSendNext) return true end
-- CASE 2 -- an UNPROVEN (show-id/look) candidate. It could be a bad guess OR -- the item is gone; demote it and try the next candidate down the ladder, -- bounded by retries. if e.key then inv.handleFailedAction(e.key, e.handle, "get") end e.tried = e.tried or {} e.tried[e.handle] = true e.tries = (e.tries or 0) + 1 if e.tries <= inv.HANDLE_RETRIES and inv.nextHandleAfter(e.key, e.tried) then -- back to the FRONT of the queue with the same src/dst, carrying the tried -- set and counter so we keep descending rather than restart at the top. table.insert(inv.moveQueue, 1, { key = e.key, src = e.src, dst = e.dst, tried = e.tried, tries = e.tries }) inv.moveEcho(string.format("'%s' did not move %s -- retrying with another handle...", e.handle, (inv.types[e.key] and inv.types[e.key].name) or e.key)) inv.deferStep(inv.moveSendNext) return true end inv.moveFail(e, "no working handle") if e.key then inv.markStuck(e.key, string.format("move failed, last tried '%s'", tostring(e.handle)), inv.ambContext(e.src)) end inv.deferStep(inv.moveSendNext) return true end
-- ---- Staging altar-bound items into the stage bag -------------------- -- What belongs in the stage bag for a bulk sacrifice: anything the altar is the -- way out for (favour-only, favour-better, or still to be learned), not already -- there, and not one the altar has refused (noSac). -- `saleBagsOnly` (ishop context): stage only what a `sell all` would otherwise -- sell by mistake — the sac-routed items sitting in an actual SALE bag. Loose -- and keep items are never bulk-sold, so moving them to treasure at a shop is -- pure churn (21 loose skins hauled bag-to-bag one at a time, which is what -- stalled and timed out); they are staged at the altar by isac instead. -- `shopRisk` (ishop context): stage out only the sac-routed items the CURRENT -- shop could actually buy -- i.e. the ones `sell all` would wrongly sell. A -- sac-only category (food) or a category this keeper is known to refuse is not -- at risk, so it stays put. That is the "only pull the weapons at a weapon -- shop" minimisation. function inv.sacStagingList(saleBagsOnly, shopRisk) local dst = inv.config.sacStageBag or "treasure" local out = {} for _, e in ipairs(inv.disposablesList()) do local looseish = (e.container == "loose" or e.container == "keep") if e.container ~= dst and not inv.coinInfo(e.key) and not (saleBagsOnly and looseish) then local t = inv.types[e.key] local route = inv.disposeRoute(e.key) local sacOnly = t and t.sellCat and inv.config.sacOnlyCats and inv.config.sacOnlyCats[t.sellCat] local wantsAltar = route == "sac" or (route == "unknown" and sacOnly) local atRisk = (not shopRisk) or (not sacOnly and not inv.shopRejectsItem(e.key)) if wantsAltar and atRisk and not (t and t.noSac) then out[#out+1] = e end end end return out end
function inv.stageSacItems(onDone, saleBagsOnly, shopRisk) if inv.moveBusy() then inv.warn("a staging move is already in progress.") if onDone then onDone() end return end local list = inv.sacStagingList(saleBagsOnly, shopRisk) if #list == 0 then if onDone then onDone() end; return end local dst = inv.config.sacStageBag or "treasure" inv.moveQueue = {} local n = 0 for _, e in ipairs(list) do inv.moveEnqueue(e.key, e.container, dst, e.count or 1) n = n + (e.count or 1) end inv.moveStats = { moved = 0, failed = 0, dst = dst } inv.moveOnDone = onDone cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[istage]<reset> staging %d altar-bound item(s) into \"%s\" for sacrifice...\n", n, dst)) inv.moveSendNext() end
-- ---- Multi-item action line parsing ---------------------------------- -- Two list formats occur: -- "the A, the B and the C" (get-to-bag echoes; "the" separators) -- "5 gold coins, X and Y" (kill drops; bare comma separators, no "the") -- Prefer splitting on ", the "/" and the " (unambiguous, safe for names that -- contain "and" like "flint and steel"). Only when the line has NO "the" -- separators do we fall back to bare ", "/" and " splitting. function inv.splitItemList(s) s = s:gsub("%s+", " "):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") local hasThe = s:find(", the ") or s:find(" and the ") or s:find("^the ") local body = s:gsub("^the ", "") if hasThe then body = body:gsub(" and the ", "\1"):gsub(", the ", "\1") else body = body:gsub(" and ", "\1"):gsub(", ", "\1") end local out = {} for piece in (body.."\1"):gmatch("(.-)\1") do if piece ~= "" then piece = piece:gsub("^the ", "") local n = tonumber(piece:match("^(%d+)%s*x%s")) or 1 local nm = piece:gsub("^%d+%s*x%s+","") out[#out+1] = { name = nm, qty = n } end end return out end
-- Apply a batched "You get ... to a <sack>." line to the location map. function inv.onGetEcho(listText, toSack, fromSack) local items = inv.splitItemList(listText) -- verification (conservative): only when a single item was fetched and we -- have a pending deliberate get awaiting confirmation. if inv.pendingGet and #items == 1 then inv.verifyGotItem(items[1].name) end -- A staging move in flight (`get X to "bag"` or the get half of get->put) -- echoes the single item we asked to move. Its echoed name can differ from -- the tracked type key -- an item identified/renamed since we stored it, or -- any case where the get-echo form and the stored name normalise differently -- -- so inv.key(it.name) resolves to a stranger key. Attribute the move to the -- key we deliberately sent (moveInFlight.key), exactly as the sac pipeline -- attributes by position. Without this the item is neither removed from the -- source bag nor filed in the stage bag, so it stays put and every later -- ishop re-stages it -- the two-shop re-staging report. Guarded to the pure -- staging case: no active shop fetch (that path needs the real echo key to -- detect handle collisions). local stageMoveKey = nil if inv.moveInFlight and #items == 1 and (inv.moveInFlight.phase == "get2bag" or inv.moveInFlight.phase == "get") and not (inv.shopJob and inv.shopJob.getCmd and not inv.shopJob.heldKey) then stageMoveKey = inv.moveInFlight.key end for _, it in ipairs(items) do local key = stageMoveKey or inv.key(it.name) if key then local ht = inv.types[key] if ht then ht.seen = true end -- The get worked, so the string we sent moved a real object: promote it -- from look-proven to action-proven, and release the weigh gate. if inv.loot.active then inv.lootGetSucceeded(key) end -- A shop fetch in flight: this echo is the ONLY place the game says -- which object the handle actually reached. Record it for onValueRaw, -- and if it is not what we asked for, the handle collided inside the -- bag — which is how one `get stone cap` fetched the soft leather cap -- twice while the heavy cloth cap was never appraised at all. local sj = inv.shopJob if sj and sj.getCmd and not sj.heldKey then sj.heldKey = key if sj.key and key ~= sj.key then -- The handle reached a different type in the same bag. That is what -- the positional index is for, and the stow order just told us its -- guess was wrong — so correct the map from the evidence rather -- than keep believing it: whatever position we asked for, THIS is -- the type sitting there. inv.noteIndexMiss(sj) inv.handleRecordAmb(sj.key, sj.handle, (sj.container and sj.container ~= "loose") and ("container:"..sj.container) or "inventory") inv.shopSay(string.format( "'%s' fetched %s, not %s — %s", tostring(sj.ref or sj.handle), (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key, (inv.types[sj.key] and inv.types[sj.key].name) or sj.key, sj.container and "trying the next position." or "marked ambiguous.")) -- Both types' queued commands were built from the order we have just -- corrected, so both need rebuilding — the one we missed and the one -- we hit. inv.requeueHandle(sj.key) inv.requeueHandle(key) -- Re-queue the type we failed to reach, with a fresh reference off -- the corrected order, so it is appraised in THIS run rather than -- waiting for the next one. Bounded, because a bag whose order -- cannot be pinned down must not loop. -- Re-queue the type we failed to reach so it is still appraised in -- THIS run. No reference is built here on purpose: the item we just -- pulled has to go back first, and it returns to the front of the -- stow order, so any index computed now would be describing the -- wrong bag. shopValueNext builds it at send time. Bounded, because -- a bag whose order cannot be pinned down must not loop. local tries = (sj.idxTries or 0) + 1 if sj.container and tries <= 2 then inv.shopQueue[#inv.shopQueue+1] = { key = sj.key, container = sj.container, needsFetch = true, idxTries = tries, } end end end for _=1, it.qty do if toSack then -- A one-command bag->bag get ("...from a leather sack to a huge -- sack") carries BOTH a from and a to; remove it from the source -- before adding to the destination, or the map double-counts. The -- echo's `from a X` capture is polluted by the trailing `to a Y`, so -- trust the in-flight move's known source when there is one. if fromSack and not inv.isCorpseText(fromSack) then local fk if inv.moveInFlight and inv.moveInFlight.key == key then fk = inv.moveInFlight.src else fk = inv.sackKeyFromText(fromSack) if not inv.contMeta[fk] then for cont in pairs(inv.loc) do if cont ~= "loose" and cont ~= "keep" and inv.locCount(cont, key) > 0 then fk = cont; break end end end end if fk and fk ~= "loose" and fk ~= "keep" then inv.locRemove(fk, key, 1) end end local descKey = inv.sackKeyFromText(toSack) local sackKey = inv.resolveSackText(toSack) -- The echo names the sack by description, never by the name you gave -- it, so a hand-typed `get all to loot` used to file the item under -- "huge leather sack". Prefer a queued put, then a learned -- description->name mapping, and learn the mapping when we can. local resolved = inv.contMeta[sackKey] ~= nil if not resolved then for i, p in ipairs(inv.pendingPuts) do if p.key == key then sackKey = p.sackKey; table.remove(inv.pendingPuts, i) if descKey and descKey ~= sackKey then inv.contDesc[descKey] = sackKey end resolved = true break end end end if resolved and not inv.isDescriptionKey(sackKey) then inv.locAdd(sackKey, key) else -- It went into SOME bag, but the echo only gave a description that -- fits more than one. Recording a guess is worse than recording -- nothing: flag the candidates for a rescan and move on. inv.markBagsDirty(descKey) inv.note(string.format("%s went into a bag the echo did not name — will re-scan.", (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key)) end elseif inv.isCorpseText(fromSack) then -- from a corpse: a new arrival, and we know who dropped it inv.locAdd("loose", key) inv.noteOrigin(key) if inv.loot.active and inv.loot.tookLoose then inv.loot.tookLoose[key] = (inv.loot.tookLoose[key] or 0) + 1 end elseif fromSack then local fk = inv.sackKeyFromText(fromSack) -- for "from" case: if unnamed, find it in any container if not inv.contMeta[fk] then for cont, _ in pairs(inv.loc) do if inv.locCount(cont, key) > 0 then fk = cont; break end end end inv.locMove(fk, "loose", key) else inv.locAdd("loose", key) -- only count loose arrivals during an active loot run toward tookLoose if inv.loot.active and inv.loot.tookLoose then inv.loot.tookLoose[key] = (inv.loot.tookLoose[key] or 0) + 1 end end end end end inv.loot.pendingLooseKey = nil -- staging mover: the fetched item is now loose, so its put can go out if inv.moveInFlight then local ks = {} for _, it in ipairs(items) do local k = stageMoveKey or inv.key(it.name); if k then ks[#ks+1] = k end end inv.moveOnGet(ks) end end
function inv.evGetBatch(listText, toSack, fromSack) for _, it in ipairs(inv.splitItemList(listText)) do local key = inv.key(it.name) if key then for _=1, it.qty do if toSack then inv.locAdd(inv.sackKeyFromText(toSack), key) elseif inv.isCorpseText(fromSack) then inv.locAdd("loose", key); inv.noteOrigin(key) elseif fromSack then inv.locMove(inv.sackKeyFromText(fromSack),"loose",key) else inv.locAdd("loose", key) end end end end end
-- ============================================================ -- Auto-loot engine: iloot -- ============================================================ -- Phases driven by game responses: -- 1. scan room -> classify each item -- 2. known-keep items: get straight to a bag (fill order, volume-predicted) -- unknown items: get to loose for weighing -- 3. if anything was taken loose to weigh, auto-fire `i weight` -- 4. on i-weight completion, re-classify the now-weighed loose items and -- sort them to bags (or drop if they weighed in as trash & were taken -- this run) -- Every command is echoed. Fullness predicted from volume; the game's -- "is full"/"no room for"/"too heavy" lines are caught as backstops.
inv.loot = { active=false, tookLoose={}, log={}, issued={} }
-- Print why each skipped item was skipped, grouped by cause. One line per -- reason, naming the items, so "leaving 4" is auditable instead of asserted. function inv.lootWhy() local why = inv.loot.why if not why or next(why) == nil then return end local reasons = {} for r in pairs(why) do reasons[#reasons+1] = r end table.sort(reasons) for _, r in ipairs(reasons) do local names = why[r] table.sort(names) cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[iloot] %s:<reset> %s", r, table.concat(names, ", "))) end -- No literal angle brackets in a cecho string: cecho reads them as colour -- tags, so a placeholder like <name> is swallowed or errors. if why["learned non-item"] then cecho("\n<grey>[iloot] a non-item is a guess from an earlier refusal — undo it with<reset> " .."<cyan>iloot include NAME<reset>") end local heavy = false for r in pairs(why) do if r:find("heav", 1, true) then heavy = true end end if heavy and inv.carry and inv.carry.maxKg then cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[iloot] carrying %.1f of %.1fkg — weight refusals are re-tested " .."once you are lighter.<reset>", inv.carry.kg or 0, inv.carry.maxKg)) end end
function inv.lootEcho(cmd) cecho("\n<grey>[iloot]<reset> <cyan>"..cmd.."<reset>") end function inv.lootSay(m) cecho("\n<grey>[iloot]<reset> "..m) end
-- Estimated remaining volume capacity of a bag (ml). Uses the bag's own -- measured volume as a proxy for current fill is NOT possible; instead we track -- the sum of contained item volumes we know about. Returns a generous estimate; -- the "no room" message is the real backstop. function inv.bagFreeVol(sackKey) local maxV = inv.config.maxVol or 120500 -- character cap as a ceiling proxy -- sum known volumes of contents local used = 0 for _, key in ipairs(inv.loc[sackKey] or {}) do local t = inv.types[key] if t and t.volume then used = used + t.volume end end -- a sack's own capacity isn't directly known; assume large. We mainly rely on -- the refusal backstop, so just return a positive number unless clearly huge. return math.max(0, (inv.bagCapVol and inv.bagCapVol[sackKey] or 999999) - used) end
-- Choose the first bag in fill order that (predictively) has room and isn't -- known-full. Returns sackKey or nil. function inv.pickBag(itemVol) for _, sack in ipairs(inv.config.bagOrder) do if not (inv.bagFull and inv.bagFull[sack]) then local free = inv.bagFreeVol(sack) if not itemVol or free >= itemVol then return sack end end end -- nothing predicted free: still return the first not-known-full bag and let -- the refusal backstop handle it for _, sack in ipairs(inv.config.bagOrder) do if not (inv.bagFull and inv.bagFull[sack]) then return sack end end return nil end
inv.bagFull = inv.bagFull or {} -- sackKey -> true when game said it's full
-- Issue: get one <item> straight into the chosen bag. -- -- Attribution is inv.loot.issued's job and ONLY its job. 8.0 removed the old -- `not inv.handleKnown(key)` guard on inv.verifyArm — right idea, wrong layer: -- inv.pendingGet is a single slot, so in a ten-item burst every get overwrote -- the last and the FIRST echo was matched against the LAST handle sent. That -- produced "'tin bracers' reached the wrong item (Bloodstone)" and, worse, -- filed `tin bracers` as an action-proven handle FOR the Bloodstone. The -- issued queue correlates by name and by send order, which is what the single -- slot could never do, so the loot path no longer arms verifyArm at all. function inv.lootGetToBag(name, tried) local key = inv.key(name) local sack = inv.pickBag(inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].volume or nil) if not sack then inv.lootSay("<yellow>all bags full — leaving "..name.." in room<reset>"); return end inv.loot.lastBag = sack inv.loot.lastItem = name local handle = inv.shortestRoomHandle(name, tried) if not inv.lootIssue{ key=key, name=name, handle=handle, dest=sack, tried=tried } then return end table.insert(inv.pendingPuts, {key=key, sackKey=sack}) local cmd = string.format('get %s to "%s"', handle, sack) inv.lootEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) end
-- Issue: get one <item> to loose (for weighing). function inv.lootGetLoose(name, tried) local key = inv.key(name) local handle = inv.shortestRoomHandle(name, tried) if not inv.lootIssue{ key=key, name=name, handle=handle, dest="loose", tried=tried } then return end local cmd = "get " .. handle inv.lootEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) -- Track tookLoose from the actual "You get" echo (onGetEcho), not the attempt, -- so failed gets (too heavy, cannot move) don't pollute the sort list. -- We register the expected key so onGetEcho can attribute the success. inv.loot.pendingLooseKey = key end
-- Pick the handle to use for a room item: the shortest one that is -- unambiguous among the OTHER items visible in the room. Proven handles are -- used when we have them; otherwise we walk the unproven ladder as before. -- Never returns the full display name (the game cannot parse it). -- -- `tried` is the set of strings this run has already had refused for this -- item, so a retry walks DOWN the ladder instead of re-sending the loser. function inv.shortestRoomHandle(name, tried) local key = inv.key(name) if not key then return name end tried = tried or {}
local others = {} if inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.lines then for _, it in ipairs(inv.roomScan.lines) do local k = inv.key(it.name) if k and k ~= key then others[#others+1] = k end end end local function clashes(cand) local pat = "%f[%a]"..cand:gsub("(%W)","%%%1").."%f[%A]" for _, ok in ipairs(others) do if ok == cand or ok:find(pat) then return true end end return false end -- A handle containing a comma is read as a multi-target separator; swap in -- a positional index instead (index 1 = most recently arrived). local function commaFix(cand) local noun = cand:match("^%S+") or cand local pos = 1 if inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.lines then for _, it in ipairs(inv.roomScan.lines) do local k = inv.key(it.name) if k == key then break end local oc = inv.handleLadder(k) if (oc[#oc] or "") == noun then pos = pos + 1 end end end return noun .. (pos > 1 and " "..pos or "") end
-- A recorded GROUND ambiguity is a fact about a room, not about the handle: -- it means something else on that floor answered to the same string. When -- this room demonstrably holds no such rival, the shadow is stale and -- blocking on it throws away a perfectly good short handle for good. The -- clash test above already knows the answer, so ask it and heal the record. local function groundBlocked(c) if not inv.ambBlocks(key, c, "ground") then return false end if clashes(c) then return true end if not (inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.lines) then return true end inv.handleClearAmb(key, c, "ground") return inv.ambBlocks(key, c, "ground") -- still blocked by another scope? end
local confirmed = inv.handleList(key) -- Prefer the game's own show-id ground pick: it is unambiguous on this floor by -- construction (it lists "cloth cloak" over the shared "cloak"), which also -- keeps a generic alias out of the map that an inventory verb could later -- misfire on once the item is in the pack. local sid = inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].showIdHandle if sid and not tried[sid] and not inv.handleIsBad(key, sid) and not groundBlocked(sid) and not clashes(sid) then if sid:find(",") then return commaFix(sid) end for _, c in ipairs(confirmed) do if c == sid then return sid end end end for i = #confirmed, 1, -1 do -- shortest proven first local c = confirmed[i] if not tried[c] then if c:find(",") then return commaFix(c) end -- ground context: a handle shadowed only by something we CARRY is -- still fine here, because `get` cannot see inventory at all. if not groundBlocked(c) and not clashes(c) then return c end end end
-- Nothing proven is both untried and unshadowed here. The blind ladder now -- gets its turn even though proven handles exist, which it never used to: -- a candidate that collides with nothing on this floor is a better command -- than a proven one we already know reaches the wrong object, and `get` -- offers no way to ask for a second opinion. local cands = inv.blindLadder(key) local h = inv.handlesOf(key) local best for _, cand in ipairs(cands) do if not tried[cand] and not (h and h.bad[cand]) and not groundBlocked(cand) then if not best then best = cand end if cand:find(",") then return commaFix(cand) end if not clashes(cand) then return cand end end end if best then return best end
-- Last resort: the most specific proven handle not already burned this run. for i = 1, #confirmed do local c = confirmed[i] if not tried[c] then return c:find(",") and commaFix(c) or c end end -- nil, not the display name: an exhausted ladder is the ihandle case, and -- sending the display name just buys another guaranteed refusal. return nil end
-- ---- In-flight loot gets: attribution, retry, and a gated weigh -------- -- iloot used to fire its gets and never read the answers. ishop and isac both -- walk the handle ladder when a command reaches nothing (inv.onNotCarried, -- inv.onSacNothing); the loot path had no equivalent, so a refusal left the -- item on the floor, taught the package nothing, and printed the cheerful -- pair "taking 1 item type(s)" / "sorted 0 to bags, dropped 0 trash". -- -- Attribution is by the QUOTED HANDLE rather than by position: "You see no -- 'X' around here." names the exact string we sent, and shortestRoomHandle -- already refuses to hand one string to two items in the same room. That -- sidesteps the response-correlation desync which is why the old code armed -- verification only for a lone deliberate get. function inv.lootIssue(e) if not e.handle then -- Every rung of the ladder is on the bad list, so there is no command left -- to send and no way for the package to learn its way out: `get` is the -- only verb that can promote a handle, and we cannot call it. This is the -- ihandle case, and it has to be loud — a grey aside was easy to miss -- between "taking 1 item type(s)" and "sorted 0 to bags". inv.warn(string.format("%s: every handle has been refused — nothing left to send.", e.name or "?")) if e.key then inv.markStuck(e.key, "every handle refused; ladder exhausted", "ground") cecho(string.format( " <grey>fix it with<reset> <cyan>ihandle<reset><grey>, or clear the refusals and start over:<reset> " .."<cyan>ihandle reset %s<reset>\n", e.name or e.key)) end return nil end e.tried = e.tried or {} e.tried[e.handle] = true inv.loot.issued = inv.loot.issued or {} inv.loot.issued[#inv.loot.issued+1] = e return e end
-- Pull the entry a reply belongs to. `handle` matches a refusal (which quotes -- the string); `key` matches a success (the echo names the item). function inv.lootClaim(by, value) if value == nil then return nil end local q = inv.loot.issued or {} for i = 1, #q do local e = q[i] if (by == "handle" and e.handle and e.handle:lower() == tostring(value):lower()) or (by == "key" and e.key == value) then table.remove(q, i) return e end end return nil end
function inv.lootRetryCount(e) local n = 0 for _ in pairs(e.tried or {}) do n = n + 1 end return n end
-- A get was refused. Demote the handle, then re-issue with the next rung. -- -- Unless the floor has already been emptied of this type by THIS run: then -- "You see no 'X' around here." is the literal truth about the room and says -- nothing about the string. Blacklisting on it burns a good handle for a -- refusal it did not earn, and a few of those in a row leave a type with no -- ladder left at all — the state that produces "every handle has been -- refused" on a plain, visible item. -- Has this run already taken every one of these the room held? If so, a -- refusal naming this type is about the room, not about the string. function inv.lootFloorEmptied(key) if not (inv.loot.active and key) then return false end local onFloor = (inv.loot.roomQty and inv.loot.roomQty[key]) or 0 if onFloor == 0 then return false end return ((inv.loot.got and inv.loot.got[key]) or 0) >= onFloor end
function inv.lootHandleRefused(handle) local e = inv.lootClaim("handle", handle) if not e then return false end local taken = (inv.loot.got and inv.loot.got[e.key]) or 0 if inv.lootFloorEmptied(e.key) then inv.lootSay(string.format("<grey>%s: already took %d — the room is empty of them, " .."not a handle problem.<reset>", e.name, taken)) inv.lootMaybeWeigh() return true end if e.key then inv.handleFailedAction(e.key, e.handle, "get") end if inv.lootRetryCount(e) > inv.HANDLE_RETRIES then inv.lootSay(string.format("<yellow>out of handles for %s — left in room<reset>", e.name)) if e.key then inv.markStuck(e.key, string.format("get failed, last tried '%s'", e.handle), "ground") end inv.lootMaybeWeigh() return true end inv.lootSay(string.format("retrying %s with another handle...", e.name)) if e.dest == "loose" then inv.lootGetLoose(e.name, e.tried) elseif e.dest == (inv.config.treasureBag or "treasure") and inv.config.groupMode then inv.lootGetToTreasure(e.name, e.tried) else inv.lootGetToBag(e.name, e.tried) end inv.lootMaybeWeigh() return true end
-- A get succeeded. The string we sent moved a real object, which is the only -- evidence that promotes a handle from look-proven to action-proven. function inv.lootGetSucceeded(key) -- Coins arrive from `get all money`, which is ONE command covering every -- pile in the room and never has an issued entry of its own. They therefore -- always look like "something turned up that nobody asked for" — which is -- exactly how `get axe to "loot"` got blamed for delivering 5 platinum -- coins. Money is never evidence about a handle. if inv.coinInfo(key) or inv.isMoney(key) then return inv.lootMaybeWeigh() end
-- Exact match: the echo names the item, so if an outstanding get asked for -- exactly that type, that is the one it answered — no ordering assumption, -- no chance of blaming the wrong command. local e = inv.lootClaim("key", key) if e then if e.key and e.handle then inv.handleRecordOk(e.key, e.handle) end else -- Nothing outstanding asked for this. Attributing it to a command is only -- safe when exactly ONE is in flight; with a burst in the air, anything -- else is the same positional guesswork that produced the last two false -- accusations. Stay quiet instead — an unclaimed entry costs one backstop -- tick, a wrongly blocked handle costs the item. local q = inv.loot.issued or {} if #q == 1 then local head = table.remove(q, 1) if head and head.key and head.handle then inv.handleRecordAmb(head.key, head.handle, "ground") inv.warn(string.format("'%s' reached %s instead of %s — marked ambiguous on the ground.", head.handle, (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key, head.name or head.key)) -- deliberately NOT recorded as a handle for what actually arrived: -- inventing an action-proven handle from a guess is how `tin bracers` -- became the Bloodstone's preferred command. end end end inv.loot.got = inv.loot.got or {} inv.loot.got[key] = (inv.loot.got[key] or 0) + 1 inv.lootMaybeWeigh() end
-- Some other refusal (too heavy / cannot move / no room) retired this item. function inv.lootAbandon(key) if inv.lootClaim("key", key) then inv.lootMaybeWeigh() end end
-- `i weight` may only be sent once every get has been answered. Firing it -- straight after the burst is what made a retry pointless: the sort ran, found -- nothing loose, and closed the run while the second attempt was still in -- flight. function inv.lootMaybeWeigh() if not inv.loot.weighWanted then return end if #(inv.loot.issued or {}) > 0 then return end inv.loot.weighWanted = false if inv.loot.weighTimer then killTimer(inv.loot.weighTimer); inv.loot.weighTimer = nil end inv.lootSay("weighing & sorting...") send("i weight", false) inv.loot.pendingSort = true inv.loot.sortGen = inv.loot.gen end
-- helper: split a handle into words function words_of(s) local t={}; for w in s:gmatch("%S+") do t[#t+1]=w end; return t end
-- Make any handle safe to send as a game command. Handles containing commas -- are misparsed by Icesus as multi-target separators. -- For gets: replace with positional index (heart 5). -- For puts: use bare noun only (put doesn't support positional indexing). function inv.safeHandle(handle, key, container, forPut) if not handle or not handle:find(",") then return handle end local noun = (handle:match("^%S+") or handle):gsub("[,%.]+$", "") if forPut then return noun end -- for gets: count same-noun predecessors in location map local pos = 1 for _, k in ipairs(inv.loc[container] or {}) do if k == key then break end local cands = inv.handleCandidates(k) local kNoun = cands[#cands] or "" if kNoun == noun then pos = pos + 1 end end return noun .. (pos > 1 and " "..pos or "") end
-- Issue: get one <item> straight to the treasure bag (group-mode glow route). function inv.lootGetToTreasure(name, tried) local tb = inv.config.treasureBag or "treasure" local key = inv.key(name) local handle = inv.shortestRoomHandle(name, tried) if not inv.lootIssue{ key=key, name=name, handle=handle, dest=tb, tried=tried } then return end local cmd = string.format('get %s to "%s"', handle, tb) inv.lootEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) end
