-- ============================================================ -- Corpses: icorpse -- ============================================================ -- The shortcut this is built on comes straight from the logs: `dig grave` -- SPILLS the contents of every corpse onto the floor before destroying them. -- So there is no reason to loot corpses at all — emptying them one item at a -- time would mean a second set of handle problems (a corpse is a container we -- cannot name reliably, holding items indexed against contents we can only -- see by looking) for no benefit. Dig first, and the whole room becomes an -- ordinary iloot: coin densities, cutoffs, the surplus sweep and every other -- rule already apply, unchanged and in one place. -- -- What IS worth doing first is looking in each corpse. `look` is free, and it -- is the only moment the game will tell us which monster carried what: -- scanEnd already routes a corpse scan to noteOrigin instead of the location -- map, which is what fills in `idrops`. Once they are in a mass grave that -- link is gone for good. -- -- Corpse display names vary with how the thing died ("Burned slush of snake", -- "Mutilated lump of carrion crawler"), so they cannot be recognised from the -- room listing. They all answer to `corpse` though, and to a positional index -- on it, so the walk is `l corpse`, `l corpse 2`, ... until the game says -- "Look at what?". inv.corpse = nil if C.corpseDig == nil then C.corpseDig = "dig grave" end
function inv.corpseEcho(c) cecho("\n<grey>[icorpse]<reset> <cyan>"..c.."<reset>") end function inv.corpseSay(m) cecho("\n<grey>[icorpse]<reset> "..m) end
function inv.icorpseRun(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") local setDig = arg:match("^dig%s+(.+)$") if setDig then inv.config.corpseDig = setDig; inv.save() inv.corpseSay("grave command set to '"..setDig.."'"); return end if arg == "" or arg == "quick" or arg == "scan" or arg == "nodig" or arg == "skin" then if inv.corpse and inv.corpse.active then inv.warn("a corpse walk is already running."); return end inv.corpse = { active = true, n = 0, found = 0, mobs = {}, dig = (arg ~= "scan"), loot = (arg ~= "scan" and arg ~= "nodig"), thenSkin = (arg == "skin"), -- `quick` skips the provenance walk entirely: straight to -- the grave and let iloot sweep up the spill. walk = (arg ~= "quick") } if not inv.corpse.walk then return inv.corpseDone() end inv.corpseSay("checking corpses...") return inv.corpseStep() end inv.warn("usage: icorpse -- look in each corpse, dig the grave, loot the spill") inv.warn(" icorpse skin -- skin them first (keeps the hides), then dig and loot") inv.warn(" icorpse quick -- skip the look, just dig and loot") inv.warn(" icorpse scan -- look only, leave the corpses alone") inv.warn(" icorpse nodig -- look, dig, but do not loot afterwards") inv.warn(" icorpse dig dg -- change the grave command") end
function inv.corpseStep() local c = inv.corpse if not (c and c.active) then return end c.n = c.n + 1 if c.n > (inv.config.corpseMax or 12) then return inv.corpseDone() end c.awaiting = true local cmd = (c.n == 1) and "l corpse" or ("l corpse "..c.n) inv.corpseEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) if c.timer then killTimer(c.timer) end -- backstop: a corpse that is empty prints no contents block, and a reply we -- fail to recognise must end the walk rather than strand it. c.timer = tempTimer(3, function() inv.corpseDone() end) end
-- "This is the dead body of X." — one corpse confirmed. function inv.corpseHit(mob) local c = inv.corpse if not (c and c.active and c.awaiting) then return end c.awaiting = false c.found = c.found + 1 c.mobs[#c.mobs+1] = (mob or "?"):lower() if c.timer then killTimer(c.timer) end -- let this corpse's contents block finish before asking for the next, so -- the scan is attributed to the corpse it came from c.timer = tempTimer(0.7, function() inv.corpseStep() end) end
-- "Look at what?" — we have walked past the last corpse. function inv.corpseMiss() local c = inv.corpse if not (c and c.active) then return end inv.corpseDone() end
function inv.corpseDone() local c = inv.corpse if not c then return end if c.timer then killTimer(c.timer); c.timer = nil end c.active = false inv.corpse = nil
if c.walk and c.found == 0 then if c.thenSkin then inv.skinSay("no corpses here.") else inv.corpseSay("no corpses here.") end return end if c.found > 0 and not c.thenSkin then inv.corpseSay(string.format("%d corpse(s): %s", c.found, table.concat(c.mobs, ", "))) end
-- Skin first when asked. Skinning CONSUMES the corpse and spills the rest, -- so it does the grave's job as well as taking the hides — digging first -- would throw the skins away. Whatever cannot be skinned is still standing -- afterwards, so the grave still runs, and it is harmless when there is -- nothing left to bury. if c.thenSkin then inv.skinBegin(c.found, c.mobs) if inv.skin then inv.skin.after = function() if c.dig then inv.corpseGrave = { loot = c.loot } inv.corpseEcho(inv.config.corpseDig); send(inv.config.corpseDig, false) inv.corpseGrave.timer = tempTimer(4, function() inv.corpseGraveDug(true) end) elseif c.loot then inv.corpseSay("looting the spill...") inv.ilootRun("") end end end return end
if not c.dig then return end
-- Dig, then WAIT for the grave's own reply before looting. Firing both in -- one breath looks fine — Icesus does answer chronologically — but the -- room scan is closed by a PROMPT, and the dig's prompt arrives first. That -- is the "no items here" reported a moment before the room listed nine of -- them. inv.onPrompt now ignores prompts until the exits line, which fixes -- it from the other side too; sequencing here as well means the spill is -- also confirmed on the floor before we go looking for it. inv.corpseGrave = { loot = c.loot } inv.corpseEcho(inv.config.corpseDig); send(inv.config.corpseDig, false) inv.corpseGrave.timer = tempTimer(4, function() inv.corpseGraveDug(true) end) end
-- "You dig a grave for the corpse and bury it carefully." (one) or -- "You dig a large mass-grave for all the corpses and shove them in." (several) function inv.corpseGraveDug(timedOut) local g = inv.corpseGrave if not g then return end inv.corpseGrave = nil if g.timer then killTimer(g.timer); g.timer = nil end if timedOut then inv.warn("no reply to '"..tostring(inv.config.corpseDig) .."' — set the right command with 'icorpse dig CMD'. Looting anyway.") end if g.loot then inv.corpseSay("looting the spill...") inv.ilootRun("") end end
-- ============================================================ -- Skinning: iskin -- ============================================================ -- Skinning is the other way to empty a corpse, and it behaves differently -- from `dig grave` in one way that matters to a tracker: the skins go -- straight into LOOSE INVENTORY, with no "You get" echo to attribute. Every -- other route into the pack announces itself; this one does not, so sixteen -- skins can accumulate that the location map has never heard of. Everything -- else the corpse held is spilled on the floor, exactly as digging does, and -- the corpse is consumed either way. -- -- The gap is narrow but real: a plain `i` would register the skins by name -- and count, and `i weight` adds mass and bulk. So the fix is not to guess at -- the skins from the skinning lines — which never name them — but to ask for -- a weigh once the knife is down. -- -- One `skin corpse` produces several "finish the skinning" lines, one per -- attempt, some succeeding and some not. It also takes about thirteen seconds -- and holds the skill busy throughout, so the corpses have to be worked one -- at a time. -- -- What tells us a corpse is finished is the *lines*, not the prompt. Icesus -- sends a prompt in reply to input, not when a skill ends by itself: in a -- logged run the four "You finish the skinning" lines and the "You retrieve" -- lines arrived with no prompt behind them, and the cleared "Skill:" field -- only showed up two seconds later when a `l` was typed. Waiting on the -- prompt would therefore stall every corpse until the watchdog gave up. -- -- So the finish lines end the attempt. They come in a burst — four finishes -- and a retrieve inside the same millisecond — so the burst is let settle for -- a moment before the next corpse is asked for, and every line in it pushes -- that moment back. A prompt that does happen to arrive with the skill clear -- is still honoured; it is just a shortcut now, not the mechanism. inv.skin = nil -- Seconds of quiet after the last skinning line before the burst is over. -- Only has to outlast one packet, never a skinning. inv.SKIN_SETTLE = 1.5 if C.skinWeigh == nil then C.skinWeigh = true end if C.skinQuiet == nil then C.skinQuiet = 30 end
function inv.skinEcho(c) cecho("\n<grey>[iskin]<reset> <cyan>"..c.."<reset>") end function inv.skinSay(m) cecho("\n<grey>[iskin]<reset> "..m) end
-- The prompt carries the current skill: "... 231372exp) Skill: busy" function inv.noteSkill(s) local wasBusy = inv.skillBusy inv.skillBusy = (s or ""):gsub("%s+","") ~= "" local sk = inv.skin if not (sk and sk.active) then return end -- still working: keep the watchdog fed however long it takes if inv.skillBusy then return inv.skinPoke() end -- The knife is down. Advance only if THIS attempt actually started — the -- character may have been busy with something else entirely when the run -- began, and that skill ending says nothing about a corpse. if wasBusy and sk.awaiting and (sk.started or 0) > (sk.startMark or 0) then inv.skinNext() end end
-- "You take your knife and start skinning the corpse of Boa constrictor." function inv.noteSkinStart(mob) inv.noteKill(mob) -- everything this corpse yields is its drop if inv.skin then inv.skin.started = (inv.skin.started or 0) + 1 if inv.skin.startTimer then killTimer(inv.skin.startTimer); inv.skin.startTimer = nil end inv.skinPoke() end end
-- "You finish the skinning and succeed in removing the skin." — one line per -- attempt, several per corpse. The first of them means the knife is down; the -- rest are the same burst, so the settle timer is what decides when to move -- on rather than the first line through the door. function inv.noteSkinResult(ok) if not inv.skin then return end if ok then inv.skin.skins = (inv.skin.skins or 0) + 1 else inv.skin.failed = (inv.skin.failed or 0) + 1 end inv.skinPoke() inv.skinSettle() end
-- Hold the door open a moment longer for anything still arriving from this -- corpse; when nothing has for SKIN_SETTLE seconds, the corpse is done. function inv.skinSettle() local s = inv.skin if not (s and s.active and s.awaiting) then return end if s.settleTimer then killTimer(s.settleTimer) end s.settleTimer = tempTimer(inv.SKIN_SETTLE, function() inv.skinNext() end) end
-- "You retrieve a clod of snake lard from the corpse." — it lands on the -- FLOOR, not in the pack, so there is nothing to add to the location map. -- What it does carry is provenance, and this is the only line that offers it. -- The retrieve line uses a SHORTER name than the floor listing does: "a clod -- of snake lard" here, "Clod of raw snake lard" once it lands. Exact lookup -- misses every time, so resolve it the way an appraisal quote is resolved. An -- unresolved or ambiguous name records nothing — provenance is worth having, -- never worth inventing a phantom type for. function inv.noteRetrieve(itemRaw) inv.skinPoke() inv.skinSettle() -- part of the same burst as the finish lines local key = inv.key(itemRaw) if not (key and inv.types[key]) then key = inv.resolveFragment(itemRaw) end if key and inv.types[key] then inv.noteOrigin(key) end end
function inv.iskinRun(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if arg == "on" or arg == "off" then inv.config.skinWeigh = (arg == "on"); inv.save() inv.skinSay("weigh after skinning: "..(inv.config.skinWeigh and "on" or "off")); return end local q = arg:match("^quiet%s+(%d+)$") if q then inv.config.skinQuiet = tonumber(q); inv.save() inv.skinSay("give up after "..q.."s of silence"); return end if arg ~= "" then inv.warn("usage: iskin -- skin every corpse here, then weigh the skins") inv.warn(" iskin on|off -- whether to weigh afterwards") inv.warn(" iskin quiet 45 -- seconds of SILENCE before giving up") return end if inv.skin and inv.skin.active then inv.warn("a skinning run is already going."); return end if inv.corpse and inv.corpse.active then inv.warn("a corpse walk is running."); return end -- Count the corpses first, with the same free `l corpse N` walk icorpse -- uses. Counting up front means the loop terminates on a number we -- measured, rather than on a refusal message nobody has captured yet. inv.skinSay("counting corpses...") inv.corpse = { active=true, n=0, found=0, mobs={}, walk=true, dig=false, loot=false, thenSkin=true } inv.corpseStep() end
-- Called by inv.corpseDone when the walk was started for a skinning run. function inv.skinBegin(found, mobs) if found == 0 then inv.skinSay("no corpses here."); return end inv.skin = { active=true, left=found, total=found, skins=0, failed=0, mobs=mobs } inv.skinSay(string.format("skinning %d corpse(s): %s", found, table.concat(mobs, ", "))) inv.skinSend() end
function inv.skinSend() local s = inv.skin if not (s and s.active) then return end if s.left <= 0 then return inv.skinDone() end -- Always index 1: a skinned corpse is consumed, so the next one moves up. inv.skinEcho("skin corpse"); send("skin corpse", false) s.awaiting = true s.startMark = s.started or 0 -- has THIS attempt begun? -- How long a skinning takes varies by monster and by skill, so nothing here -- may depend on a duration. Progress is what is watched, not elapsed time: -- inv.skinPoke resets the watchdog on every line the skinning produces, so -- the timeout means "half a minute of silence", never "half a minute of -- work". A slow monster simply keeps poking it. inv.skinPoke() -- Separately: if the command never starts a skinning at all — no corpse -- left, or one that cannot be skinned — no "You take your knife" line -- arrives. Three seconds of that is the answer, and it saves waiting out -- the full watchdog for a refusal message we have never seen the text of. if s.startTimer then killTimer(s.startTimer) end s.startTimer = tempTimer(3, function() local cur = inv.skin if cur and cur.active and cur.awaiting and (cur.started or 0) <= (cur.startMark or 0) then cur.refused = true inv.skinDone() end end) end
-- Any sign of life from the knife: restart the silence watchdog. function inv.skinPoke() local s = inv.skin if not (s and s.active) then return end if s.timer then killTimer(s.timer) end s.timer = tempTimer(inv.config.skinQuiet or 30, function() inv.skinDone(true) end) end
function inv.skinNext() local s = inv.skin if not (s and s.active and s.awaiting) then return end s.awaiting = false s.left = s.left - 1 if s.timer then killTimer(s.timer); s.timer = nil end if s.startTimer then killTimer(s.startTimer); s.startTimer = nil end if s.settleTimer then killTimer(s.settleTimer); s.settleTimer = nil end if s.left > 0 then inv.skinSend() else inv.skinDone() end end
function inv.skinDone(timedOut) local s = inv.skin if not s then return end if s.timer then killTimer(s.timer); s.timer = nil end if s.startTimer then killTimer(s.startTimer); s.startTimer = nil end if s.settleTimer then killTimer(s.settleTimer); s.settleTimer = nil end inv.skin = nil if timedOut then inv.warn(string.format( "no sign of the knife for %ds — stopping with %d corpse(s) left. " .."Raise it with 'iskin quiet N' if your skinning is slower than that.", inv.config.skinQuiet or 30, s.left or 0)) elseif s.refused then inv.skinSay(string.format("nothing left to skin (%d of %d done).", (s.total or 0) - (s.left or 0), s.total or 0)) end inv.skinSay(string.format("%d skin(s) taken, %d attempt(s) failed.", s.skins or 0, s.failed or 0)) local after = s.after if inv.config.skinWeigh and (s.skins or 0) > 0 then -- The one command that turns those skins into tracked items: `i weight` -- gives the name, the count, the mass and the bulk in one reply. inv.skinSay("registering the skins...") inv.skinEcho("i weight"); send("i weight", false) end if after then after() end end
-- ---- iloot command ---------------------------------------------------- function inv.ilootRun(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if arg == "sort" then return inv.lootSort() end if arg:match("^cutoff%s+%d") then inv.config.cutoffSL = tonumber(arg:match("(%d+)")); inv.save() inv.lootSay("cutoff set to "..inv.config.cutoffSL.." s/l"); return end if arg == "coins" or arg == "coins on" or arg == "coins off" then if arg ~= "coins" then inv.config.coinCutoff = (arg == "coins on"); inv.save() end cecho(string.format("\n<white>Coins<reset> judged by the %d s/l cutoff: <cyan>%s<reset>\n", inv.config.cutoffSL, inv.config.coinCutoff and "on" or "off")) local ds = {} for d in pairs(inv.coinSilver) do ds[#ds+1] = d end table.sort(ds, function(a,b) return (inv.coinSilver[a] or 0) < (inv.coinSilver[b] or 0) end) for _, d in ipairs(ds) do local sl = inv.coinPerLitre(d) cecho(string.format(" %-9s %4d s each %5.2f ml %10s s/l %s\n", d, inv.coinSilver[d], inv.coinVol[d] or 0, sl and string.format("%.0f", sl) or "?", inv.coinWorthTaking(d) and "<green>take<reset>" or "<yellow>leave<reset>")) end cecho(" <grey>densities are measured from 'i weight' lines; 'iloot coins off' takes everything.<reset>\n") return end local ex = arg:match("^exclude%s+(.+)$") if ex then local key = inv.key(ex) or ex:lower() inv.config.excludes[key] = true; inv.save() inv.lootSay("excluded from auto-loot: "..ex); return end local inc = arg:match("^include%s+(.+)$") if inc then return inv.includeItem(inc) end local unex = arg:match("^unexclude%s+(.+)$") if unex then local key = inv.key(unex) or unex:lower() inv.config.excludes[key] = nil; inv.save() inv.lootSay("un-excluded: "..unex); return end if arg == "excludes" then local ks = {} for k in pairs(inv.config.excludes) do ks[#ks+1] = k end if #ks == 0 then inv.lootSay("no exclusions set.") else cecho("\n<cyan>Auto-loot exclusions:<reset>\n") table.sort(ks); for _,k in ipairs(ks) do cecho(" "..k.."\n") end end return end -- Begin: request a room scan. We parse the room item block from `look`. inv.loot.active = true inv.loot.tookLoose = {} inv.loot.issued = {} inv.loot.roomQty = {} inv.loot.got = {} inv.loot.coinSelective = nil -- A weight refusal belongs to the run that saw it. Carrying it forward made -- a one-off "your pack was full at the time" into a permanent verdict on the -- item, so a Shovel you could not lift at 95% load was never offered again -- even after you had emptied everything at a shop. inv.tooHeavy = {} inv.loot.weighWanted = false if inv.loot.weighTimer then killTimer(inv.loot.weighTimer); inv.loot.weighTimer = nil end inv.loot.weighNeeded = false inv.loot.gen = (inv.loot.gen or 0) + 1 -- invalidates any stale pending sort inv.bagFull = {} inv.pendingPuts = {} -- clear stale put attributions inv.lootSay("scanning room...") inv.roomScan = { active=true, lines={} } send("look", false) -- Backstop for the gate above: if no exits line ever arrives, the scan would -- sit open and the run would never finish. Close it out rather than hang. if inv.loot.scanTimer then killTimer(inv.loot.scanTimer) end inv.loot.scanTimer = tempTimer(5, function() if inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.active and not inv.roomScan.atItems then inv.warn("no room description came back — iloot stopped. Try again.") inv.roomScan = nil inv.loot.active = false end end) end
-- Room parsing: the item block follows the exits line. Each line is recorded -- with whether it was COLOR-LED (first char colored => creature, skip). The -- trigger passes isMob (from getFgColor inspection); if it couldn't read color -- it passes nil and we treat as item (user chose aggressive looting). function inv.roomExitsSeen() if inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.active then inv.roomScan.atItems = true -- `atItems` is a cursor: roomLine clears it the moment the item block ends, -- and the prompt line is one of the things that ends it. `sawRoom` is the -- durable fact — our own look's room block arrived — and it is what -- inv.onPrompt gates on. Gating on atItems meant the "Scan line" trigger -- (earlier in the package, so it fires first) cleared the flag on the -- prompt line before the prompt trigger could read it, and the scan never -- closed at all. inv.roomScan.sawRoom = true inv.roomScan.lines = {} -- fresh list (handles a re-printed room) inv.roomScan.skipThisLine = true -- the exits line itself isn't an item end end
-- Determine if the CURRENT trigger line begins with a non-default foreground -- colour (=> a creature). Returns false on any failure (treat as item). function inv.lineIsMob() local ok, mob = pcall(function() if not (getLineNumber and selectSection and getFgColor and moveCursor) then return false end local ln = getLineNumber() moveCursor(0, ln) selectSection(0, 1) local r,g,b = getFgColor() if not r then return false end local isGreen = (g > r + 40) and (g > b + 40) local isRed = (r > g + 60) and (r > b + 60) return isGreen or isRed end) if not ok then return false end return mob end
function inv.roomLine(raw) if not (inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.active and inv.roomScan.atItems) then return end if inv.roomScan.skipThisLine then inv.roomScan.skipThisLine = false; return end if raw:match("^%s*$") then return end if raw:find("%d+/%d+HP") or raw:find("^You are carrying") or raw:find("^Money:") or raw:find("obvious exits?") or raw:find("^Keep:") or raw:find("You see no '") or raw:find("^You cannot move") then inv.roomScan.atItems = false return end -- The mapper draws an ASCII map with the room description beside it. Those -- lines are not items; ingesting them created thousands of junk types with -- names like "##### the road. The sky is overcas". local glyphs = select(2, raw:gsub("[#~^|+=@*\\/]", "")) if glyphs >= 3 then return end if #raw > 72 then return end if not raw:find("%a") then return end
-- Creatures share the room listing with items but are drawn in a non-default -- colour, and they answer to no `get` handle -- ingesting one burns a whole -- handle ladder and leaves an `ihandle` nag for something that was never an -- item (this is how "Orc patroller humming a happy tune" ended up tracked). -- Skip a colour-led line, UNLESS it is a glowing item (an item that happens -- to be coloured) or a money pile (which `get all money` takes wholesale, -- never by its own handle). lineIsMob() reads the current line's colour and -- returns false whenever it cannot, so a terminal without colour info falls -- back to the old aggressive behaviour rather than skipping real items. do local mk = inv.key(raw) local isMoneyLine = mk and (inv.coinInfo(mk) or inv.isMoney(mk)) if inv.lineIsMob() and not inv.parseGlow(raw) and not isMoneyLine then inv.roomScan.skippedMobs = (inv.roomScan.skippedMobs or 0) + 1 return end end
-- one room line can list several items joined by " and " for _, part in ipairs(inv.splitAndLine(raw)) do local n = tonumber(part:match("^(%d+)%s*x%s")) or 1 local nm = part:gsub("^%d+%s*x%s+","") if nm ~= "" then inv.roomScan.lines[#inv.roomScan.lines+1] = { name=nm, qty=n } end end end
function inv.roomScanEnd() if not (inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.active) then return end inv.roomScan.active = false if inv.loot.scanTimer then killTimer(inv.loot.scanTimer); inv.loot.scanTimer = nil end local items = inv.roomScan.lines -- This room's contents are proof about every outstanding GROUND request: -- anything not listed here is not here, and a request you cannot act on -- becomes a phantom complaint at the tail of every later run. local present = {} for _, it in ipairs(items) do local k = inv.key(it.name); if k then present[k] = true end end local gone = inv.stuckDropAbsentGround(present) if gone > 0 then inv.lootSay(string.format( "<grey>dropped %d stale handle request(s) — those items are not in this room<reset>", gone)) end if (inv.roomScan.skippedMobs or 0) > 0 then inv.lootSay(string.format("<grey>skipped %d creature(s) in the room (colour-led, not items)<reset>", inv.roomScan.skippedMobs)) end if #items == 0 then inv.lootSay("no items here."); inv.loot.active=false; return end
-- Classify each. Skip excluded, known non-items (mobs/fixtures learned from -- prior refusals), too-heavy, trash and established-cheap. Everything else is -- attempted with an individual get; a refusal teaches us it's a non-item. -- "leaving 4" answers the wrong question. Every skip has a specific, -- recorded cause, and they are not interchangeable: "too heavy" is a fact -- about your pack, "below cutoff" is a routing decision you can retune, and -- "not an item" is a guess the package made once and may have got wrong. -- Silently collapsing them into a count is what makes the loot engine look -- arbitrary — and hides a wrongly-learned non-item indefinitely. local wanted, anyLoose, skipped = {}, false, 0 local why, passed = {}, {} local function skip(reason, name, key, qty, soft) skipped = skipped + 1 why[reason] = why[reason] or {} table.insert(why[reason], name) -- `soft` marks a skip made purely on value: the item is reachable and not -- junk, we simply judged it not worth the space. Those are the only ones -- eligible to be swept up as surplus when they block a keeper. if soft and key then passed[#passed+1] = { name=name, key=key, qty=qty or 1, reason=reason } end end for _, it in ipairs(items) do local key = inv.key(it.name) -- Money is decided by `get all money`, not by any per-item list: one -- command takes every pile in the room whatever these tables say, so -- consulting them here can only produce a skip the very next line -- contradicts. Coins go straight into `wanted` and set the coin flag. if inv.coinInfo(key) or inv.isMoney(key) then local denom = inv.coinInfo(key) if denom and not inv.coinWorthTaking(denom) then skip(string.format("coins below the %d s/l cutoff (%s, %.0f s/l)", inv.config.cutoffSL, denom, inv.coinPerLitre(denom) or 0), it.name) else wanted[#wanted+1] = { name=it.name, qty=it.qty, disp="sell", key=key, coin=denom } end elseif inv.config.excludes[key] then skip("excluded", it.name) elseif inv.config.nonItems[key] then skip("learned non-item", it.name) -- A type we already know is a corpse is never looted -- it is dug (below). -- First-encounter corpses are not flagged yet; they are dropped from `wanted` -- after show id reveals them, in the roomScanEnd callback. elseif inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].corpse then skip("corpse (will dig)", it.name) elseif inv.tooHeavyNow(key) then skip(inv.tooHeavyNow(key), it.name) else local disp, metric = inv.classify(key) -- A "sac" route with no favour reading yet is a LEARNING sacrifice, and -- classify returns it however cheap the item is — otherwise a type could -- never acquire its favour number. That is the right answer for routing -- something already in the pack, and the wrong one for deciding what to -- pick up: it would drag every sub-cutoff type home just to measure it. -- Pay for the lesson out of stock we already carry. local ct = inv.types[key] local learningOnly = (disp == "sac") and not (ct and ct.sac) local function m() return metric and string.format("%.0f s/l", metric) or "?" end if disp == "trash" then skip("trash ("..m()..")", it.name) elseif disp == "leave" then skip(string.format("below the %d s/l cutoff", inv.config.cutoffSL).." ("..m()..")", it.name, key, it.qty, true) elseif learningOnly and metric and metric < inv.config.cutoffSL then -- "Pay for the lesson out of stock we already carry" is right only -- while there IS stock. For a type we have never held, this branch was -- a closed loop: skipped on the floor because its favour is unknown, -- and its favour stays unknown because it is never picked up. It gets -- written off on the silver figure alone, which is exactly the call -- that needs both numbers to make. if inv.dfWorthLearning(key) then wanted[#wanted+1] = { name=it.name, qty=1, disp=disp, key=key, dfLearn=true } inv.lootSay(string.format("<grey>taking one %s to price its favour (%s on silver alone)<reset>", it.name, m())) else skip("sub-cutoff, not worth a learning sacrifice ("..m()..")", it.name, key, it.qty, true) end elseif metric and metric < inv.config.cutoffSL and disp ~= "unknown" then -- classify returns the ROUTE (not "leave") for a below-cutoff item -- whose average is not yet ESTABLISHED (n < estN) — its verdict is -- "worth another sample". That is a refine-IN-PLACE judgement and it is -- the wrong answer for a PICK-UP: an item already measured well below -- the s/l cutoff belongs on the floor whatever its sample count, or the -- pack fills with 42-s/l lead spears hauled home just to reach n=3 — -- and a cheap sac-route item never gets there anyway, because you would -- have to sacrifice it three times to establish its favour, which you -- never do. The cutoff is a pick-up rule; enforce it here regardless of -- established-ness. Genuine first appraisals (no data at all -> disp -- "unknown", or value-known-but-unweighed) are still taken above, and -- the learning-favour case was handled above too. Soft-skip, so the -- surplus sweep can still rescue it if a keeper's handle can't be -- separated from it on the floor. skip(string.format("below the %d s/l cutoff", inv.config.cutoffSL).." ("..m()..")", it.name, key, it.qty, true) else wanted[#wanted+1] = { name=it.name, qty=it.qty, disp=disp, key=key } if disp == "unknown" then anyLoose = true end end end end inv.loot.why = why
-- ---- Handle collisions on the floor --------------------------------- -- Some types share their ONLY handle. Every heart in the game answers to -- exactly `heart` and to nothing else — the mob words are not id words, so -- `heart of troll` and `troll heart` do not parse — which means a room -- holding troll hearts and guard dog hearts offers no string that reaches -- one without risking the other. `get heart` fetches whichever the game -- picks, and no amount of handle discovery can improve on that. -- -- Nor can it be indexed from here: positional order on the GROUND is not -- something we have ever observed. We watch our own pack change, never the -- floor, and the room listing is grouped into stacks in an order that is -- neither alphabetical nor by count. -- -- So take the lot, and let the sort put it right afterwards. In the pack the -- order IS ours — we chose the sequence the items arrived in — and by the -- time the surplus is dropped every keeper is already stowed, which leaves -- the bare handle unambiguous with no index needed at all. inv.loot.surplus = {} if #wanted > 0 and #passed > 0 then local rescued = {} for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do if not inv.coinInfo(w.key) then local h = inv.shortestRoomHandle(w.name) if h then for _, p in ipairs(passed) do if not rescued[p.key] and inv.keyAnswersTo(p.key, h) then rescued[p.key] = { name = p.name, qty = p.qty, blocks = w.name, handle = h } end end end end end for key, r in pairs(rescued) do wanted[#wanted+1] = { name=r.name, qty=r.qty, disp="unknown", key=key, surplus=true } inv.loot.surplus[key] = (inv.loot.surplus[key] or 0) + r.qty anyLoose = true skipped = math.max(0, skipped - 1) inv.lootSay(string.format( "<grey>'%s' cannot reach %s without also reaching %s — taking both, " .."the surplus is dropped after sorting<reset>", r.handle, r.blocks, r.name)) end -- Anything sharing a handle with the surplus must come out LOOSE, so the -- sort can tell the keepers apart by name and stow them first. if next(rescued) then for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do if rescued[w.key] or (w.key and not inv.coinInfo(w.key)) then local h = inv.shortestRoomHandle(w.name) for rk in pairs(rescued) do if h and inv.keyAnswersTo(rk, h) then w.disp = "unknown"; anyLoose = true end end end end end end
if #wanted == 0 then inv.lootSay("nothing worth taking here.") inv.lootWhy() inv.loot.active = false return end
-- ensure every wanted type has a row before we ask about handles for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do if not inv.coinInfo(w.key) then inv.getType(w.key, w.name) end end
-- Handle discovery. `show id ground` is the game's own parser oracle: one -- command gives the exact handle for every ground object, so it replaces the -- look-probe ladder for room items. Anything it does not cover (a type we do -- not yet track, or a handle it omits) still falls back to the probe. local function probeThenTake() local toProbe, seenKey = {}, {} if inv.config.probeAuto and inv.config.probeRoom then for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do if not seenKey[w.key] and not inv.coinInfo(w.key) and not inv.handleKnown(w.key) and not inv.handleProbed(w.key) then seenKey[w.key] = true; toProbe[#toProbe+1] = w.key end end end if #toProbe > 0 then inv.lootSay(string.format("learning handles for %d type(s)...", #toProbe)) inv.probeQueue = toProbe inv.probeQueueRun(function() inv.lootTake(wanted, skipped) end, { source = "room", max = inv.config.probeRoomMax }) else inv.lootTake(wanted, skipped) end end
-- Every distinct room item type (trash included) — for full-handle -- registration below. Ensure a row exists so show id can adopt its handle. local roomItemKeys, seenRK = {}, {} for _, it in ipairs(inv.roomScan.lines or {}) do local k = inv.key(it.name) if k and not seenRK[k] and not inv.coinInfo(k) then seenRK[k] = true; roomItemKeys[#roomItemKeys+1] = k inv.getType(k, it.name) end end
if inv.config.useShowId then inv.showIdRun("ground", function(s) -- Corpses are never looted; they are dug (which SPILLS their contents onto -- the floor) and the spill re-looted. Detection has TWO signals and the -- second only arrives after full registration, so the dig decision waits -- for it: (1) the ground handle `corpse`/`corpse N` (s.corpses, set during -- the ground scan); (2) a body-part-named corpse ("cadaver"/"yolk") whose -- `show id <item>` Names list carries "corpse" -- idNamesLine flags the -- type (t.corpse) during idFullRun below. So run the full registration -- FIRST, then decide. inv.idFullRun(roomItemKeys, function() local corpseKeys = {} for k in pairs((s and s.corpses) or {}) do corpseKeys[k] = true end for _, k in ipairs(roomItemKeys) do if inv.types[k] and inv.types[k].corpse then corpseKeys[k] = true end end local anyCorpse = next(corpseKeys) ~= nil if anyCorpse and inv.config.digCorpses and not inv.loot.skipDigOnce then return inv.lootDigThenReloot() end inv.loot.skipDigOnce = nil -- digCorpses off, or a dig already failed: drop corpses from the take -- list so we never `get corpse` (which just fills a bag). if anyCorpse then local kept = {} for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do if not corpseKeys[w.key] then kept[#kept+1] = w end end wanted = kept end probeThenTake() end) end) else probeThenTake() end end
-- Corpses present: dig the grave (spills their contents), then re-loot. Reuses -- the icorpse grave machinery -- the "Grave dug" trigger calls corpseGraveDug, -- which re-runs iloot on the spill. function inv.lootDigThenReloot() inv.loot.active = false inv.loot.skipDigOnce = true -- the coming re-loot must not dig again inv.lootSay("corpses here — digging the grave, then looting the spill...") inv.corpseGrave = { loot = true } local dig = inv.config.corpseDig or "dig grave" inv.lootEcho(dig); send(dig, false) inv.corpseGrave.timer = tempTimer(4, function() inv.corpseGraveDug(true) end) end
-- Issue the pickups for an already-classified room list. function inv.lootTake(wanted, skipped) local anyLoose = false for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do if w.disp == "unknown" then anyLoose = true end end inv.lootSay(string.format("taking %d item type(s)%s.", #wanted, skipped>0 and (", leaving "..skipped) or "")) inv.lootWhy() -- Coins: `get all money` is one command for every pile in the room, so it is -- still the right call when every denomination present clears the cutoff. -- When one does not, it is too blunt — it would take the silver we just -- decided to leave — so the wanted denominations are fetched individually. local anyCoin, coinDenoms, seenDenom = false, {}, {} for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do local d = w.coin or inv.coinInfo(w.key) if d then anyCoin = true if not seenDenom[d] then seenDenom[d] = true; coinDenoms[#coinDenoms+1] = d end end end local coinsLeft = false for d in pairs(inv.coinSilver) do if not seenDenom[d] and inv.loot.why then for reason in pairs(inv.loot.why) do if reason:find("coins below", 1, true) and reason:find(d, 1, true) then coinsLeft = true end end end end if anyCoin then if not coinsLeft then inv.lootEcho("get all money"); send("get all money", false) else -- `get all <denom> coins` is the `all foo` form from `help object -- handling`. It is not separately documented for money, so if the parser -- refuses it we fall back to `get all money` once and stop trying — -- see inv.onNoSuchHandle. Taking the silver is a far smaller mistake -- than silently leaving the platinum. inv.loot.coinSelective = true table.sort(coinDenoms) for _, d in ipairs(coinDenoms) do local cmd = "get all "..d.." coins" inv.lootEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) end end end -- How many of each type the floor actually held, so a refusal that arrives -- after we have taken them all can be read as "the room is empty" rather -- than "the handle is wrong". See inv.lootHandleRefused. inv.loot.roomQty = {} inv.loot.got = {} for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do if w.key then inv.loot.roomQty[w.key] = (inv.loot.roomQty[w.key] or 0) + (w.qty or 1) end end
-- Every get is now registered and verified, not just a lone deliberate one: -- replies are matched by the handle they quote, so a batch reconciles -- without the response-correlation desync the old `single` gate avoided. for _, w in ipairs(wanted) do if inv.coinInfo(w.key) then -- already handled by 'get all money' elseif inv.config.groupMode and inv.isGlowItem(w.key) then -- group play: glowing (likely high-DF) items go to treasure for division for _=1,w.qty do inv.lootGetToTreasure(w.name) end elseif w.disp == "unknown" then for _=1,w.qty do inv.lootGetLoose(w.name) end else for _=1,w.qty do inv.lootGetToBag(w.name) end end end
-- Weigh + sort if any unknowns were taken loose — but only once every get -- has been answered. Sending `i weight` here unconditionally is what made a -- retry useless: the sort ran, saw nothing loose and closed the run while -- the second attempt was still in flight. The room scan is KEPT, because it -- is the only thing that can tell onNoSuchHandle which item a refused -- handle belonged to; it is already inactive, so it cannot eat `i weight`. if anyLoose then inv.loot.weighWanted = true if inv.loot.weighTimer then killTimer(inv.loot.weighTimer) end -- backstop: an echo we do not recognise must not strand the run inv.loot.weighTimer = tempTimer(4, function() if inv.loot.weighWanted then inv.loot.issued = {} inv.lootMaybeWeigh() end end) inv.lootMaybeWeigh() elseif #(inv.loot.issued or {}) == 0 then inv.loot.active = false inv.roomScan = nil end end
-- After an i-weight completes while looting, sort freshly-loose items. -- Anything that reached the inventory without a proven handle gets probed -- here first: it is loose, we are out of the fight, and the sort commands we -- are about to send are exactly the ones that need a correct handle. function inv.lootSort() inv.loot.pendingSort = false if inv.config.probeAuto and not inv.probe then local todo = {} for key, cnt in pairs(inv.loot.tookLoose or {}) do if cnt and cnt > 0 and not inv.coinInfo(key) and not inv.handleProbed(key) then todo[#todo+1] = key end end if #todo > 0 then inv.probeQueue = todo inv.lootSay(string.format("learning handles for %d loose type(s)...", #todo)) return inv.probeQueueRun(function() inv.lootSortNow() end, { source = "loose" }) end end return inv.lootSortNow() end
-- A put echo arrived during a sort. Tally it against what pass 1 intended. function inv.lootNotePut(key) if not (inv.loot.putLeft and inv.loot.putLeft > 0) then return end inv.loot.putSeen[key] = (inv.loot.putSeen[key] or 0) + 1 inv.loot.putLeft = inv.loot.putLeft - 1 if inv.loot.putLeft <= 0 then inv.lootFinishSort() end end
-- Fire the drops, if and only if the puts landed where they were aimed. function inv.lootFinishSort(timedOut) if inv.loot.dropTimer then killTimer(inv.loot.dropTimer); inv.loot.dropTimer = nil end local toDrop = inv.loot.toDrop or {} local expect, seen = inv.loot.putExpect or {}, inv.loot.putSeen or {} local moved = inv.loot.moved or 0
-- The intent check only means anything when we actually waited for the put -- echoes. On an ordinary run this runs in the same breath as the puts, so -- nothing has been confirmed yet and "0 of 1 stowed" is just the truth about -- timing, not a misfire. local mismatch = nil if not inv.loot.gated then expect = {} end for k, n in pairs(expect) do if (seen[k] or 0) ~= n then mismatch = string.format("%s: meant to stow %d, stowed %d", (inv.types[k] and inv.types[k].name) or k, n, seen[k] or 0) break end end if inv.loot.gated then for k in pairs(seen) do if not (inv.loot.putExpect or {})[k] then mismatch = string.format("stowed %s, which was not the intended item", (inv.types[k] and inv.types[k].name) or k) end end end
local dropped, surplusDropped = 0, 0 if mismatch and #toDrop > 0 then inv.warn(string.format( "the sort did not land as aimed (%s) — dropping nothing. The surplus is " .."carried instead; sacrifice it at an altar.", mismatch)) elseif timedOut and #toDrop > 0 and (inv.loot.putLeft or 0) > 0 then inv.warn("no reply to the sort's puts — dropping nothing, the surplus is carried.") else for _, d in ipairs(toDrop) do for _=1, d.cnt do local h = inv.shortestHandle("loose", d.key) h = inv.safeHandle(h, d.key, "loose", true) or h local rivals = 0 for _, k in ipairs(inv.loc.loose or {}) do if k ~= d.key and inv.keyAnswersTo(k, h) then rivals = rivals + 1 end end if rivals > 0 then inv.warn(string.format("%s still shares a handle with something in hand — not dropping it.", d.name)) else local cmd = "drop " .. h inv.lootEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) inv.locRemove("loose", d.key) dropped = dropped + 1 if d.why == "surplus" then surplusDropped = surplusDropped + 1 end end end end end
inv.lootSay(string.format("sorted %d to bags, dropped %d%s.", moved, dropped, surplusDropped > 0 and string.format(" (%d surplus taken only to reach a keeper)", surplusDropped) or "")) inv.loot.putExpect, inv.loot.putSeen, inv.loot.putLeft = nil, nil, nil inv.loot.toDrop, inv.loot.surplus, inv.loot.moved = nil, {}, nil inv.loot.gated = nil inv.loot.active = false inv.loot.issued = {} inv.roomScan = nil -- the run is over; release the retained scan if inv.loot.weighTimer then killTimer(inv.loot.weighTimer); inv.loot.weighTimer = nil end inv.stuckNag("loot") end
function inv.lootSortNow() local moved, dropped = 0, 0 local surplus = inv.loot.surplus or {} local function handleFor(key, name) -- refFor("loose") indexes among instances of the SAME key, which is the -- wrong count when a rival TYPE shares the handle: with two troll hearts -- and four dog hearts in hand it emits `heart 1`, and position 1 among -- everything answering `heart` may well be a dog. Use the handle-aware -- index over the loose order instead — that order is genuinely ours, since -- every arrival was named by its own get echo. Then sanitize: -- comma-containing handles are misparsed by the game. local h = inv.shortestHandle("loose", key) h = inv.safeHandle(h, key, "loose", true) or h local rivals = 0 for _, k in ipairs(inv.loc.loose or {}) do if k ~= key and inv.keyAnswersTo(k, h) then rivals = rivals + 1 end end if rivals == 0 then return h end -- unambiguous: no index at all local n = inv.handleIndexIn("loose", key, h) return n and n > 1 and (h .. " " .. n) or h end
-- PASS 1: stow every keeper. This has to finish before a single drop is -- sent. While a keeper and its lookalike are both loose, no string separates -- them and `drop heart` is a coin toss; once the keepers are in the bag the -- only heart left in hand is the surplus, and the bare handle is exact. That -- ordering is what makes this work without a positional index at all. local toDrop, expect = {}, {} for key, cnt in pairs(inv.loot.tookLoose or {}) do if cnt and cnt > 0 and not inv.coinInfo(key) then local disp = inv.classify(key) local name = inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name or key if surplus[key] or disp == "trash" then toDrop[#toDrop+1] = { key=key, name=name, cnt=cnt, why=surplus[key] and "surplus" or "trash" } elseif disp ~= "leave" then for _=1, cnt do local sack = inv.pickBag(inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].volume or nil) if sack then table.insert(inv.pendingPuts, {key=key, sackKey=sack}) local cmd = string.format('put %s in "%s"', handleFor(key, name), sack) inv.lootEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) -- model the move so the next index is computed against what will -- actually be in hand by the time that command runs inv.locMove("loose", sack, key) expect[key] = (expect[key] or 0) + 1 moved = moved + 1 end end end end end
-- PASS 2: the drops — but only once the puts have been ACCOUNTED FOR. -- -- Those puts are the one command in this sequence that has to name a -- specific item while a lookalike is still in hand, so they carry a -- positional index and an index is a claim, not a certainty. If it misfires -- the keeper stays loose and a surplus item goes in the bag; the bare drops -- that follow would then throw the keeper away. Each put echo names what it -- moved, so wait for them and only drop if every one matched intent. When it -- does not match, nothing is dropped and the surplus is simply carried — -- which is the safe outcome, not a broken one. -- By now every keeper is in a bag, so for the common case — a keeper and its -- lookalike — nothing sharing the handle is left in hand and handleFor drops -- the index entirely. That is the point of the two passes: the bare handle -- becomes exact, and no positional form has to be trusted. inv.loot.putExpect = expect -- key -> how many we meant to stow inv.loot.putSeen = {} inv.loot.putLeft = moved inv.loot.toDrop = toDrop inv.loot.moved = moved
inv.loot.tookLoose = {} -- Only a SURPLUS drop needs the gate. An ordinary trash drop names an item -- nothing else answers to, so there is nothing for a misfired put to ruin -- and no reason to make the common run wait on an echo. local risky = false for _, d in ipairs(toDrop) do if d.why == "surplus" then risky = true end end inv.loot.gated = (moved > 0 and risky) or nil if inv.loot.gated then if inv.loot.dropTimer then killTimer(inv.loot.dropTimer) end inv.loot.dropTimer = tempTimer(4, function() inv.lootFinishSort(true) end) return end inv.lootFinishSort() end
-- ---- Loot backstop messages ------------------------------------------ -- "<item> is too heavy." / "The X, the Y ... are too heavy." -> mark tooHeavy function inv.onTooHeavy(listText) for _, it in ipairs(inv.splitItemList(listText)) do local key = inv.key(it.name) -- Record the load it failed AT, not a bare flag: that is the whole -- difference between "this will not fit right now" and "never try again". if key then inv.tooHeavy[key] = { kg = inv.carry and inv.carry.kg } inv.lootAbandon(key) end end inv.save() end -- "You cannot move the X." / "You see no 'X' around here." -> X is not a -- takeable item (mob or fixture). Learn it so iloot never tries it again. -- "You cannot move the <x>." — a fixture, scenery, a mob. Permanent. function inv.onNonItem(name) local key = inv.key(name) if not key then return end -- Money is never scenery. A pile of coins is picked up by `get all money`, -- never by its own handle, so any refusal that named one came from some -- other command — and filing it as a non-item then made iloot "leave 1" -- while `get all money` hoovered it up two lines later. The list is for -- fixtures and mobs; coins cannot join it. if inv.coinInfo(key) or inv.isMoney(key) then return end inv.config.nonItems[key] = true inv.save() inv.lootAbandon(key) if inv.loot.active then inv.lootSay("learned non-item (won't retry): "..name) end end
-- ---- inonitem: flag a tracked type as a non-item (mob / fixture) ------ -- The room listing mixes items with creatures and scenery. The colour filter -- catches most creatures, but when one slips through and iloot burns a handle -- ladder on it (it then shows up in the `ihandle` list, because no `get` ever -- reached it), this is the manual escape hatch. `purge` also deletes the -- phantom type the mis-read created, so it stops cluttering iinv/idrops. function inv.markNonItem(key, purge) if not key then return false end if inv.coinInfo(key) or inv.isMoney(key) then return false end -- money is never scenery inv.config.nonItems[key] = true inv.clearStuck(key) inv.lootAbandon(key) if purge then for cont in pairs(inv.loc or {}) do inv.reconcileCount(cont, key, 0) end inv.types[key] = nil end inv.save() return true end
function inv.nonItemCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")
-- un-flag: it was an item after all local rs = arg:match("^reset%s+(.+)$") if rs then local key = inv.key(rs) if not (key and inv.config.nonItems[key]) then for k in pairs(inv.config.nonItems or {}) do if k:find(rs:lower(), 1, true) then key = k; break end end end if key and inv.config.nonItems[key] then inv.config.nonItems[key] = nil; inv.save() cecho(string.format("\n<green>[inonitem]<reset> '%s' is an item again — iloot will consider it.\n", key)) else inv.warn(string.format("'%s' is not on the non-item list.", rs)) end return end
-- list: the stuck items (numbered, the usual source) and the learned set if arg == "" or arg == "list" then local l = inv.stuckList() if #l > 0 then cecho("\n<yellow>[inonitem]<reset> flag any of these as a non-item by its number:\n") for i, s in ipairs(l) do cecho(string.format(" %d. <white>%s<reset> <grey>(%s)<reset>\n", i, s.name or s.key, s.container or "?")) end cecho("<grey> inonitem N | inonitem all | inonitem \"exact name\"<reset>\n") end local ni = {} for k in pairs(inv.config.nonItems or {}) do ni[#ni+1] = k end table.sort(ni) if #ni > 0 then cecho(string.format( "\n<cyan>Learned non-items (%d)<reset> <grey>— inonitem reset NAME to undo<reset>\n", #ni)) for _, k in ipairs(ni) do cecho(" <grey>"..k.."<reset>\n") end end if #l == 0 and #ni == 0 then cecho("\n<green>[inonitem]<reset> nothing is stuck and no non-items learned yet.\n") end return end
-- all currently-stuck types at once (the common case after a bad auto-loot) if arg == "all" then local l = inv.stuckList(); local n = 0 for _, s in ipairs(l) do if inv.markNonItem(s.key, true) then n = n + 1 end end cecho(string.format( "\n<green>[inonitem]<reset> flagged %d stuck type(s) as non-items — iloot will skip them.\n", n)) return end
-- by number from the stuck list, or by (partial) name local key, label local idx = arg:match("^(%d+)$") if idx then local s = inv.stuckList()[tonumber(idx)] if not s then inv.warn(string.format("there is no stuck item #%s — run 'inonitem' for the list.", idx)) return end key, label = s.key, s.name or s.key else local nm = arg:match('^"([^"]+)"$') or arg key = inv.key(nm) if not (key and inv.types[key]) then local hit for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do if k:find(nm:lower(), 1, true) or (t.name and t.name:lower():find(nm:lower(), 1, true)) then hit = k; break end end key = hit end if not key then inv.warn(string.format( "'%s' is not a tracked type — use the number from 'inonitem', or 'iinv' for exact names.", nm)) return end label = (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key end if inv.markNonItem(key, true) then cecho(string.format( "\n<green>[inonitem]<reset> flagged <white>%s<reset> as a non-item — iloot will never try it again.\n", label)) else inv.warn("that looks like money — not flagging it.") end end
-- "You see no '<handle>' around here." is a DIFFERENT thing and used to be -- funnelled into the same place. It says the handle matched nothing — which, -- for an item we can see listed in the room, means the handle is wrong, not -- that the item is scenery. Marking it a non-item excluded a real 13,000 -- silver dagger from looting forever, because a hand-typed `drop steel -- dagger` had failed once. function inv.onNoSuchHandle(handle) if not handle or handle == "" then return end local h = handle:lower()
-- an armed single get is reconciled by the verification layer inv.verifyNoSuch(h)
-- A refused `all <denom> coins` means the parser does not accept that form -- for money. That is a fact about Icesus, not about this room: record it, -- take everything the blunt way this once, and never try the selective form -- again. Leaving the platinum behind on a syntax guess would be the worse -- failure by some margin. local badDenom = h:match("^all%s+(%a+)%s+coins?$") if badDenom and inv.coinSilver[badDenom] then if inv.config.coinCutoff then inv.config.coinCutoff = false inv.save() inv.warn("this game does not accept 'get all "..badDenom.." coins' — " .."falling back to 'get all money' and taking every denomination from now on. " .."Re-enable with 'iloot coins on' if that was a fluke.") end -- NOT gated on inv.loot.active: a coins-only room creates no issued -- entries, so the run has already closed by the time the refusal lands. -- The flag is what says we sent the selective form, and it is the only -- thing that matters here. if inv.loot.coinSelective then inv.loot.coinSelective = nil inv.lootEcho("get all money"); send("get all money", false) end return end
-- An active loot run owns the string it just sent, so it gets first claim: -- it knows the item, demotes the handle and re-issues down the ladder. This -- has to come before the guesswork below, which cannot see a room item -- whose type key ("piece of cerbie's skin") does not contain the handle -- ("cerbie's skin") — the exact shape that left the bad handle in place. if inv.loot.active and inv.lootHandleRefused(h) then return end
-- A staging move owns the string it just sent, the same way: it knows the -- type, demotes the refused bag handle and re-sends down the ladder. Comes -- before the world-guesswork below because a bagged type's handle can be a -- word its display name never contains, so the loose/room scan cannot find it. if inv.moveInFlight and inv.moveHandleRefused(h) then return end
-- otherwise: whichever tracked type this handle was meant for, the handle -- does not name it. Demote it rather than blaming the item. local hit
-- The get that failed may have been aimed INSIDE a bag -- ('get sized sack from "loot"'), and neither the loose list nor the room -- scan can see in there. So a bad handle for a bagged type was never -- demoted, and ishop re-sent the same dead handle on every run forever. -- The command we sent is the authoritative owner of the handle — ask the -- in-flight job before guessing from the world. local ij = inv.shopJob if ij and ij.key and ij.handle and ij.handle:lower() == h then hit = ij.key end local isj = inv.sacInFlight if not hit and isj and isj.key and isj.handle and isj.handle:lower() == h then hit = isj.key end
for _, key in ipairs(inv.loc.loose or {}) do if hit then break end local hs = inv.handlesOf(key) if hs and hs.ok[h] then hit = key; break end end if not hit and inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.lines then for _, it in ipairs(inv.roomScan.lines) do local k = inv.key(it.name) local hs = k and inv.handlesOf(k) if hs and hs.ok[h] then hit = k; break end end end if not hit and inv.types[h] then hit = h end -- The loot run has already cleared the floor of these, so "You see no 'X'" -- is a true statement about the room. Demoting on it burns a handle that -- just worked — and a few of those leave the type with no ladder at all. if hit and inv.lootFloorEmptied(hit) then return end if hit then -- handleFailedAction, not handleRecordBad: if the prober was the only -- thing that ever blessed this string, say so out loud. That asymmetry is -- otherwise invisible, and it is the reason the string was ever sent. if not inv.handleFailedAction(hit, h, "get") then inv.note(string.format("'%s' does not name %s — handle dropped.", h, (inv.types[hit] and inv.types[hit].name) or hit)) end end end
-- Undo a wrongly learned non-item. function inv.includeItem(nameRaw) local key = inv.key(nameRaw) or (nameRaw or ""):lower() local hits = {} for k in pairs(inv.config.nonItems) do if k == key or k:find(key, 1, true) then hits[#hits+1] = k end end if #hits == 0 then inv.warn("'"..tostring(nameRaw).."' is not on the non-item list."); return end for _, k in ipairs(hits) do inv.config.nonItems[k] = nil inv.lootSay("will loot '"..k.."' again.") end inv.save() end -- "The <sack> is full." -> mark that bag full (we infer which from context) function inv.onBagFull(sackDesc) local nm = sackDesc and (sackDesc:match('named "([^"]+)"')) local key = nm and nm:lower() or inv.loot.lastBag if key then inv.bagFull[key] = true; inv.lootSay("<yellow>"..key.." is full<reset>") end end -- "There is no room for X, Y and Z." -> those items didn't fit; current bag full function inv.onNoRoom(listText) if inv.loot.lastBag then inv.bagFull[inv.loot.lastBag] = true end inv.lootSay("<yellow>bag full; retrying in next bag<reset>") -- if this fires during an ishop pull, the item couldn't come loose if inv.shop and inv.shop.pendingValueKey then inv.warn(string.format("can't pull %s loose (no volume) — skipping value", inv.shop.pendingValueKey)) inv.shop.pendingValueKey = nil inv.shop.pullFailed = true end if inv.loot.active then for _, it in ipairs(inv.splitItemList(listText)) do -- Retire the attempt that bounced before re-issuing, or the weigh gate -- waits on a reply that has already arrived. The handle is NOT added to -- `tried`: a full bag says nothing about whether the string was right. inv.lootClaim("key", inv.key(it.name)) inv.lootGetToBag(it.name) end inv.lootMaybeWeigh() end end
-- ============================================================ -- Shop disposal: ishop -- ============================================================ -- At a shop, for items currently in the disposal bags (and loose): -- * unknown value -> `value <ref>` to learn the price (pull loose first if -- the shop can't value bagged items). Once valued, route on next pass. -- * sell-route, established or not -> `sell <ref>` -- * sac-route -> deferred to an altar (ishop only sells; sacrifice at altar) -- Because `value` only reaches LOOSE items, unknowns are pulled loose, valued, -- and left loose for you to re-run; known-sell items are sold from wherever. -- Every command echoed; acts immediately.
function inv.shopEcho(c) cecho("\n<grey>[ishop]<reset> <cyan>"..c.."<reset>") end function inv.shopSay(m) cecho("\n<grey>[ishop]<reset> "..m) end
-- Build a list of {key,name,container,disp} for everything in loose+bags. function inv.disposablesList() local out, seen = {}, {} local function scan(container) local counted = {} for _,key in ipairs(inv.loc[container] or {}) do if not counted[key] then counted[key] = true local t = inv.types[key] if t then out[#out+1] = { key=key, name=t.name, container=container, disp=inv.classify(key), count=inv.locCount(container,key) } end end end end scan("loose") for sack in pairs(inv.config.disposalSacks) do scan(sack) end return out end
function inv.ishopRun(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if inv.shopJob or #(inv.shopQueue or {}) > 0 then inv.warn("an appraisal run is already in progress."); return end inv.currentShopNPC = nil -- re-learned from the first reply of this run inv.ensureFresh(function() inv.ishopProbe(arg) end) end
-- A shop cycle is get/value/put, all addressed by handle. Sending an unproven -- handle burns the whole cycle, so learn them first — bagged items can be -- probed in place with `l <handle> in "<bag>"`. -- `show id inventory` gives the exact handle for every LOOSE item in one -- command, so the look-probe ladder only has to cover BAGGED items (which show -- id cannot reach). Bag contents are still tracked by get/put echoes. function inv.ishopProbe(arg) local function afterId() if not inv.config.probeAuto then return inv.ishopGo(arg) end local q, seen = {}, {} for _, e in ipairs(inv.disposablesList()) do if e.key and not seen[e.key] and not inv.coinInfo(e.key) and not inv.handleKnown(e.key) and not inv.handleProbed(e.key) then seen[e.key] = true; q[#q+1] = e.key end end if #q == 0 then return inv.ishopGo(arg) end inv.probeQueue = q inv.shopSay(string.format("learning handles for %d bagged type(s)...", #q)) inv.probeQueueRun(function() inv.ishopGo(arg) end) end if inv.config.useShowId then inv.showIdRun("inventory", afterId) else afterId() end end
-- Runs once every disposal sack's contents have been verified this session. function inv.ishopGo(arg) local list = inv.disposablesList() if #list == 0 then inv.shopSay("nothing in loose or disposal bags to process."); return end inv.shop = inv.shop or {} inv.shop.pendingValueKey = nil
local valued, sold, deferred, skipped = 0, 0, 0, 0 for _, e in ipairs(list) do -- Route on disposeRoute, NOT classify: the bags are here to empty, so the -- pick-up cutoff does not apply. Anything with a sale value is sold however -- cheap; favour-only and worthless items are the altar run's job. local route = inv.disposeRoute(e.key) local t = inv.types[e.key] local sacOnly = t and t.sellCat and inv.config.sacOnlyCats and inv.config.sacOnlyCats[t.sellCat] if route == "coin" then -- coins go to ibank
elseif inv.config.nonItems[e.key] then -- learned non-item (mob/fixture) — skip silently skipped = skipped + 1
elseif route == "sac" or route == "drop" then -- favour-only (hearts, food) or worth nothing at all: a shop deals in -- neither, so hold it for isac, which sacrifices it or drops it. deferred = deferred + 1
elseif sacOnly then -- A KNOWN sac-only category (food, hearts) is never bought by any shop, so -- appraising one here is a wasted get/value/put every single run — the -- keeper just repeats "I don't buy food stuff" and we put it straight -- back. Its disposeRoute "unknown" means "favour not measured yet", and -- that reading comes from the ALTAR, not a keeper. Hold it for isac. -- (A brand-new heart type has no sellCat yet, so it still gets one shop -- appraisal — which is how it LEARNS it is food — and is deferred after.) deferred = deferred + 1
elseif route == "unknown" then -- Appraisal needs the item LOOSE, so this is a get/value/put cycle. -- Queued rather than fired immediately: an unpaced burst turns one bad -- handle or one stale map entry into a cascade of failures with no way -- to tell which command each reply belonged to. -- -- If the item is bagged and we cannot build a fetch for it, the whole -- cycle is pointless: `value` only reaches loose items. Skip it rather -- than sending a command the game will always refuse. local fromBag = (e.container ~= "loose") local getRef, getHandle, getIdxRef -- index requested: this is the fetch, and its echo names what arrived if fromBag then getRef, getHandle, getIdxRef = inv.bagRef(e.container, e.key, true) end if fromBag and not getRef then inv.shopSay(string.format("cannot reach %s in \"%s\" — skipped.", (inv.types[e.key] and inv.types[e.key].name) or e.key, e.container)) skipped = skipped + 1 else local job = { key = e.key, container = e.container, handle = getHandle, ref = getIdxRef } if getRef then job.getCmd = "get " .. getRef end -- The item will be loose by the time `value` runs, but refFor("loose") -- would see count=0 at build time, so take the best handle directly. local vref = inv.bestHandle(e.key) job.vref = inv.safeHandle(vref, e.key, "loose", false) or vref -- The put-back is NOT built here. It used to be, from -- handleShortest() — the shortest handle ever confirmed for the type, -- chosen with no ambiguity check at all. For an "Empty medium sized -- sack" that resolved to bare `sack`, which in a pack holding three -- named sacks and a sack of oil reached the WRONG object: `get sized -- sack from "loot"` failed and `put sack in "loot"` then filed the -- character's lamp oil away in the disposal bag. -- It is now built in shopPutBack() at step time, from the handle that -- actually fetched the item, and only when something fetched it. job.putBack = (job.getCmd ~= nil) inv.shopQueue[#inv.shopQueue+1] = job valued = valued + 1 end
elseif route == "sell" then -- One `sell` moves ONE item, so eleven skins need eleven commands — and -- they belong in the paced queue like everything else. Fired loose -- alongside the appraisals, their replies advanced the appraisal queue -- early and prices landed on whichever item was in flight by then. if inv.shopRejectsItem(e.key) then skipped = skipped + 1 elseif inv.config.bulkSell and e.container ~= "loose" and e.container ~= "keep" then -- Bulk sale: leave it in the bag and empty the whole bag with one -- `sell all from "<bag>"` after appraisals finish. Each sold line still -- names and prices the item, so nothing is lost; the sac-routed items -- are staged out of the sale bags first so the vendor cannot buy them. sold = sold + (e.count or 1) elseif not inv.shopRejectsItem(e.key) then local ref, hnd = inv.bagRef(e.container, e.key) if ref then -- `sell <h> from "<bag>"` was seen reaching a LOOSE item of another -- type, so a sale handle must be unambiguous in both places. local lh = inv.shortestHandle("loose", e.key) local function wc(x) local n = 0 for _ in (x or ""):gmatch("%S+") do n = n + 1 end; return n end if lh and wc(lh) > wc(hnd) then hnd = lh local meta = inv.contMeta[e.container] ref = (e.container == "loose") and lh or string.format('%s from "%s"', lh, (meta and meta.name) or e.container) end for _ = 1, (e.count or 1) do inv.shopQueue[#inv.shopQueue+1] = { kind = "sell", key = e.key, container = e.container, handle = hnd, sellCmd = "sell " .. ref, } end sold = sold + (e.count or 1) else skipped = skipped + 1 end else skipped = skipped + 1 end end end local msg = string.format("%d to appraise, %d sold, %d await altar", valued, sold, deferred) if skipped > 0 then msg = msg..string.format(", skipped %d (wrong shop)", skipped) end inv.shopSay(msg..".") if #inv.shopQueue > 0 then inv.shopMisses, inv.shopValued = 0, 0 inv.shopValueNext() elseif inv.config.bulkSell then -- No appraisals to run, so the bags are already all-decided: go straight to -- staging + the bulk sell. (When appraisals DO run, shopValueDone chains -- here instead, once every unknown has a price.) inv.shopBulkPhase() end end
-- Stage sac-routed items out of the sale bags, then empty each remaining sale -- bag with a single `sell all from "<bag>"`. Shared by ishopGo (no-appraisal -- case) and shopValueDone (post-appraisal case). function inv.shopBulkPhase() if not inv.config.bulkSell then return end -- saleBagsOnly: at a shop we only clear the SALE bags. shopRisk: and only the -- sac items this keeper could actually buy — food/hearts and refused -- categories the vendor won't touch anyway, so they stay put. Loose/keep sac -- items are staged at the altar by isac. inv.stageSacItems(function() inv.bulkSellRun() end, true, true) end
-- Fire `sell all from "<bag>"` for each non-empty sale bag, one bag at a time. inv.bulkSellPending = nil inv.bulkSellActive = nil inv.bulkSellTimer = nil
function inv.bulkSellRun() local dst = inv.config.sacStageBag or "treasure" local bags = {} for sack in pairs(inv.config.disposalSacks or {}) do if sack ~= dst and #(inv.loc[sack] or {}) > 0 then bags[#bags+1] = sack end end table.sort(bags) inv.bulkSellPending = bags inv.bulkSellStep() end
function inv.bulkSellStep() if inv.bulkSellTimer then killTimer(inv.bulkSellTimer); inv.bulkSellTimer = nil end local sack = table.remove(inv.bulkSellPending or {}, 1) if not sack then inv.bulkSellPending, inv.bulkSellActive = nil, nil inv.save() return end inv.bulkSellActive = sack local cmd = string.format('sell all from "%s"', inv.sackName(sack)) inv.shopEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) -- The per-item "You sell X for N silver." lines record price + prune the map -- via the existing Sold trigger; the total line advances us. Backstop in case -- the shop buys nothing (no total line at all). inv.bulkSellTimer = tempTimer(8, function() if inv.bulkSellActive == sack then inv.bulkSellActive = nil inv.deferStep(inv.bulkSellStep) end end) end
-- "<Keeper> says: ... you sold items for a total worth of N silver." or -- "<Keeper> gives you money worth of N silver." — a bulk sale finished. The -- line names the keeper, so learn it (the only shop-name evidence when a run -- had no appraisals to fire "You show the item to X."). function inv.onBulkSellTotal(name, silver) if name and name ~= "" then inv.currentShopNPC = name end if not inv.bulkSellActive then return end inv.bulkSellActive = nil if inv.bulkSellTimer then killTimer(inv.bulkSellTimer); inv.bulkSellTimer = nil end inv.shopSay(string.format("sold the bag for <green>%s<reset> silver.", tostring(silver))) inv.deferStep(inv.bulkSellStep) end
-- ibulk: show or toggle the bulk-disposal switches. function inv.bulkCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", ""):lower() local which, val = arg:match("^(%a+)%s+(%a+)$") local function onoff(s) if s == "on" or s == "true" or s == "yes" then return true elseif s == "off" or s == "false" or s == "no" then return false end return nil end if which == "sell" and onoff(val) ~= nil then inv.config.bulkSell = onoff(val); inv.save() elseif which == "sac" and onoff(val) ~= nil then inv.config.bulkSac = onoff(val); inv.save() elseif arg ~= "" then inv.warn("usage: ibulk | ibulk sell on/off | ibulk sac on/off"); return end cecho(string.format( "\n<cyan>Bulk disposal<reset>\n sell all: %s\n sacrifice all: %s\n stage bag: \"%s\"\n", inv.config.bulkSell and "<green>on<reset>" or "<yellow>off<reset>", inv.config.bulkSac and "<green>on<reset>" or "<yellow>off<reset>", inv.config.sacStageBag or "treasure")) end
-- ---- Paced appraisal -------------------------------------------------- inv.shopQueue = inv.shopQueue or {} inv.shopJob = nil inv.shopMisses = 0 inv.shopValued = 0 inv.shopTimer = nil
function inv.shopValueNext() if inv.shopTimer then killTimer(inv.shopTimer); inv.shopTimer = nil end local j = table.remove(inv.shopQueue, 1) if not j then return inv.shopValueDone() end inv.shopJob = j inv.shop = inv.shop or {} inv.shop.pendingValueKey = j.key if j.kind == "sell" then inv.shopEcho(j.sellCmd); send(j.sellCmd, false) else -- Rebuild the fetch NOW rather than trusting the one built when the queue -- was assembled. A positional index is only true of the bag as it stands, -- and the bag moves under us constantly: every put-back returns an item to -- the FRONT of the stow order, so an index computed three jobs ago is -- describing a container that no longer exists. Recomputing costs nothing -- and removes the entire class of stale-reference bugs. if j.container and j.container ~= "loose" and j.container ~= "keep" and (j.getCmd or j.needsFetch) then local ref, bare, idxRef = inv.bagRef(j.container, j.key, true) if ref then j.getCmd, j.handle, j.ref = "get "..ref, bare, idxRef if not j.vref then local v = inv.bestHandle(j.key) j.vref = inv.safeHandle(v, j.key, "loose", false) or v end j.putBack = true end end if j.getCmd then inv.shopEcho(j.getCmd); send(j.getCmd, false) end inv.shopEcho("value "..j.vref); send("value "..j.vref, false) -- The put-back waits for the appraisal outcome (see shopPutBack). Sent -- here, in the same burst, it went out even when the get had failed — -- and a put whose item never left the bag can only reach something else. end inv.shopTimer = tempTimer(8, function() if inv.shopJob == j then inv.shopStep(false, "no reply") end end) end
-- Called by the appraisal outcomes: a price quote, a vendor refusal, or -- "You do not have <item>." (which means the get never landed). -- Return a fetched item to its bag. Two rules, both learned the hard way: -- * only if it actually came out. `ok` means an appraisal outcome landed, -- which it cannot do while the item is still bagged; the location-map -- check covers a successful get whose `value` reply we then missed. -- * with the handle that FETCHED it. That handle is proven to name this -- object; the shortest known handle is not, and `put` is scoped to the -- whole pack, where short handles collide with everything. -- `i weight` reads LOOSE inventory only, and the one moment a bagged item is -- loose is right here — between the get that fetched it for appraisal and the -- put that returns it. Nothing used to measure it there, so a type that -- reached a bag without ever passing through your hands never acquired a -- volume; and with no volume, classify cannot compute silver-per-litre, so it -- returns "unknown" forever. That is not a cosmetic gap: an "unknown" is -- pulled out, shown to the keeper and stowed again on EVERY ishop run, and -- isac will not route it at all. A Bloodstone with 18,004 silver and 2,688 DF -- both recorded sat in "loot" doing exactly that. -- -- One extra command per unsized type, once ever — the condition is -- self-limiting, because the reply is what fills the volume in. function inv.shopSizeIfNeeded(j) if not (j and j.key) then return false end if inv.loot.active then return false end -- would trip the loot sort if inv.coinInfo(j.key) then return false end local t = inv.types[j.key] -- `or t.volume == 0`: a stored zero is a legacy sub-resolution reading (see -- scanItem) and is useless to classify, so it still needs measuring. if not t or (t.volume and t.volume > 0) then return false end inv.shopSay(string.format("<grey>sizing %s while it is out<reset>", t.name or j.key)) -- One-shot, and it expires: a flag that leaked onto a later scan would -- silently suppress that scan's reconciliation, which is the one thing -- keeping the location map honest. inv.sizingScan = true if inv.sizingTimer then killTimer(inv.sizingTimer) end inv.sizingTimer = tempTimer(6, function() inv.sizingScan = nil end) inv.shopEcho("i weight"); send("i weight", false) return true end
function inv.shopPutBack(j, ok) if not j or not j.putBack or not j.container then return end if not (ok or inv.locCount("loose", j.key) > 0) then inv.shopSay(string.format( "%s never left \"%s\" — not putting anything back.", (inv.types[j.key] and inv.types[j.key].name) or j.key, j.container)) return end -- Everything below is about the object actually in hand, which is not always -- the one we asked for (see the collision check in onGetEcho). Size THAT, -- and file THAT under the bag it is going back into. local holding = j.heldKey or j.key inv.shopSizeIfNeeded({ key = holding }) local meta = inv.contMeta[j.container] local sack = (meta and meta.name) or j.container local h = j.handle or inv.handleShortest(j.key) or j.key h = inv.safeHandle(h, j.key, "loose", true) or h local cmd = string.format('put %s in "%s"', h, sack) table.insert(inv.pendingPuts, { key = holding, sackKey = j.container }) inv.shopEcho(cmd); send(cmd, false) end
function inv.shopStep(ok, why) local j = inv.shopJob if not j then return end inv.shopJob = nil if inv.shopTimer then killTimer(inv.shopTimer); inv.shopTimer = nil end inv.shopPutBack(j, ok) if ok then -- The item came out of the bag and was appraised, so whatever handle we -- used demonstrably works: this type is no longer waiting on a human. inv.clearStuck(j.key) inv.shopMisses = 0 inv.shopValued = (inv.shopValued or 0) + 1 else inv.shopMisses = (inv.shopMisses or 0) + 1 if inv.shopMisses >= 3 then local left = #inv.shopQueue inv.shopQueue = {} inv.warn(string.format( "3 appraisals in a row failed (%s) — stopped, dropped %d. Try 'iprobe all', " .."or 'iclean confirm' if the location map has drifted.", why or "?", left)) return inv.shopValueDone() end end inv.deferStep(inv.shopValueNext) end
-- "You do not have <item>." — the pull out of the bag never landed, so the -- map's claim that an instance is in there is wrong. Prune it. function inv.onNotCarried() local j = inv.shopJob if not j then return end if j.kind == "sell" then return inv.shopStep(false, "sale failed") end -- Same two causes as a failed sacrifice: try the next handle once before -- deciding the bag does not hold it. if j.getCmd and j.handle then local tried = j.tried or {} tried[j.handle] = true local n = 0 for _ in pairs(tried) do n = n + 1 end local alt = (n <= inv.HANDLE_RETRIES) and inv.nextHandleAfter(j.key, tried) or nil if not alt then -- Out of candidates. Every string the ladder can build has now been -- refused, so this needs a human: see inv.markStuck. inv.markStuck(j.key, string.format("get failed, last tried '%s'", j.handle), j.container) end if alt then inv.shopJob = nil if inv.shopTimer then killTimer(inv.shopTimer); inv.shopTimer = nil end for i, p in ipairs(inv.pendingPuts) do if p.key == j.key then table.remove(inv.pendingPuts, i); break end end local meta = inv.contMeta[j.container] local sackName = (meta and meta.name) or j.container inv.shopSay(string.format("'%s' fetched nothing — retrying as '%s'", j.handle, alt)) table.insert(inv.shopQueue, 1, { key = j.key, container = j.container, handle = alt, tried = tried, getCmd = string.format('get %s from "%s"', alt, sackName), vref = alt, putCmd = string.format('put %s in "%s"', alt, j.container), }) return inv.deferStep(inv.shopValueNext) end end -- Only evidence of a phantom if we actually tried to fetch it. Without a -- get, "You do not have" just means we never picked it up — pruning there -- would eat a real entry on every run. if j.getCmd and j.container and j.container ~= "loose" then inv.locRemove(j.container, j.key, 1) inv.note(string.format("'%s' is not in \"%s\" — pruned.", (inv.types[j.key] and inv.types[j.key].name) or j.key, j.container)) end for i, p in ipairs(inv.pendingPuts) do if p.key == j.key then table.remove(inv.pendingPuts, i); break end end inv.save() inv.shopStep(false, "not carried") end
-- "That is not worth anything." — a real appraisal of zero, not a refusal. -- Unrecorded, the item stayed "unknown" and was pulled out, shown and -- restowed on every single ishop run. function inv.onWorthless() local k = inv.shop and inv.shop.pendingValueKey if k then local t = inv.getType(k, (inv.types[k] and inv.types[k].name) or k) if t then t.sell = inv.ema(t.sell, 0) inv.note(string.format("%s: appraised at 0 silver.", t.name or k)) inv.save() end end inv.shopStep(true) end
-- "<Item> has no value." — the shop appraises it at zero, and it NAMES the -- item. If that is not the item we asked for, our handle reached something -- else: the same evidence the altar's echo gives us. -- Does this loose name plausibly describe that type? ("Spider skin" vs -- "piece of spider's skin": every word of the name appears in the key.) local nameFits = inv.nameFits -- one definition, promoted for onValueRaw's use
function inv.onNoValue(nameRaw) local j = inv.shopJob local named = inv.key(nameRaw) local key = (named and inv.types[named]) and named or inv.resolveFragment(nameRaw) if not key and j and nameFits(nameRaw, j.key) then key = j.key end
if j and key and key ~= j.key then -- The shop named something we did not ask for, so the handle reached the -- wrong item. Blame the handle and try a better one rather than counting -- this against the run. if j.handle then inv.handleRecordAmb(j.key, j.handle, (j.container and j.container ~= "loose") and ("container:"..j.container) or "inventory") inv.shopSay(string.format("'%s' reached %s instead — marked ambiguous.", j.handle, (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key)) inv.requeueHandle(j.key) end local tried = j.tried or {} if j.handle then tried[j.handle] = true end local n = 0 for _ in pairs(tried) do n = n + 1 end local alt = (n <= inv.HANDLE_RETRIES) and inv.nextHandleAfter(j.key, tried) or nil if not alt then -- Out of handles for this item.
