That is a problem with this ITEM, not -- with the run: drop its remaining commands and carry on with the rest. local dropped, kept = 0, {} for _, q in ipairs(inv.shopQueue) do if q.key == j.key then dropped = dropped + 1 else kept[#kept+1] = q end end inv.shopQueue = kept inv.shopSay(string.format("no working handle for %s — skipped it%s.", (inv.types[j.key] and inv.types[j.key].name) or j.key, dropped > 0 and (" and "..dropped.." more") or "")) return inv.shopStep(true) end if alt and j.kind == "sell" then inv.shopJob = nil if inv.shopTimer then killTimer(inv.shopTimer); inv.shopTimer = nil end local ref = alt if j.container and j.container ~= "loose" and j.container ~= "keep" then local meta = inv.contMeta[j.container] ref = string.format('%s from "%s"', alt, (meta and meta.name) or j.container) end inv.shopSay(string.format("retrying the sale as '%s'", alt)) table.insert(inv.shopQueue, 1, { kind = "sell", key = j.key, container = j.container, handle = alt, tried = tried, sellCmd = "sell " .. ref }) -- and fix every other command still queued for this item for _, q in ipairs(inv.shopQueue) do if q.key == j.key and q ~= inv.shopQueue[1] and not q.tried then q.handle = alt if q.kind == "sell" then q.sellCmd = "sell " .. ref end end end return inv.deferStep(inv.shopValueNext) end return inv.shopStep(false, "wrong item reached") end
if not key then return inv.shopStep(true) end if key then local t = inv.getType(key, (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or nameRaw) if t then t.sell = inv.ema(t.sell, 0) inv.note(string.format("%s: this shop values it at 0.", t.name or key)) end -- nothing else of this type is worth offering here local dropped, kept = 0, {} for _, q in ipairs(inv.shopQueue) do if q.kind == "sell" and q.key == key then dropped = dropped + 1 else kept[#kept+1] = q end end if dropped > 0 then inv.shopQueue = kept inv.shopSay(string.format("worth nothing here — dropped %d more sale(s).", dropped)) end inv.save() end inv.shopStep(true) end
-- "You do not seem to have any <item>." is the game's reply when a SELL is -- aimed at something that is not (reachably) there. It matches NO other trigger -- ("Not carried" is "You do not have X.", a different string), so it fell -- through and a phantom was retried on every run and never pruned. -- -- But the line has the same two causes as a failed sacrifice: the item is not -- there, OR the handle does not name it. Those need opposite responses: -- * an ACTION-PROVEN handle failing means the item genuinely is gone — a real -- phantom (a chain mail suit already sold, a stale "armour" bucket). Prune. -- * a GUESSED handle failing means the item may still be here under a handle -- we have not tried — the drained oil sack answers only to `sack of oil`, -- never to the ladder's `sized sack`. Walk the ladder; if it runs out, mark -- the type STUCK for `ihandle` rather than deleting a real item. function inv.onNoSuchItem(nameRaw) local j = inv.shopJob if j then local key = j.key local h = j.handle local proven = h and inv.handleActProven and inv.handleActProven(key, h)
if h and not proven then -- a guess reached nothing: try the next handle before blaming the map local tried = j.tried or {}; tried[h] = true local n = 0; for _ in pairs(tried) do n = n + 1 end local alt = (n <= inv.HANDLE_RETRIES) and inv.nextHandleAfter(key, tried) or nil if alt then inv.shopJob = nil if inv.shopTimer then killTimer(inv.shopTimer); inv.shopTimer = nil end for i = #(inv.pendingPuts or {}), 1, -1 do if inv.pendingPuts[i].key == key then table.remove(inv.pendingPuts, i) end end local ref = alt if j.container and j.container ~= "loose" and j.container ~= "keep" then local meta = inv.contMeta[j.container] ref = string.format('%s from "%s"', alt, (meta and meta.name) or j.container) end local nj = { key = key, container = j.container, handle = alt, tried = tried } if j.kind == "sell" then nj.kind = "sell"; nj.sellCmd = "sell " .. ref else nj.getCmd = "get " .. ref; nj.vref = alt; nj.needsFetch = true end table.insert(inv.shopQueue, 1, nj) inv.shopSay(string.format("'%s' reached nothing — retrying as '%s'", h, alt)) return inv.deferStep(inv.shopValueNext) end -- out of handles: the item is probably here but unreachable, so surface -- it for `ihandle` instead of pruning a real item off the map. inv.markStuck(key, string.format("nothing answered '%s'", h), j.container) local kept, dropped = {}, 0 for _, q in ipairs(inv.shopQueue) do if q.key == key then dropped = dropped + 1 else kept[#kept+1] = q end end inv.shopQueue = kept j.putBack = nil inv.shopSay(string.format("no working handle for %s — left it, flagged for 'ihandle'%s.", (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key, dropped > 0 and (", dropped "..dropped.." more") or "")) inv.save() return inv.shopStep(true) end
-- a proven handle failed (or we had none): the item genuinely is not here. if j.container and j.container ~= "loose" and j.container ~= "keep" then if inv.locCount(j.container, key) > 0 then inv.locRemove(j.container, key, 1) end elseif inv.locCount("loose", key) > 0 then inv.locRemove("loose", key, 1) end local kept, dropped = {}, 0 for _, q in ipairs(inv.shopQueue) do if q.key == key then dropped = dropped + 1 else kept[#kept+1] = q end end inv.shopQueue = kept j.putBack = nil for i = #(inv.pendingPuts or {}), 1, -1 do if inv.pendingPuts[i].key == key then table.remove(inv.pendingPuts, i) end end inv.shopSay(string.format("'%s' not here — pruned the phantom%s.", (inv.types[key] and inv.types[key].name) or key, dropped > 0 and (", dropped "..dropped.." more") or "")) inv.save() return inv.shopStep(true) end -- during isac the same line means the queued sacrifice is not there if inv.sacInFlight then return inv.onSacNothing() end end
-- "You sold nothing." — the sale did not happen. Usually preceded by the -- vendor's refusal, which has already advanced the queue; harmless either way -- because a second advance for one reply is ignored. function inv.onNoSale() -- A shop declining is a perfectly good answer, not a malfunction. Counting -- it as a failure aborted the whole run after three refusals. inv.shopStep(true) end
function inv.shopValueDone() inv.shopJob = nil inv.shopQueue = {} if inv.shopTimer then killTimer(inv.shopTimer); inv.shopTimer = nil end inv.save() if (inv.shopValued or 0) > 0 then if inv.config.bulkSell then inv.shopSay(string.format("appraised %d item(s) — selling the now-priced ones next.", inv.shopValued)) else inv.shopSay(string.format("appraised %d item(s) — re-run ishop to route the newly-priced ones.", inv.shopValued)) end end inv.shopValued = 0 inv.stuckNag() -- Appraisal done -> every item is now decided. Stage the altar-bound ones out -- and empty each sale bag in one command. Deferred so this run's final -- appraisal outcome is fully processed before the moves start. if inv.config.bulkSell then inv.deferStep(inv.shopBulkPhase) end end
-- ============================================================ -- Altar disposal: isac -- ============================================================ -- At an altar, sacrifice everything currently routed "sac" (best route is -- sacrifice) from loose + disposal bags, one at a time so favour is learned. -- ============================================================ -- Banking: ibank (run at the bank) -- ============================================================ -- Coins are kept LOOSE (bag compression is small and breaks value-reading). -- A 500-mithril reserve lives BAGGED in "treasure". Since `deposit` only -- touches LOOSE money (never reaches into bags unless a container is named), -- the treasure reserve is automatically protected. So ibank simply deposits -- all loose coins — no reserve arithmetic needed. inv.bankKeepMithril = inv.bankKeepMithril or 500 function inv.bankEcho(c) cecho("\n<grey>[ibank]<reset> <cyan>"..c.."<reset>"); send(c, false) end
function inv.ibankRun() local keepBag = inv.config.treasureBag or "treasure" inv.bankEcho("deposit all") cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[ibank]<reset> deposited all loose coins. The mithril reserve in \"%s\" is untouched (deposit can't reach bagged coins).", keepBag)) end
-- ============================================================ -- Group mode: igroup -- ============================================================ -- A flag plus actions. When ON, iloot routes likely-high-DF (glowing) items to -- the treasure sack for fair favour-division; everything else is sold and the -- silver shared by depositing to the bank. `igroup` actions trigger at the -- relevant location: at a shop it sells the non-glowing disposables; at the -- bank it deposits the shared silver. function inv.isGlowItem(key) local t = inv.types[key] return t and t.glow ~= nil end
function inv.groupCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+",""):gsub("%s+$","") if arg == "on" then inv.config.groupMode = true; inv.save() cecho("\n<green>[igroup]<reset> group mode ON — glowing items -> \"treasure\" for division; rest sold & silver shared.\n") elseif arg == "off" then inv.config.groupMode = false; inv.save() cecho("\n<yellow>[igroup]<reset> group mode OFF.\n") elseif arg == "sell" then inv.groupSell() elseif arg == "deposit" then inv.bankEcho("deposit all") cecho("\n<grey>[igroup]<reset> deposited shared silver to bank.") else cecho(string.format("\n<cyan>[igroup]<reset> group mode is %s. Use: igroup on | off | sell | deposit\n", inv.config.groupMode and "ON" or "OFF")) end end
-- At a shop: sell all non-glowing disposables (glowing ones are kept for the -- group in treasure). Coins/known-sac items are left for their own routes. function inv.groupSell() local list = inv.disposablesList() local n = 0 for _, e in ipairs(list) do if not inv.coinInfo(e.key) and not inv.isGlowItem(e.key) and e.disp ~= "leave" and e.disp ~= "trash" then local ref = inv.refFor(e.container, e.key) or inv.shortestRoomHandle(e.name) local cmd = "sell "..ref cecho("\n<grey>[igroup]<reset> <cyan>"..cmd.."<reset>"); send(cmd, false) n = n + 1 end end cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[igroup]<reset> sold %d non-glowing item type(s); 'igroup deposit' to share the silver.", n)) end
-- ---- iprobe command --------------------------------------------------- function inv.probeCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") local C = inv.config
if arg == "auto on" or arg == "auto off" then C.probeAuto = (arg == "auto on"); inv.save() inv.warn("auto-probing during iloot: "..(C.probeAuto and "on" or "off")); return end if arg == "room on" or arg == "room off" then C.probeRoom = (arg == "room on"); inv.save() inv.warn("room probing before pickup: "..(C.probeRoom and "on" or "off")); return end if arg == "quiet on" or arg == "quiet off" then C.probeQuiet = (arg == "quiet on"); inv.save() inv.warn("probe output gagging: "..(C.probeQuiet and "on" or "off")); return end if arg == "stop" then if inv.probe then inv.probeAbort("stopped by user") else inv.warn("no probe running.") end inv.probeQueue = {}; return end if inv.probe then inv.warn("a probe is already running (iprobe stop to cancel)."); return end
-- iprobe -> drain whatever is queued -- iprobe all -> queue every unprobed type currently loose or in room -- iprobe <name> -> re-probe one item now, even if already probed if arg == "" then if #inv.probeQueue == 0 then inv.warn("probe queue is empty. Try 'iprobe all' or 'iprobe NAME'."); return end cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[iprobe]<reset> draining queue: %d type(s)...\n", #inv.probeQueue)) return inv.probeQueueRun() end
if arg == "all" then local q = {} local function consider(key) if key and not inv.coinInfo(key) and not inv.handleProbed(key) then for _, k in ipairs(q) do if k == key then return end end q[#q+1] = key end end -- everything we can currently see: loose, kept, inside any tracked bag -- (look reaches those with `in "<bag>"`), and the last room scan. for cont, list in pairs(inv.loc or {}) do if type(list) == "table" then for _, k in ipairs(list) do consider(k) end end end if inv.roomScan and inv.roomScan.lines then for _, it in ipairs(inv.roomScan.lines) do consider(inv.key(it.name)) end end if #q == 0 then inv.warn("nothing reachable needs probing."); return end inv.probeQueue = q cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[iprobe]<reset> probing %d loose type(s)...\n", #q)) return inv.probeQueueRun() end
if arg == "status" then local probed, total = 0, 0 for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do total = total + 1 if inv.handleProbed(k) then probed = probed + 1 end end cecho(string.format("\n<cyan>Handle knowledge:<reset> %d/%d types probed. auto=%s room=%s quiet=%s\n", probed, total, tostring(C.probeAuto), tostring(C.probeRoom), tostring(C.probeQuiet))) return end
-- name lookup: exact key first, then substring against stored display names local key = inv.key(arg) if not (key and inv.types[key]) then key = nil local needle = arg:lower() for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do if (t.name and t.name:lower():find(needle, 1, true)) or k:find(needle, 1, true) then key = k; break end end end if not key then inv.warn("no known item matching '"..arg.."'."); return end if not inv.probeStart(key, { source = "manual", force = true }) then inv.warn("could not start a probe for '"..arg.."'.") end end
-- ---- Sack verification ------------------------------------------------ -- A `look in "<sack>"` is only interpretable if we know WHICH sack it was: -- the reply header is just "This is a huge leather sack." and never carries -- the name. The only identifier is the command that was typed, captured by -- our alias — and if anything else in the profile claims `l`/`look` first, -- that capture silently never happens. -- -- So we no longer ask the user to type it. ishop/isac issue the look -- themselves, which means the key is never in doubt. inv.sackScanWaiting = nil inv.sackScanDone = nil inv.sackScanTimer = nil
function inv.expectSack(k) inv.curSackKey = k inv.sackScanWaiting = k end
-- Refresh loose inventory, then the disposal sacks, then call onDone. -- -- disposablesList has always included loose items, but nothing ever re-read -- them: the loose bucket only changed when iloot happened to run `i weight`. -- So an item picked up by hand, or left loose after a fight, was invisible to -- ishop and isac until something else refreshed it. inv.looseScanWaiting = false inv.looseScanDone = nil inv.looseScanTimer = nil
function inv.ensureFresh(onDone) if inv.looseScanWaiting then inv.warn("an inventory check is already running."); return end inv.looseScanWaiting = true inv.looseScanDone = function() inv.ensureSacksScanned(onDone) end cecho("\n<grey>[inv]<reset> checking loose inventory...\n") -- this scan IS a census and must reconcile, so make sure no stale sizing -- flag is left over to suppress it inv.sizingScan = nil if inv.sizingTimer then killTimer(inv.sizingTimer); inv.sizingTimer = nil end send("i weight", false) if inv.looseScanTimer then killTimer(inv.looseScanTimer) end inv.looseScanTimer = tempTimer(6, function() if inv.looseScanWaiting then inv.looseScanWaiting = false local f = inv.looseScanDone; inv.looseScanDone = nil inv.warn("no reply from 'i weight' — continuing without a loose refresh.") if f then f() end end end) end
-- Verify every disposal sack we believe has contents, then call onDone. function inv.ensureSacksScanned(onDone) if inv.sackScanWaiting then inv.warn("a container scan is already running."); return end local todo = {} for sack in pairs(inv.config.disposalSacks) do if inv.loc[sack] and #inv.loc[sack] > 0 and not inv.scannedSacks[sack] then todo[#todo+1] = sack end end table.sort(todo) if #todo == 0 then return onDone and onDone() end
local i = 0 local function step() i = i + 1 local sack = todo[i] if not sack then inv.sackScanWaiting, inv.sackScanDone = nil, nil if inv.sackScanTimer then killTimer(inv.sackScanTimer); inv.sackScanTimer = nil end return onDone and onDone() end inv.expectSack(sack) inv.sackScanDone = step cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[inv]<reset> verifying contents of \"%s\"...\n", sack)) -- `l "<sack>"` opens the container. `look in "<sack>"` is NOT the syntax -- for that — `in "<bag>"` is a modifier for finding an ITEM inside a bag. send(string.format('l "%s"', sack), false) if inv.sackScanTimer then killTimer(inv.sackScanTimer) end inv.sackScanTimer = tempTimer(6, function() if inv.sackScanWaiting == sack then inv.warn(string.format("no reply scanning \"%s\" — continuing without it.", sack)) inv.sackScanWaiting, inv.sackScanDone = nil, nil step() end end) end step() end
-- ---- Multi-item lines -------------------------------------------------- -- Icesus prints several room entries on ONE line joined by " and ": -- "Small wooden lottery console floating in the air and Street lamp" -- Ingesting that whole line as one item created composite junk types such as -- "heavy cloth shoes and iron dagger", which then poisoned every ambiguity -- check. Split on " and " only — never on commas, since item names contain -- them ("A spacy merchant booth, holding 3 items (Tormtor) and Street lamp"). -- One room line can list several items joined by " and ", so the line has to -- be split — but "and" is also an ordinary word inside a name, and splitting on -- every occurrence turned "Flint and steel" into a "Flint" and a "steel" and -- "Fishing rod with a line and a hook" into a rod and "a hook". None of those -- exist, so every one became a permanent phantom type that no listing ever -- matched again. -- -- The discriminator is capitalisation. A room listing prints each item's -- DISPLAY name, and those always begin with a capital or a digit: -- -- Heavy cloth shoes and Iron dagger -> two items -- Small wooden lottery console ... and Street lamp -> two items -- Flint and steel -> one item -- Fishing rod with a line and a hook -> one item -- -- So split only where the text after " and " starts a new display name. A -- line that is already a known type is never split at all, which covers any -- item whose name breaks the capitalisation habit once we have seen it once. -- Split at every " and " that begins a new DISPLAY name, leaving the ones that -- sit inside one alone. function inv.splitAndParts(raw) local s = (raw or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") if s == "" then return {} end local pieces, start, i = {}, 1, 1 while true do local a, b = s:find(" and ", i, true) if not a then break end local nxt = s:sub(b + 1, b + 1) if nxt:match("%u") or nxt:match("%d") then pieces[#pieces+1] = s:sub(start, a - 1) start = b + 1 end i = b end pieces[#pieces+1] = s:sub(start) local out = {} for _, p in ipairs(pieces) do p = p:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") if p ~= "" then out[#out+1] = p end end return out end
function inv.splitAndLine(raw) local whole = (raw or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") if whole == "" then return {} end -- A line that is already a known type is one item, whatever its name -- contains — this covers any display name that breaks the capitalisation -- habit, once we have seen it whole even once. local wk = inv.key(whole) if wk and inv.types[wk] then return { whole } end return inv.splitAndParts(whole) end
-- ---- Composite junk cleanup ------------------------------------------- function inv.cleanJunk(arg) -- "contains ' and '" was the old test, and it condemned the very names the -- splitter now protects: `iclean junk` would have deleted "Flint and steel" -- along with its price, its favour and its proven handles. A composite is a -- type the splitter would BREAK UP — a real name is one it leaves whole. local junk = {} for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do if k:find(" and ") and #inv.splitAndParts(t.name or k) > 1 then junk[#junk+1] = k end end table.sort(junk) if #junk == 0 then inv.warn("no composite junk types found."); return end if arg ~= "confirm" then cecho(string.format("\n<yellow>[inv]<reset> %d composite type(s). These came from room lines that " .."listed two items joined by \" and \", so their stored values are meaningless:\n", #junk)) for _, k in ipairs(junk) do cecho(" <grey>"..((inv.types[k] and inv.types[k].name) or k).."<reset>\n") end cecho("Type <cyan>iclean junk confirm<reset> to delete them.\n") return end for _, k in ipairs(junk) do inv.types[k] = nil for cont in pairs(inv.loc) do inv.reconcileCount(cont, k, 0) end inv.config.excludes[k] = nil inv.config.nonItems[k] = nil inv.tooHeavy[k] = nil end inv.save() cecho(string.format("\n<green>[inv]<reset> removed %d composite type(s).\n", #junk)) end
-- ---- isac ------------------------------------------------------------- function inv.isacRun(arg) if inv.sacBusy() then inv.warn("a sacrifice run is already in progress."); return end inv.sacLearnMode = ((arg or ""):gsub("%s+","") == "learn") inv.ensureFresh(function() inv.isacProbe() end) end
-- Same reasoning as ishop: a sacrifice is addressed by handle and consumes -- the item, so an unproven handle is the most expensive kind of mistake. function inv.isacProbe() local function afterId() if not inv.config.probeAuto then return inv.isacGo() end local q, seen = {}, {} for _, e in ipairs(inv.disposablesList()) do if e.key and not seen[e.key] and not inv.coinInfo(e.key) and not inv.handleKnown(e.key) and not inv.handleProbed(e.key) then seen[e.key] = true; q[#q+1] = e.key end end if #q == 0 then return inv.isacGo() end inv.probeQueue = q cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[isac]<reset> learning handles for %d bagged type(s)...\n", #q)) inv.probeQueueRun(function() inv.isacGo() end) end if inv.config.useShowId then inv.showIdRun("inventory", afterId) else afterId() end end
function inv.isacGo() -- Stage the altar-bound items into one bag first (idempotent — items already -- there are skipped), then dispose. Staging is what lets a bulk `sacrifice -- all from "<bag>"` target only sac items and never a sellable one. if inv.config.bulkSac and not inv.sacLearnMode then return inv.stageSacItems(function() inv.isacDispose() end) end inv.isacDispose() end
-- Decide the run: if EVERY altar-bound item is established (a reading already -- owed to none of them) and sitting in the stage bag, empty it in one command. -- Otherwise fall back to the proven per-item path, which learns the unlearned -- ones one at a time — exactly the old behaviour. function inv.isacDispose() local list = inv.disposablesList() inv.sacReset() inv.pendingDrops = {} local dst = inv.config.sacStageBag or "treasure" local estN = inv.config.estN or 3
-- Sacrifice the STAGE BAG first. disposablesList scans loose then the sacks, -- so stale phantom sac-entries in loose/loot (items long gone but never -- pruned -- the persistent "N await altar" count) were queued ahead of the -- items just staged into treasure this run. Three phantom "There was nothing -- to sacrifice" replies in a row then tripped the stale-map guard and dropped -- the rest of the queue -- stranding the real, freshly-staged items in the -- stage bag unsacrificed. Ordering the stage bag first means the known-present -- items are consumed before any phantom can trip the guard; the guard then -- only ever discards the trailing phantoms, which is what it is for. do local rank = function(c) return (c == dst) and 0 or (c == "loose" and 2 or 1) end for i, e in ipairs(list) do e._i = i end -- stable tiebreaker table.sort(list, function(a, b) local ra, rb = rank(a.container), rank(b.container) if ra ~= rb then return ra < rb end return a._i < b._i end) for _, e in ipairs(list) do e._i = nil end end
-- First pass: collect drops (needed either way) and test bulk eligibility. local canBulk, anySac = (inv.config.bulkSac and not inv.sacLearnMode), false for _, e in ipairs(list) do local t = inv.types[e.key] local route = inv.disposeRoute(e.key) local sacOnly = t and t.sellCat and inv.config.sacOnlyCats[t.sellCat] local wantsAltar = (route == "sac" or (route == "unknown" and sacOnly)) and not (t and t.noSac) if wantsAltar then anySac = true local established = t and t.sac and (t.sac.n or 0) >= estN if e.container ~= dst or not established then canBulk = false end elseif route == "drop" then inv.pendingDrops[#inv.pendingDrops+1] = { key = e.key, container = e.container, count = e.count } end end
if canBulk and anySac then return inv.sacBulkFire(dst) end
-- Per-item path (unchanged): learning sacrifices cost one item each. local learning = 0 for _, e in ipairs(list) do local t = inv.types[e.key] local route = inv.disposeRoute(e.key) local isSacOnly = t and t.sellCat and inv.config.sacOnlyCats[t.sellCat] local isLearning = (not (t and t.sac)) and (route == "sac" or (route == "unknown" and isSacOnly)) local needsDF = inv.sacLearnMode and not (t and t.sac) if (t and t.noSac) then -- on the keeplist: the altar refuses it, so do not ask elseif route == "sac" or (route == "unknown" and isSacOnly) or needsDF then local ref, hnd = inv.bagRef(e.container, e.key) local want = (isLearning or needsDF) and 1 or e.count if ref then for _ = 1, want do inv.sacEnqueue{ key = e.key, container = e.container, ref = ref, handle = hnd, learning = isLearning } if isLearning then learning = learning + 1 end end end end end local n = #inv.sacQueue if n == 0 then if #inv.pendingDrops > 0 then return inv.dropRun() end cecho("\n<grey>[isac]<reset> nothing routed for sacrifice.\n"); return end inv.sacStats = { done = 0, favour = 0, missing = 0 } cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[isac]<reset> %d sacrifice(s) queued (%d to learn DF), one at a time.\n", n, learning)) inv.sacSendNext() end
-- Empty the stage bag in one command. Only reached when every altar-bound item -- in it is established, so the lump favour need not be attributed to anything. -- We record exactly which established types were consumed so the location map -- can be corrected without a rescan (an established sac type has positive -- favour readings, so the altar accepts it — the assumption is safe, and a -- later scan self-heals if it is ever wrong). inv.sacBulk = nil inv.sacBulkTimer = nil
function inv.sacBulkFire(dst) local estN = inv.config.estN or 3 local consumed = {} for _, e in ipairs(inv.disposablesList()) do if e.container == dst then local t = inv.types[e.key] if t and t.sac and (t.sac.n or 0) >= estN and not t.noSac then consumed[#consumed+1] = { key = e.key, count = e.count or 1 } end end end inv.sacBulk = { dst = dst, consumed = consumed } local cmd = string.format('sacrifice all from "%s"', inv.sackName(dst)) cecho("\n<grey>[isac]<reset> <cyan>"..cmd.."<reset>") send(cmd, false) if inv.sacBulkTimer then killTimer(inv.sacBulkTimer) end inv.sacBulkTimer = tempTimer(10, function() if inv.sacBulk then inv.warn("no reply to the bulk sacrifice — assuming it completed.") inv.onSacBulkFinish(nil) end end) end
-- The altar answered a bulk sacrifice: one lump favour (or "nothing"). We do -- not re-attribute the favour (every item was already established), we just -- remove the consumed instances from the map and run any pending drops. function inv.onSacBulkFinish(n) local b = inv.sacBulk; inv.sacBulk = nil if inv.sacBulkTimer then killTimer(inv.sacBulkTimer); inv.sacBulkTimer = nil end if not b then return end n = tonumber(n) local dst = b.dst or (inv.config.sacStageBag or "treasure") local removed = 0 for _, c in ipairs(b.consumed or {}) do for _ = 1, (c.count or 1) do if inv.locRemove(dst, c.key, 1) then removed = removed + 1 end end end if n then cecho(string.format( "\n<grey>[isac]<reset> bulk sacrifice: <green>%d<reset> favour for %d established item(s) " .."(not re-attributed).\n", n, removed)) else cecho("\n<grey>[isac]<reset> bulk sacrifice: nothing was on the altar.\n") end inv.save() if inv.pendingDrops and #inv.pendingDrops > 0 then inv.dropRun() end inv.stuckNag() end
-- Clear worthless items (no sale value, no favour) out of the disposal flow. -- Loose ones are dropped directly. Bagged ones are only REPORTED: a blind -- `drop` from a bag would need a handle we cannot confirm, and mis-dropping a -- valuable item is unrecoverable, so those are left for a deliberate hand-drop. function inv.dropRun() local drops = inv.pendingDrops or {}; inv.pendingDrops = nil local dropped, bagged = 0, {} for _, d in ipairs(drops) do if d.container == "loose" or d.container == "keep" then local have = inv.locCount("loose", d.key) for _ = 1, math.min(have, d.count or have) do local h = inv.shortestHandle("loose", d.key) h = inv.safeHandle(h, d.key, "loose", true) or h or d.key cecho("\n<grey>[isac]<reset> <cyan>drop "..h.."<reset>"); send("drop "..h, false) dropped = dropped + 1 end else bagged[#bagged+1] = string.format("%s in \"%s\"", (inv.types[d.key] and inv.types[d.key].name) or d.key, d.container) end end if dropped > 0 then cecho(string.format("\n<grey>[isac]<reset> dropped <green>%d<reset> worthless item(s).\n", dropped)) end if #bagged > 0 then inv.warn(string.format( "%d worthless item(s) sit in a disposal bag (no sale or favour value): %s. " .."Pull them loose and `drop` by hand — I will not blind-drop from a bag.", #bagged, table.concat(bagged, "; "))) end inv.save() end
-- Appraisal outcome wrappers: the recording logic runs first, then the queue -- advances to the next item. function inv.onValue(itemRaw, silver) inv.onValueRaw(itemRaw, silver) inv.shopStep(true) end
function inv.onVendorReject(catRaw) inv.onVendorRejectRaw(catRaw) -- This shop will refuse every other instance too, so do not offer them. local j = inv.shopJob if j and j.kind == "sell" then local dropped, kept = 0, {} for _, q in ipairs(inv.shopQueue) do if q.kind == "sell" and q.key == j.key then dropped = dropped + 1 else kept[#kept+1] = q end end if dropped > 0 then inv.shopQueue = kept inv.shopSay(string.format("this shop refuses that category — dropped %d more sale(s).", dropped)) end end inv.shopStep(true) end
-- A completed sale is an outcome like any other: record it, then advance. function inv.onSold(itemRaw, silver, fromSack) inv.onSoldRaw(itemRaw, silver, fromSack) inv.shopStep(true) end
-- ---- idrops: what a monster is known to drop --------------------------- function inv.dropsCmd(arg) arg = (arg or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", ""):lower() if arg == "" then local mobs = {} for _, t in pairs(inv.types) do for mob in pairs(t.origins or {}) do mobs[mob] = (mobs[mob] or 0) + 1 end end local list = {} for mob, n in pairs(mobs) do list[#list+1] = { mob = mob, n = n } end if #list == 0 then inv.warn("no drop origins recorded yet."); return end table.sort(list, function(a, b) return a.n > b.n end) cecho("\n<cyan>Monsters seen dropping tracked items<reset>\n") for _, e in ipairs(list) do cecho(string.format(" %-40s %d type(s)\n", e.mob:sub(1, 40), e.n)) end cecho("\n") return end local rows = inv.dropsOf(arg) if #rows == 0 then -- allow a partial name local hit for _, t in pairs(inv.types) do for mob in pairs(t.origins or {}) do if mob:find(arg, 1, true) then hit = mob; break end end if hit then break end end if hit then rows = inv.dropsOf(hit); arg = hit end end if #rows == 0 then inv.warn("nothing recorded from '"..arg.."'."); return end cecho(string.format("\n<cyan>Drops from %s<reset>\n", arg)) for _, r in ipairs(rows) do local t = inv.types[r.key] local flag = (t and t.unidentified) and " <yellow>(unidentified)<reset>" or "" cecho(string.format(" %-44s x%d%s\n", ((t and t.name) or r.key):sub(1, 44), r.n, flag)) if t and t.identifiesAs then for k2 in pairs(t.identifiesAs) do cecho(string.format(" -> <cyan>%s<reset>\n", (inv.types[k2] and inv.types[k2].name) or k2)) end end end cecho("\n") end
-- ---- iclean ghosts ----------------------------------------------------- -- Types that were never seen in any listing, are nowhere in the location map -- and have no measurements: they came from a shop's short form or an altar's -- echo rather than from a real item. function inv.cleanGhosts(arg) local ghosts = {} for k, t in pairs(inv.types) do if not t.seen and not t.weight and not t.volume and not inv.coinInfo(k) then local anywhere = 0 for cont in pairs(inv.loc or {}) do anywhere = anywhere + inv.locCount(cont, k) end if anywhere == 0 then ghosts[#ghosts+1] = k end end end table.sort(ghosts) if #ghosts == 0 then inv.warn("no ghost types found."); return end if arg ~= "confirm" then cecho(string.format("\n<yellow>[inv]<reset> %d type(s) never seen in a listing, held " .."nowhere, never weighed. Most came from a shop's short form:\n", #ghosts)) for i, k in ipairs(ghosts) do if i > 30 then cecho(string.format(" ...and %d more\n", #ghosts - 30)); break end local t = inv.types[k] cecho(string.format(" <grey>%-44s<reset> %s\n", (t.name or k):sub(1, 44), t.sell and string.format("%.0f s", t.sell.avg) or "")) end cecho("Type <cyan>iclean ghosts confirm<reset> to delete them.\n") return end for _, k in ipairs(ghosts) do inv.types[k] = nil end inv.save() cecho(string.format("\n<green>[inv]<reset> removed %d ghost type(s).\n", #ghosts)) end
